Nehemiah BullB003. Nehemiah Bull to JE, 11/4/34. BRBL, "Notes on Imputation and Free Grace," f. 1232. Addressed on back "For the Reverend / Mr Jonathn Edwards / E C D / att / Northampton."

Westfield Nov. 4 1734

Revd Sr While I was at Housatunuck I had considerable talk with Sr Pumroy, & I find him wider in his notions about ye nature of conversion yn I imagind before, wch I cant help but fear may be of much more dangerous consequence yn his opinions about ye docte of predestination -- I intreat you therefore to Send him a letter. prepare it if you can by Tuesday noon next week - wn I hope, Deo votente, to meet Mr Hopkins at yr house Equipt with his arms compleat to study hebrew - for I have sent him a lettr desiring him to meet me at yr house then - it Seems to me yt you need not Spend a great deal of time about ye first lettr besides some preliminaries - for it will take up sundry lettrs I doubt if managd to effect - & if he will not be reclaim'd by such a method it seems to me yt we must do something to prevent his settling quick -for I more fully fall in now with yr opinion yn I did before I went to Sheffield - but I wish yt some method could be taken with him to reclaim him & not set him up to be a country=talk & I can think of none more proper yn this. I was exceedingly pleasd with it wn you first proposd it at N.H. & I can never get it out of my mind since, but yt tis a method that carrys in it an hopefull prospect of success if I had such a talent (as I take you to have) of expressing my ideas to ye best advantage to be receivd by others, & of managing a controversie effectualy, I wod engage in it myself, provided you utterly refuse it. - I wod now inform you about his opinions (as he discoverd 'em to me) concerning ye nature of conversion, but I choose you shod draw 'em from him by a lettr - for if you have em from him under his own hand, he wot have any pretense to make yt he has been misrepresented. - it seems to me yt there is a real call to somebody to stir in a prudent method, & I cant see any body to whom (datis circumstantiis) ye call seems more immediately directed yn to you - as things look now the interest of religion there in futuru, gives this call. no more till you see me, from yr - hearty friend & Humble Servt, N. Bull

## B5. Letter from George Whitefield, November 16, 1739 B005.G.Whitefield-JE 11-16-39

George WhitefieldB005. George Whitefield to JE, 11/16/39. *Works of George Whitefield* (1771), 1:12122.

*Rev. Sir, New York, Nov.* 16, 1739.

MR. N[^267-note1], and the report of your sincere love for our dear LORD JESUS, embolden me to write this. I rejoice for the great things GOD has done for many souls in *Northampton*. I hope, God willing, to come and see them in a few months. The journal sent with this[^267-note2], will shew you what the LORD is about to do in *Europe*. Now is the gathering time. A winnowing time will shortly succeed. Persecution and the power of religion will always keep pace. Our LORD'S word begins to be glorified in *America*. Many hearts gladly receive it. Oh *Rev. Sir*, it grieves me to see people, every where ready to perish for lack of knowledge. I care not what I suffer, so that some may be brought home to CHRIST. I am but a stripling, but the LORD chooses the weak things of this world to confound the strong. I should rejoice to be instructed by you. Mr. N will convey a letter to me-May the GOD of all grace give you all peace and joy in believing! May he increase you more and more, both you and your children! May you every day be feasted, and built up with fresh anointings of his blessed spirit! And by[^267-note3] your fervent prayers, may you be enabled to hold up the hands of, reverend Sir,

Your unworthy brother, fellow labourer and servant in our dear LORD,*G. W.*

[^267-note1]: Not further identified; possibly Thomas Noble of New York.

[^267-note2]: Probably A Continuation of Mr. Whitefield's Journal: from his Arrival at London, to his Departure from Thence on his Way to Georgia (London, 1739).

[^267-note3]: **marginal.** [122]

## B6. Letter from Aaron Burr, March 1741 B006.A.Burr-JE 3-41 edited

Aaron BurrB006. Aaron Burr to JE, 3/41. ANTS, f. 1741, #7. Text lacking at end.

Newark March 1741

Revd & dear Sr

Your’s of Decr 14 Came Safe to hand ye 5th of this instant. I received it with Joy & heartily thank you for it. I desire to bless God that he inclined you to write & especialy to write So freely of your own Experiences. I think it has been much blessed to your my Spiritual Good: tho I have often heard & read of others Experiences, I neer with’m, any thing that the like Effect upon Me - It came in a most Seasonable Time, & was the Means of Clearing up Several Things that I was in ye dark about.

The Week that I received your Letter I was much in ye dark about my own State, And had determin’d by the first Opportunity to open my Case to you by a Letter, that I might have your Advice & Direction, which I Shall now do with ye greater Freedom Since I have heard from you. I think at present, I feel no Disposition to flatter My Self. I long to See & know the worst. The Thoughts of being deceived lie with great Weight on My Mind - I Shall endeavour to Speak of what God has done for [my] Soul without Reserve, according to the best Recollection I can Make of it, and I doubt not you will act the Part of a Spiritual Father & faithful Friend in your Reflections upon it.

From my Childhood I used to be under Distress of mind, great Terrours & horrors from a guilty Conscience and the Fears of Hell, at these Times, as I remember, I used to get

Relief by Promises & Resolutions, Especialy by reading

Bp. Bevearidges Thoughts on Religion.[^268-note1] I used (when my Distress was great) to Set my Self as twere in ye Presence of God & Make over his Resolutions, which would give Me Ease & make Me more Strict in Secret Prayer for a Season, then would all wear off & I became as vain, & Careless as ever. Then I continued under frequent Strivings of God’s Spirit, which I refuted & Stifled, till I Commenced A:B. in ye year 1735 After this I reason’d my Self into a more thorough Reformation; forsook every thing But what ye Devil & my own deceitfull Heart flatered Me was right. Set up the Practice of all outward Duties & Soon began to be well pleased with My Self. By reading Foster, Tillotson, Sharp, &c I had found Such a rational Religion (as I then Called it) as afforded Me no Small Delight Such as ’twas. I thought there were few Such Christians to be found. When I used to hear of Ministers Speaking Against the Arminian Scheme, I used to pity their Ignorance. But O! the Pride that then reign’d in my Heart; it was the Secret Spring of all my Actions, whether I had to do with God or Man. All this Time I never see the Badness of my own Heart, and never Imagin’d but that I was much better than the Most of those among whom I conversed. And I Secretly rejoiced that others were worse than I, for [^268-note2] the Comparison used to Afford Me Peace & Comfort.

This continued not long before it pleased God to open My Eyes & Shew Me Something what I was I See my Self an holy God to be exceeding vile & odious in ye Sight of [-] I had a distressing Apprehension of my Misery & Danger, of that Eternal Wrath to which I lay exposed. I beheld Such a Fountain of Sin & Corruption, as I never imagin’d was in the Heart of any Man - I Soon Changed My Thoughts of being better than others & concluded that there was not Such a another Sinner on the Face of God’s Earth. I was much inclined to despairing Thoughts of God’s Mercy from a Sense of my own vileness; was much afraid I had Sinned away the Day of God’s Patience - I used to think, if I cou’d but be convinced that there ever was So great a Sinner Saved it would afford Me much Relief This Distress was much increased by an Apprehension, that I Should die in a little Time; (for this Winter I did Sensibly decay in my bodily Health) which Made often fear my Concern proceeded more from that than a Sense of Sin. And here I cant but use your own words, they do so exactly express the Sense I then & Since have had of my Case: that the greatness of my Distress was not owing to the greatness of my Convictions, but ye Degree of my Wickedness[^268-note3] I did then & do Still think there never was Such a botomless Depth of Pride & Hypocrisy, Such an amazing Scene of ye most vile & abominable Thoughts indulged in the Heart of any Sinner as there was in mine.

At this Time I had no Just Notion in my Head about the Nature of Conviction, Conversion, & the Way of Salvation by Faith in Christ. There was no Suitable Care taken to instruct in those things in my early Days; I had Scarce ever heard any Conversation about them; learnt Nothing of them at Colledge. I never open’d My Case to any one, for I did not imagine any Body had ever been So before. at this Time as I remember I had Strong Desires after Christ wc I am convinced proceeded from the Fear of Hell. I did not question My Willingness to be Saved by him on any Terms; but Secretly his willingness to Save Me - I thought I could have laid down my Life or forsake 10000 Worlds If [I] had them for an Interest in Him - I dont remember I had any particular Thoughts about my unwillingness to come to Christ - I See that my Heart was fill’d with an Opposition to everything that was good and knew it must be Changed by the Almighty Power of divine Grace or I cou’d never be Saved.

I think I had a Sense of being in the Hands of a Sovereign God. That if he Sent Me to Hell & Saved others, I must pronounce him Just with my last Breath, That it must be by free Sovereign Grace if I ever was Saved - This Concern continued greater or less at Seasons, the most of that Winter I lived Bachelor at Colledge - One Morning in my Study as I was reading that Sermon of Dr. Watt’s on those Words of Job. O! that I knew where I might find him &c[^268-note4] which Made a great & unusual Impression on my Mind in my S.I.[^268-note5] Devotions afterwards I Seem’d to be near to God & have Liberty to pour out My Complaints before Him. My Sins Seemed to come fresh in my Mind in an unusual Maner.

And while I was confessing my original & actual Sins, [^268-note6] I felt an inward Melting & mourning that I never felt before & in my Prayer I had Such a Sense given Me of the Fullness & Sufficiency of the Lord Jesus Christ to Save the Chief of Sinners; I think it came from one of those two passages of Sacred Write viz. He is able to Save to the uttermost &c or That, His Blood Cleanseth from all Sin.[^268-note7] I remember I then used that Argument with Some inward Satisfaction & Delight; Lord thou canst get Glory to thy gr Name in Saving Such a great Sinner as I am. I thought I See how the Justice of God could be glorified in my Salvation. -- upon this I felt Some inward Peace & Ease But I did not think then of being converted, or having Closed with Christ. -- Thou when I came to understand more of the Nature of these Things by reading I used to hope I was then brought home. About this Time I meet with a very considerable Change in my Principals, from an Arminian; became a Calvinist; though I not so any thing so Clear a view of the Calvinistical Doctrine as I have had Since. I used often to be puzzled with many Dificulties about them, tho I Seemed to have an inward Sense of those Truths; & thought they must be So whether I cou’d answer Objections made against them or not - I used to meet with Many Objections against the Sovereignty of God. But I found Something within that acquiesced in it; Saying Who art thou that replyest[^268-note8] &c Tis the Lord let him do as he pleases. I used to live between Hopes & Fears. I often with Something of the Same Nature that I felt that Morning. - I used to feel Some Steady Concern upon My Mind about these Things. Sometimes in great Distress (but never felt such kind of Convictions as I had before tho I often Sought them). What used to be the greatest Support of hope was a Steady Desire, as I imagin’d I had after Christ, & of being like to Him . a willingness to Suffer the Loss of all Things for Him; tho my Practice did not Stand it. The Fall before last Sometime in Novr: in my return from NewEngland The Thoughts about my everlasting Peace & wellfare Came into my Mind with more power than usual, I reflected with Shame upon my living at Such a miserable low Rate as I had done, want of Zeal & Fidelity in my great Work. I began to fear all was wrong. That I [had] been building My Hopes on the Sand. - On my Return to My People, I providentially Meet with Mr. Law’s Treatise on Christian Perfection[^268-note9]; It made Such an Impression on My Mind that I can’t well Express.

What he Said Concerning renouncing the World and SelfDenial; which I Supposed all God’s Children complied with: So far Exceeded what ever I have Experienced that I concluded I knew Nothing yet as I ought to know. [^268-note10] The Foundation of all my hope failed Me. I resign’d up All my former Experiences for meer Delusions. Endeavoured to lay My Self at ye Footstool of Sovereign Grace; waiting for the Consolation of Israel. - The Concern I then felt was increased by what I heard of Mr. Whitefield’s Zeal & Success.

When I reflected on my past Life, I thought I See many Things inconsistent with a State of Grace. -- As my being So much Conform’d to this present World; being govern’d So much by worldly Hopes & Fears and thereby often hindred from dealing So plainly & faithfully with my People as I ought. - Finding So much Pride in My Heart, being often Secretly pleased with the vain Applause of my fellowWorms & greived with their Reproaches & Revilings - Finding So much Selfrighteous & Selfpleasing in my Duty. living So much on my Frames, as it appeared to me I had done, tho I then in the Time of it I thought I hated these Things. My being no more Zealous & faithfull in my great Work. - These Things made Me Conclude I had been deceiving my Self with a false Hope & false Confidence. - That Self had been at the Botom of all. -- In this State of Darkness I continued for Some Time; tho I did not feel any Thing as I did at Colledge had none of those Terrors & fearful Apprehensions of divine Wrath. - I found an engagedness of Spirit after the Things of my Peace. I thought little about being delivered from Hell. But I thought I longed exceedingly to be freed from all Sin, Especialy Pride, Selfrighteousness and a love to this present World. I Seem’d to loathe & hate my Self for that Sin I felt within; and longed to have Christ form’d in my Soul, to find [] holy, heavenly, divine Temper & Disposition - I often thought of what an eminent divine Says - I had rather feel the real Impression of a Godlike Nature on my Soul, than have a Vision from Heaven, or an Angel Sent to tell Me My Name was enroll’d in the Book of Life. - I thought to be free from all Sin, to be like God & Christ, would be Such an Heaven as I wanted. - I long’d for Such a Discovery of Christ to My Soul as would Change & transform Me into ye Same Image. - I devoted My Self to the Service of God, both in Secret & publick in another Manner than ever I had done before & with more pleasure & Delight. But dare not conclude I was in a Safe State. - About this Time one Day in my Secret Devotions: Christ Seemed to appear exceeding precious to my Soul, Methought, I did Commit my Soul to him, to be Saved in his Way. That I cou’d Spend & be Spent for him, part with all, take up my Cross & follow him - This gave Me Some Joy and Comfort, removed my Darkness in Some Measures. I found hereupon Such a Zeal for God’s Glory, Such a Love for Christ & Souls, as I never felt before. […][^268-note11]

[^268-note1]: William Beveridge (16371708), Private thoughts upon religion, digested into twelve articles; with practical resolutions form'd thereupon. By the Right Reverend Father in God, William Beveridge ... Written in his younger years, for the settling of his principles, and conduct of his life (3d ed., 2 vols. London, 170912).

[^268-note2]: **marginal.** [2]

[^268-note3]: Burr is paraphrasing JE’s narrative. A close parallel is: “That my Sins appear to me so great, don't seem to me to be, because I have so much more Conviction of Sin than other Christians, but because I am so much worse, and have so much more Wickedness to be convinced of.” WJE, 16, 802803.

[^268-note4]: Job 23:3.

[^268-note5]: e. “secret.”

[^268-note6]: **marginal.** [3]

[^268-note7]: Heb. 7:25, I John 1:7.

[^268-note8]: Rom. 9:20.

[^268-note9]: William Law (16861761), Practical Treatise upon Christian Perfection.

[^268-note10]: **marginal.** [4]

[^268-note11]: Conclusion of letter missing.

## B7. Letter from Ebenezer Parkman, December 1741 B007.E.Parkman-JE 12-41 edited

Ebenezer ParkmanB007. Ebenezer Parkman to JE, 12/41. MHS, Parkman Commonplace Book, CXVIIIA, 108-9.

To the Rev. Mr. Jonn. Edwards Pastor of ye Chh in North :hampton. Westb. Dec: 1741.

Rev. & Dear Sr.

Whoever you have writ to me by, I have not been So happy as to receive it. But I have recd. yr. valuable Favours (The distinguishing Marks of a Work of ye Spt. of G.) by ye Hand of Mr. Benj. Sheldon, for which I not only thank you, but bless G. Who has enabled you in this eminent manner to hold forth such div. Light to ye Chhs of G. in this important, usef. point. I hope some Singular Blessing will accompany it, to ye grt. Glory of yt. Adorable gracious Influences Spt. whose [--] furnishd & endowd you to compose it, and disposd you to publish it.

May ye Same almighty Grace be Still more plenteously shed forth upon you to qualify you for ye Service of Chts Km,[^269-note1] & may you have a Mouth and Wisdom wc. no one of His Adversarys may be able to Gainsay or resist. I believe it causes ye Thanksgivings of many to G. and O yt ye Evils on both Hands might be avoided, Tepidity and Enthusiasm, and that unwarrantable, rash judging wc. both sides run into! And O yt ye minds of all men, of ministers especially might be opend to behold ye glors. work of G. & ye power & Grace of or. L. J. X more universally experienced everywhere! -- Whilst I mourn over my own Dullness (Ah my Leanness, my Leanness!) I give praise for any Measure of Success to my poor Endeavours among this pp wre. ye Sovgn. G. has cast my Lot. Some observable reviving there is Among our Youth particly. and no less than Six [] Religious Societys (of all Sorts) are sett up among us; But Lads & Young Women I think are foremost. I wish I might be able suitably to preside over ym. and teach ym. ye Good knowledge and right ways of ye Lord; yt. I might with Skill and success, conduct & promote & ripen yeir Convictions, yt. yy may be truely Converted, & yeir Sanctifn. carryd. on: yt Converts may be filld wth. Rss.[^269-note2] & Joy in ye holy Ghost & made meet for the Inheritance of ye Saints in Light: That yy may be guarded agst. all Snares & Delusions, vain presumptions & black Despair; & yt. yy may be able to Stand in the Devil Day against all their Spl. Foes, & finally overcome But who is sufficient for these Things? Surely Chts Grace alone.

Let me have ye Assistance of yr prayers, I entreat you, both for me and all mine -- And may ye Hand of ye L. Still be wth. you and give you still greater successes! My hearty Love to yr. dear Spouse, that helper in ye Lord.

I am yr. unworthy Brother & obliged Servt in wt I am able, E. P.

P.S. I cannot repent of my Refusal to join wth. ye Council at South Hadley; for I was afraid that nothing butI have heard of wondrous Things Evil would ensue; as I Still doubtaccomplishing at Ipswich -- whether any good will come of Mr.but more eminently at Piscataqua: R's[^269-note3] tarrying there. I was notand am told yt. Rev. Mr. Cooper[^269-note4] is at ye late adjournmt. of ye Council;gone there. -- and wish rather it had been dissolvd.

[^269-note1]: Christ's kingdom.

[^269-note2]: Righteousness.

[^269-note3]: Rev. Grindall Rawson, who was dismissed from the pulpit at South Hadley.

[^269-note4]: William Cooper of Boston.

## B8. Letter from Chester Williams, February 15, 1742 B008.C.Williams-JE 2-15-42 edited

Chester WilliamsB008. Chester Williams to JE, Feb. 15, 1742. BRBL, Sermon fragments, f. 1161. Shorn on left side.

Hadley Feb. 15. 1741/2

Revd & Hond Sir

This Line waits on You to Entreat [that] you would Come over & Assist us in Seeking to God by prayer [and fas]ting for ye Outpouring of his holy Spirit upon Us in ys place [--] & for Light & Direction in all Spiritual Matters [We] Need Wisdom & Teaching from above at All Times & particularly now [We] yrfore Beseech & Entreat you to Come over on Wednesday or ye Evening [befo]re, as You please in yt Respect, & Join wth us in offering up our Sincere to God [hear]ty Requests for the Effusion of his Blessed Spirit, & to preach one [pa]rt of ye Day.

I hope You Will Gratify my people as Well as myself [by comin]g over & I believe serve ye Interest of Christ.

With All Due Regards to you & Madam I remain your hble Servt Chesr Williams

Please to Let me Know whether You Can Come by ye Bearer.

## B10. Attestation from Timothy Edwards, May 5, 1742 B010.TE-JE 5-5-42 edited

Timothy EdwardsB010. Timothy Edwards to JE, 5/5/42. Excerpt of a letter or testimony regarding the frequency of “Great Out--cries under Awakenings” in earlier times, printed in *Some Thoughts* (1742), p. 28. See TE, MS “Accounts of Awakenings,” ANTS, for related materials.

“I well remember that one Mr. *Alexander "Allyn*, a Scots Gentleman of good Credit, that dwelt formerly in this Town, shewed me a Letter that came from *Scotland*, that gave an Account of a Sermon preached in the City of *Edinburgh*, (as I remember) in the Time of the sitting of the general Assembly of Divines in that Kingdom, that so affected the People, that there was a great and loud Cry made throughout the Assembly. I have also been credibly informed, & how often I cannot now say, that it was a common Thing, when the famous Mr. *John Rogers* of *Dedham* in *England* was preaching, for some of his Hearers to cry out; and by what I have heard, I conclude that it was usual for many that heard that very awakening and rousing Preacher o GOD’s Word, to make a great Cry in the Congregation.”

*Windsor*, May 5. 1742. TIMOTHY EDWARDS

## B11. Letter from William Russel, May 6, 1742 B011.W.Russel-JE 5-6-42 edited

William RusselB011. William Russel to JE, 5/6/42. ANTS, Sermon on Matt. 7:15 (Jan. 1743). Addressed on back "To The / Rd: Mr: Jonathan Edwards / Att / Northampton / These / Pr Mr Allen."

Dear Brothr: This may Inform yt I got Comfortably home that day I Left you about 5 of ye Clock found my family well. I purpose to go to Wethersfield next week according to yr advice and hope to meet Mr Williams of Lebanon[^273-note1] there & I believe there will be diverse other minsiters there of this Neighbourhood who are Concerned for the promoting of vital religion and Maintaining of good order: I Should be glad to know whether there was any more Comffortable appearance at New Haven before you Came away. & desire you would Send me the particulars you have drawn up Respecting Exhorters. yr Meeting will be over before the barer Returns if it would not be too much trouble I desire you would Inform me wt is done it may be of service to us our Next meeting of this Association being the first of June. I prest my Love to yrself & Sister & yr Children. & desire a Constant Remembrance in yr & her prayers

Yr Loving Brother W. Russel

May. 6. 1742

[^273-note1]: Solomon Williams.

## B12. Letter from Daniel Bliss, August 26, 1742 B012.D.Bliss-JE 8-26-42 edited

Daniel BlissB012. Daniel Bliss to JE, 8/26/42. BRBL, Sermon on Luke 15:15--16 (Nov. 1742), f. 576.

Reverend Sir These are humbly to inform You that it is the Earnest desire of many -- Especially my own that You would take this Town in Yr Return home -- The way is not much further than that You Usually ride -- by coming You will undoubtedly be an instrument in promoting the Kingdom of Christ & the Salvation of immortal Souls -- There are reasons peculiar for my So Judging. -- Requesting an interest in Yr Prayers -- I continue Yr unworthy Servt

Dan. Bliss. Concord, 8th 26. 1742. For the Revd Mr Jona Edwards

## B14. Letter from John Stoddard, October 18 1742 B014.J.Stoddard-JE 10-18-42 edited

John StoddardB014. John Stoddard to JE, 10/18/42. BRBL, Sermon on Luke 22:27 (Nov. 1742), f. 601. Cut in two parts. This is in reference to a "Paper" that Stoddard had written "Concerning the Present Work of God in the Land" (no longer extant) communicated by JE to the Hampshire Association meeting of April 13, 1742, which voted to "Desire him to give a Copy of it for the Press."

Nth Hampton Octbr 18 - 1742 I have not time to write any thing new, I have some apprehensions of Inconvenience in making Publick what I have written, but having been much urged thereto, I leave it to you to make what use of it you think proper.

I am yours J. Stoddard

To the Revnd Mr Jonathan Edwards.

## B15. Letter from Samuel Mather, [Before December 1742] B015.S.Mather-JE before12-42 edited

Samuel MatherB015. Samuel Mather to JE, n.d. [before 12/42]. BRBL, Sermon on Luke 12:35-36 (Dec. 1742), f. 567.

Revd Sr

Let Mrs Edwards take one of these potions of the Jovial Bezoardick every morning and Evening (‘till they are Spent) in a Spoonfull or two of balm water or the decoction of mugwort --

Let this Epithem be Applyed to her forehead (viz) take a Cloath and wet it with this in the bottle & bind it on to Her forehead and temples -

If any of this in the bottl be left let it be mixed with water as I directed in the morning and let her drink of it often 3 or 4 Spoonfulls at a time.

I think that Mynsichtu’s Emplastrum Matricale would be of great Service to Her, If applyed to her Navel and worn there for Some weeks or months together. It’s an Admirable remedie, in all diseases retaining to an Hystericall originall and I have Seen Sirprising Affects from this Application in Histerick Cases. I think it would be worth your while to Send to Boston for it -- I have none of it at present.

In Hast from Yr Humble Servt S: Mather

## B16. Letter from Southampton Church, [Before December 1742] B016.S'tonChh-JE before12-42 edited

Southampton (Mass.) ChurchB016. Southampton Church to JE, n.d. (before 12/42), fragment. BRBL, Sermon on Luke 12:35-36 (Dec. 1742), f. 567. In hand of Jonathan Judd.

Revd Sir Our Circumstances are in some measure know[n] to your self and seeing our people have & are are are much influenced by the advice you have given to us . we would humbly beseech mr Edwards if it were possible to Come & see us . that we might be directed we having understood by mr Judd yt designs (God willing) to be at N:Hapton some time next & will if mr Edwards is willing Come here & be wt us on ye Sabath. thought of it to send a few Lines that mr Edwards might think of it - we Cant but think mr Edwardss advice if here would be of great advantage especialy at this time -- Revd sir we bege yo you would think of & if Convenietly visit us. However we bege your prayers for us that we might be directed. so we remain your humble […]

## B17. Letter from Jonathan Judd, December 15, 1742 B017.J. Judd-JE 12-15-42 edited

Jonathan JuddB017. Jonathan Judd to JE, 12/15/42. BRBL, Sermon on Is. 57:21 (Dec. 1742).

Suffeild December 15 1742 Revd and Dear Sir I would Let you know that ye people of New Hampton have sent a man to me to go to preach with them in order to settle with them if I go from Suffeild which I have at present determaned to do being 10: or 12 men against me and the Circumstances of ye place [-] appearing to me to be remarkable difficult if I should tarry with them so that I think it my duty to go away exceept a remarkable alteration beyound what apparse likly at present tho God can Change yr hearts as he pleases having ym all in his hands - Dear Sir you may Remember what discourse I had with an man at Mr Edwards' house about going to preach with the people where he belonged and that if they Could not get one and I was at Liberty I was willing to go there -- now if they have none and Mr Edwards thinks it my Duty to go there I should be Glad Mr Edwards would Let me know or if they are sup supplied or otherwise I Desire Mr Edwards ad advice about going to N: Hampto [. . .]

if Mr Edwards would take trouble of sending to me his advic about going to N: Hampton I believe the barer of this Letter will convey it to me for he or some others are to come to me next week if Mr Edwards adviseth them to me and me to the them - &c sir I am thro divine Goodness in usial[?] hea[l]th as I hope this will find you and family. I do herin send not my respect not only to you but also to madam and Mrs Sarah so I desire to your prayers for me and to subscribe myself

your Humble petitioner & welwisher Jonathan Judd

## B18. Letter from David Parsons, Jr., [Before January 1743] B018.D.Parsons-JE bef edited

David Parsons, Jr.B018. David Parsons to JE, n.d. frag. [before Jan. 1743]. ANTS, Sermon on Matt. 7:15 (Jan. 1743). MS damage throughout, as indicated by words or parts of words in brackets.

[. . .] advance a work [. . .]

I rather fear the design of Some (if Possible) to Confound Gods Work; or at least Means that God has & does remarkably Bless for the Carrying on his own Work*

*What Should be the Reason the opposing Gentlemen stand to readily Come into the Scheme unless yy thought yy shd have a lucky oppertunity in yr hands to Knok Religion in [ye] Head

I woud hope be[tter th]ings of Some who at times appear to Encourage the present [seaso]n, but yr Conduct is very preposterous who pull down wt on[e han]d wt yy build up wt ye other; -- I Believe these are wrought upon [by oth]ers. -- Tis Easy to see thrÔ the Craft of Some Gentlemen w[ho sin]ce the[y] dare not Appear open & Barefacd do Indirectly fight ag[ainst] Religion by the Instrumentality of others Not Much unlike the [mo]nkey that Scratchd the Embers wt ye Catspaw: --

I informd this [Chh of] the Ministers proposal Choose not to Give E’m any though[ts upon] the Matter, but desird Em to Act yr own Judgment. They univ[ersally] agreed to take no regard to it

Religion Great [flou]rishes among us; the Holy Spirit seems to be powred down in a Gre[ater] Measure than Ever it has been here heretofore in this place. -- there [. . .]ar a Score that are from Day to Day wonderfully filld wt Divin[e Co]mforts; & the Number Encreases -- many sinncers are laid under deep Convictions of their sin & Danger & are put upon Greater [ende]avours yn yy Ever have been to secure yr Salvation; -- & sever[al a]mong us have been of late hopefully Converted Revd Sr Pray for us, that Go[d’s wor]k might be Carryd on wt Greater Power & success & that a weak unwort[hy Ins]trument may be Enabld to apply properly to the various Circums[tances] of souls under his Care -- may Experience the Joys in his own soul [an]d at last obtain ye Character of a faithfull servant

Please to Give my regards [. . .] & accept ye same your self from Revd Sr your Respectful friend [&] obliged servant David Parsons Jun

North Hampton March

Dear Sir yesterday I received these letters and two of your books one of which I have Sent to Mr Potwine Considering our great obligations and the need they at that town have . it was best to Send as sone as it Came to me.

## B20. Letter from Isaac Lyman, April 12, 1743 B020.I.Lyman-JE 4-12-43 edited

Isaac LymanB020. Isaac Lyman to JE, Apr. 12, 1743. BRBL, sermon fragments, f. 1175.

[York, Maine?]

Reverend Sr After my Duty to you, & my humble request to you for your prayers for me. I would Inform you yt it hath Pleased ye Church in this place, to requre those who design to take up there abode in this place for any Considerable to get certificates of there standing in ye churches from whence they Come. yrfore my humble request to you is for one, and in so Doing you will very much oblige your humble servant, Isaac LymanApril ye 12, 1743.

## B20. Letter from Ebenezer Gay, April 12, 1743 B020.I.Lyman-JE 4-12-43 edited

Ebenezer GayB021. Ebenezer Gay to JE, 4/19/43. BRBL, Sermon on Eccles. 2:17 (May 1743), f. 240. Beginning of letter missing.

[…] broken circumstances here at Suffield,[^283-note1] yt it is needless to relate them to You, or to tell you how much we want Correction & Advice from others -- The Revd. Association (at Springfield) upon a Question proposed to you, by ye Chh here Respecting the Members of Chts Chh, in ye West Society, whether they were a Part of my Charge, & had a Right to act, in Matters of Discipline, in yt particular Chh, To wm I stand in a Pastoral -- instead of giving a direct Answer, advised us to keep a Day of Fasting & Prayer to God, to humble &c- and to invite ye. Neighbouring ministers to assist in ye Fast, & to advise what Measures we should take to heal our unhappy Divisions. This is to desire your Presence & Assistance in this Affair, on Wednesday ye 27th of this Instant.

I am your humble Servant, Ebenezer Gay Suffield. April 19. 1743.

[^283-note1]: A Separatist congregation in Suffield had established themselves under Rev. Joseph Hastings.

## B23. Letter from Samuel Hopkins, May 5, 1743 B023.S.Hopkins-JE 5-5-43 edited

Samuel HopkinsB023. Samuel Hopkins to JE, 5/5/43. BRBL, Sermon on Eph. 4:15-16 (May 1743), f. 774. Addressed on back, top cut off: "Pastor of the Church / in Northampton."

Rev’d Sir, I would by these inform you that I am not yet fully determin’d to leave Symsbury, according to my Proposal when at Northampton last; but after much Consideration of the Matter and an Endeavour, so far as I am able, to look on Things relating to it [-] without Partiality, or any Respect to Self, (which I find beyond my Power to do) togeather with a Looking to God by Prayer for Direction in this Affair; I notwithstanding hesitate & know not what is my Duty. This I write, that Mr. Edwards may not leave his People with any Dependence on me to preach to them in his absence unless I Should come the week before, or Send word. -- If I do not leave this People, I Shall, if Providence permit, come to Northampton by the Time that Mr. Edwards returns from Boston. I desire a Remembrance in your Prayers. And after presenting my Duty to yourself, & Madam, with proper Respects to your family I subscribe myself your oblidged, humble servant Samll. Hopkins___ Symsbury May 5th. 1743.

## B25. Letter from Stephen Williams, June 18, 1743 B025.S.Williams-JE 6-18-43 edited

Stephen WilliamsB025. Stephen Williams to JE[?], 6/18/43. BRBL, Sermon on Prov. 17:16 (June 1743), f. 223. No address on back.

L. M. june 18. 1743

Revd. And Dear Sr --

I wrote a line to you a day, or two ago. - But fearing yt will miscary - I now inform you, that tis Expectd - at Boston, yt we Send down, or. testimony, to ye late happy re vivall of religion &c- to ye ministers yt shall meet ye day after comencmt &c I should be glad to know, from you whether, we shall Endeavour to do it a number of us together &c-- or separately &c.[^287-note1] Mr. Raynolds & I design to meet at Mr. Allis next Tuesday, to pray & confer together - if your circumstances, would allow you, to come to my house on monday night and ride thither - I should be glad &c I request, I may hear from you (if I dont see you) next week &c- I wish Salvation to you & your family. I believe we are calld of God, to Give our testimony at this day &c- I am dear sir

Your brr & very humble Servt. Stephn. Williams

[^287-note1]: See letter no. 42, the letter sent to the Assembly of Pastors, 6/30/43.

## B26. Letter from William Rand, [c. July 1743] B026.Wm Rand to JE (c. 7-43) edited

William RandB026. William Rand to JE, n.d. [before 7/43]. BRBL, Sermon on I John 2:25 (July 1743), f. 867.

Revd Sir, It is a time of Affliction and trouble in this place: God is sending sickness among us, it is a time of great drought, and God is sending Armies of insects to devour the fruits of the Earth. Religion seems to be in a declining State, the contensions, devisions & Errours which have been among us do but little abate.

I have therefore concluded to turn my Lecture next week into a fast, to humble our selves before God under the frowns and rebukes of his providence and to implore (his) favour; And above all to seek of him that Religion in the power and purity of it may prevail among us, that our divisions may be healed; that all Errours and disorders, and what ever might have a tendency to hinder the work of God among us, may cease.

These are therefore to beg the favour of you, yt you would come and assist me at the fast, which as it would be very acceptable to me, and might be very serviceable to this people in order to heal our divisions &c if you would Testifie against the Errours and irregularities yt prevail, as you have often done.

I hope sir you will not fail.

Willm Rand

## B29. Letter from David Parson, Jr., August 6, 1743 B029.D.Parsons-JE 8-6-43 edited

David Parsons, Jr.B029. David Parsons, Jr., to JE, 8/6/43. BRBL, Sermon on Num. 23:9 (Aug. 1743).

Hadley Augst 6: 1743

[Re]vd & Hond sr: at my house you remember the Time of our appointment happens the next Tuesday; fearing therefore you'l be Disappointed by Reason of my Illness of that Conveniency that might be Expected, tho't proper to let you Know seasonably that you might let others concernd Know of it; & make alter your place if you see fitt. -- I have Kept house for more than a week & for several days past have mainly Kept my Bed. -- Dr Mather the Bearer Gives me no Encouragement of being abroad hastily. -- I cant but look upon a great frown of Providence to be deprived of ye opportunity of meeting with you; which I have so much depended upon. - may God meet you when assembled & answer the prayers of his servants - Revd sr pray for me that God wd send light in Darkness & that I may not after I have in some faint measure Endeavoured the salvation of other loose my own from your obliged friend & servant David Parsons Jun. if Notwithstanding my sickness you should think proper to meet here by reason of the retiredness of the place & the difficulty of Giving notice seasonably will order affairs as comfortably for you as we can -- My House is now inhabited by my servts only

D P

## B30. Letter from John McLaurin (Extract), August 10, 1743 B030.J.McLaruin-JE 8=10-43

John McLaurinB030. John McLaurin to JE, 8/10/43 (extract). *Christian History* 1 (Dec. 31, 1743-Jan. 7, 1743), 352-53.

*Extract of a Letter from the Rev. Mr.* MCLAURIN *of* Glasgow *to the Rev. Mr.* EDWARDS *of* Northampton, *dated* Aug. 10. 1743.

" -- As to the State of Things with us, I must chiefly refer you to those Parts of Mr. *Robe's* Narrative, I now transmit. Besides the Places mentioned in those Prints there are comfortable Accounts, tho' comparatively speaking perhaps not so considerable, nor so notour concerning some Parts of the Counties of *Ross* and *Murray* far North, and some Parts toward the South, about the Borders of *England*, and other Parts near the Heart of the Land."

(*To be continued.*)

[Jan. 7, 1744 issue:]*Remainder of the* Extract*from Mr.* McLaurin's *Letter to Mr.* Edwards.

"I Have had more Confort than I can easily express, in conversing this Summer with some *young Men* from the*Eastern* Parts, who since the late Revival have turn'd their Thoughts towards the Ministry; and give good Ground to hope that it is from an uncommon Zeal for the Glory of GOD in the Conversion of Souls. Some of them had begun other Kinds of Business, but they are of such an Age at present, that, if they are spar'd, they will be Young, I think, when they have finish'd their University Education."

## B31. B031.S.Hopkins-JE 8-11-43 edited

Samuel HopkinsB031. Samuel Hopkins to JE[?], 8/11/43. Top portion in ANTS, Sermon on Is. 65:17-18, n.d. [c. early 1744]; bottom portion in BRBL, Sermon on Ps. 45:9 (Dec. 1743), f. 143.

Revd Sir,

I have receiv'd yours by which I am inform'd of the Desire of ye People of Col-rain that I would come, & preach among them. -- but I, in no wise, think it my Duty to comply with their Desire. I think I have a clear Call to Stay among this People at present. there is a Considerable Number of them; and all united in Me as yet, and that beyond all Expectation. Several things have remarkably happened, which Seem to be ye Means of their Union. I know not how long it will last: but desire to wait on Providence hoping that I Shall be led in the Way of My Duty. -- People are willing to hear the Word. but there is No Sensible Revival of[^293-note1] Religion. Mr Lewis[^293-note2] is here and and tells me yt he has lately been onto Part of the Oblong, & to a Place joyning to that calld ye Nine-Partners, where he finds an Seriousness among ye People & a great Desire to hear the Word Preached, and I have determined (if Providence permit) to go there with him next week. It is Nigh 30 Miles from this Place. I desire your Prayers that I may have Direction & Success. I am, Sir, your much obliged & humble Servant Samll Hopkins HousatunokAugust 11th 1743.

[^293-note1]: ANTS portion ends, BRBL portion begins.

[^293-note2]: Probably Rev. Daniel Lewis of Pembroke.

## B32. Letter from William McCulloch (Extract), August 13, 1743 B032.W.McCulloch-JE 8-13-43 edited

William McCullochB032. William McCulloch to JE, Aug. 13, 1743, extract. *Christian History*, I, no. 46 (Boston, Jan. 14, 1743/44), 361-63.

*Extract of a Letter from the Rev. Mr.* McCulloch *to the Rev. Mr.*Edwards*of* Northampton. Cambuslang, Aug. 13. 1743.

*Rev. and dear Sir,*

"THE *happy Period* in which we live, and the Times of Refreshing from the Presence of the Lord, wherewith you first were visited in *Northampton* in the Year 1736; and then more generally in *New-England*, in 1740, and 1741; and then we in several Places in *Scotland*, in 1742, and 1743; and the strong Opposition made to this Work with you and with us, check'd by an infinitely superior Power; often brings to my Mind that Prophecy, Isai. lix. 19. *So shall they fear the Name of the LORD from the West, and his Glory from the rising of the Sun: When the Enemy shall come in as a Flood, the Spirit of[^294-note1] the LORD shall lift up a Standard against him.* I [362] cannot help thinking that *this Prophecy* eminently points at *our Times*; and begins to be fulfilled in the Multitudes of Souls that are bringing in to fear the LORD, to worship GOD in CHRIST, in whom his Name is, and to see his Glory in his Sanctuary. And it is to me pretty remarkable, that the Prophet here fortells they should do so in the Period he points at, *not* from *East* to *West* but from*West* to *East*; mentioning the *West* before the *East*, contrary to the usual Way of speaking in other Prophecies, as where *Malachi* fortells, that *the Name of the*LORD*should be great among the Gentiles, from the Rising of the Sun to the West*, (Mal. I. 11.) And our LORD JESUS, that *many should come from East to West*, &c. (Math. 8. 11.) And in this Order it was that the Light of the Gospel came to dawn on the several Nations in the Pro- pagation of it thro' the World. But the Prophet here, under the Conduct of the HOLY SPIRIT who chooses all his Words in infinite Wisdom, puts the *West* before the *East*; intending, as I conceive, thereby to signify, that the glorious Revival of Religion, and the wide and diffusive Spread of vital Christianity, in the latter Times of the Gospel, should begin in the more *westerly* Parts, and proceed to these more *easterly*. And while it should be doing so, or shortly after, *great Opposition* should arise, *the Enemy should come in as a Flood*:*Satan* should with great Violence assault particular believing Souls; and stir up Men to malign and repraoch the Work of GOD; and, it's like also, raise a terrible Persecution against the Church. But while the Enemy might seem, for a Time, to be thus carrying all before him, *the Spirit of the*LORD*should lift up a Standard against him*; give a Banner to them that fear Him and animate them to display it for the Truth, and make his Word mightily to prevail and bear down all opposing power. For on what Side soever, the Almighty and Eternal SPIRIT of JEHOVAH, lifts up a Standard, there the Victory is certain; and we may be sure he will lift it up in Defence of his own Work. The *Caldee Paraphrast* makes the Words in the latter Part of this Verse, to allude to the *River* Euphrates, *when it breaks over all its Banks, and overflows the adjacent Plains,* thus, *when Persecutors shall come in, as the Inundation of the River* Euphrates, *they shall be broke in Pieces by the Word of the*LORD.

The whole of this Verse seems to me to have an Aspect to [363] the *present* and *past Times* for *some Years*. The *Sun of Righteousness* has been making his Course from *West* to *East* and shedding his benign and quickening Influences on poor forlorn and benighted Souls in Places vastly distant from one another. But Clouds have arisen and intercepted his reviving Beams. The Enemy of Salvation has broke in as an overflowing Flood, almost overwhelmed poor Souls newly come into the spiritual World, after they had got some Glimpse of the Glory of CHRIST, with a Deluge of Temptations: Floods of ungodly Men stirred up by *Satan* and their natural Enmity at Religion, have affrighted them: mistaken and prejudged Friends have disown'd them. Many such Things have already befallen the Subjects of this glorious Work of GOD of Late Years: But I apprehend *more general and formidable Trials*are*yet to come:* and that the Enemy's coming in as a Flood, may relate to a Flood of *Errors* or *Persecutions* of fierce Enemies rushing in upon the Church, and threatning to swallow her up. But our Comfort is, that the SPIRIT*of the*LORD*of Hosts will lift up a Standard* against all the combin'd Powers of Earth and Hell and put them all to flight: And CHRIST having begun to conquer so remakably, will go on from conquering to conquer, 'till the whole Earth be filled with his Glory. *Rev*. 12. 15. *Isai*. 17. 12, 13.

I mention these Things, dear Sir, not for your Information, for I know that I can add nothing to you; but to *shew my Agreement with you, in what you express as your Sentiments, that what has now been a doing, is the Fore-runner of something vastly greater, more pure and more extensive, and that*GOD*will revive his Work again, e're long, and that it will not wholly cease, 'till it has subdued the whole Earth:*and, without pretending to prophecy, to hint a little at the Ground of my Expectations. Only I'm afraid (which is a Thing you do not hint at) that *before* these glorious Times, *some dreadful Stroke* or *Trial* may be yet abiding us. May the LORD prepare us for it. But as to this, I cannot and *dare not peremptorily determine*. All these Things *I give up to further Light*, without pretending to fix the Times and Seasons for GOD'S great and wonderful Works, which he has reserv'd in his own Power, and the certain Knowledge of which he has lock'd up in his own Breast.

[^294-note1]: Original: "if."

## B33. Letter from James Robe (Extract), August 16, 1743 B033.J.Robe-JE 8-16-43 edited

James RobeB033. James Robe to JE, 8/16/43 (extract). *Christian History* 1 (Jan. 7, 1743).

*Extract of a Letter from the Rev Mr.*ROBE *of* Kilsyth,

*to the Rev. Mr.* EDWARDS *of* Northampton.*Kilsyth,* August 16. 1743.*Rev. Sir, and very dear Brother*,

"WE acknowledge with Praise and Thanks, the LORD'S keeping his Work hitherto *with us* free from those Errors and Disorders, which through the Subtilty of the Serpent, and the Corruptions even of good Men, were mixed with it in NEW-ENGLAND. As this was no more just Ground of Objection against what was among *you* being a real Work of the HOLY SPIRIT, than the same Things were against the Work of GOD in *Corinth* and *other Places* at the *first Conversion of the Pagans*, and afterwards at the *Reformation from Popery*; so the many Adversaries to this blessed Work here, have made use of all those Errors, Disorders and Blemishes against it *there*, as Objections, as if they had really been *here*. The most unfavourable Accounts from *America*, the most scurrilous and bitter Pamphlets, and Representations from mistaking Brethren, were much & zealously propagated. Only it was over-ruled by Providence, that the most of those Letters and Papers dropped what was a real Testimony to the Goodness of the Work, they designed to defame and render odious. Many thinking Persons concluded from the gross Calumnies forged and spread against the LORD'S Work *here* within a few Miles of them, that such Stories from *America* could not be much depended upon.

What you write about the *Trial* of *extraordinary* Joys *and* [359] *Raptures*, by their *Concomitants* and *Effects*, is most solid; and our Practice by all I know, hath been conform to it. It hath been in the strongest Manner declared, that no Degree of such rapturous Joys evidenced them to be from GOD, unless they led to GOD, and carried with them those Things which accompany Salvation. Such *conditional Applications* of the *Promises* of Grace and Glory as you justly recommend, hath been all along our Manner. A *holy Fear of Caution* and *Watchfulness* hath been much pressed upon the Subjects of this Work who appeared to believe through Grace. And what is greatly comfortable, and Reason of great Praise to our GOD is, that there is as yet known to me in these Bounds no certain Instance of what can be called Apostacy; and not above four Instances of any who have fallen into any gross Sin.

As to the State and Progress of this blessed Work *here* and in *other Places*, it is as followeth. Since the Account given in the several Prints of my *Narrative*, which I understand is or will be at *Boston*; the awakening of secure Sinners hath and doth continue in this Congregation; but not in such Multitudes as last Year; neither can it be reasonably expected. What is Ground of Joy and Praise is, that there scarce hath been *two* or *three Weeks* but wherein I have *some Instance* of Persons *newly awakened*, besides several come to my Knowledge who have been awakened and appear in a most hopeful State, before they were known to me. Of which I had an Instance *Yesterday* of a *Girl* awakened as she saith in *October last*. I have at writing this, an Instance of a *Woman* who appears to have attained a good Issue of her awakening last Year; tho' I supposed it had come to nothing, through her intermitting to come to me of a long Time. There is this Difference in *this Parish* betwixt the Awakening *last Year* and *now*; that none of their *Bodies* have been affected by their Fears in a convulsive or hysteric Way; and yet the *inward Distress* of some of them hath been very sharp. I have seen *two* or *three* who have *fainted* under Apprehension of the Hiding of GOD's Face, or their having received the Lord's Supper unworthily. In some of the *neighbouring Congregations* where this blessed Work was *last Year*, there are Instances of *discernable Awakenings this Summer*. In the large Parish of St. NINIANS to the *North* of this, I was witness to the *awakening of some* and conversed with others *awakened, middle* of *July last*. in the Parish of SINTRIE to the *West* of St.[360] NINIANS there were several *newly awakened* at the giving the Lord's Supper, *End* of *July*. In GARGUNNOCK, KIPPEN, KILLERN farther *North* and *West*, the LORD'S Work is yet discernable. At MUTHED which is about *twenty miles north* from this; the Minister wrote me about the *Middle* of *July*, that this blessed Work which hath appeared *there since last Summer* as at *Cambuslang*, yet *continueth*; and hath spread into *other Parishes* and reacheth even to the *Highlands* bordering upon that Parish.

I am not without Hopes of having good Accounts of the *Out-pouring* of the HOLY SPIRIT in the *Shires* of ROSSE and NAIRN among the *northermost* Parts of SCOTLAND. There was more than ordinary Seriousness in some Parishes in hearing the Word, and in a Concern about their Souls, in *the Spring*, when I saw some godly *Ministers* from *those Bounds*. This more than ordinary Seriousness in hearing, and about Communion Times, is observable in several Parts in SCOTLAND *this Summer*. *Societies for Prayer setting up* where there were none, and in other Places *increasing*. A Concern among the *Young* are in some of the least hopeful Places in SCOTLAND, particularly in the MEUSE near the *English Borders*. There is a great Likelihood of the LORD'S doing Good by the Gospel in this discernable Way in those Bounds. Mr. *McLaurin*, my dear Brother, gives you an Account of the Progress of this Work to the *West* of GLASGOW and *other Places*. There have been very *extraordinary Manifestations* of the Love of GOD in CHRIST JESUS unto his People in the Use of the *holy Supper*, and in the Dispensation of the *Word* about that Time, *this Summer*. Which hath made the LORD'S People desire it a *second Time* in these Congregations during the Summer Season. It was given here upon the *first Sabbath* of *June*, and is to be given here *next Lord's Day* a *second Time*, upon such a Desire.

*Your affectionate Brother and Servant in our dearest LORD*, JAMES ROBE.

Revrand sir these are to inform you that Last time I was at North Hempton I was inquring at madam Edwards if you wod spear a cow in the spring and at that time she Could give me no answer and sir I wod pray you to be pleased to writ me a lin and send it by the bearer and let me know if you intend to spear one or no - allso we intended to a sent Searah befor now but my hors is seek so as I Can do nothing with him so now I wod have you to be a good tell Esther to be a good Girl and stay Contented till such tims as I Can have an oppertuinety to send Sarah and Revrand sir I hope youll be advising of her to her duety for one of her age wants to be minded my kind Love and service to you and madam which is from you[r] frind and most humbel servant Pelham Febr. ye 28th 1743/4 [. . .]

Revd & Dear Brothr

This may Inform that I am thro' Divine goodness in Usual health & the most of my family Esther hath been poorly all Winter yet hath for the most part kept about She hath been at New Haven this fortnight I hope it may be for her health. Mehitabel also is poorly Looks pale but keeps about. I conclude you have heard of the death of my aged and hond mother wch. was in a short time after you were here: I desire yr. prayers that it may be sanctified me. and that all my Afflictions & troubles here may forward my preparation for the rest that remains for the people of God. My Children prst. their duty to you & their Aunt and their Love to their Cousins. I also prest. my Love to yr. Self & sister & yr. Children.

And Am Yr. Loving Brothr W Russel Midd: May. 2d. 1744: P S . I shall be glad to hear from you as oft as opportunity prests.

## B45. Letter from Thomas Clap, April 1, 1745 B045.T.Clap-JE 4-1-45 edited

Thomas ClapB045. Thomas Clap to JE, 4/1/45. Printed as *A Letter from the Rev. Mr.Clap . . . to the Rev. Mr. Edwards* (Boston, 1745).

A LETTER, *&c.*

*Reverend Sir*,

SOME Months ago, when I heard a Report of a *Contradiction*between us, I wrote some Letters to you in a *pacific Manner*, representing the ill Consequences of it to *Religion,* and endeavouring to come to a right*Understanding*. In your Answers, it appeared to me, that you plainly *conceded* to the *Substance* of what I had said, and yet seem'd *unaccountably* to insist upon a *Contradiction*; tho' I could see but little or none, but only between the several Parts of your Letters. And you sent a Letter to *Boston* to be printed, containing sundry Reflections upon me, which necessitated me to write a Letter to a Friend, giving him a short Account of the Case, and which was tho't necessary to be printed in *my Vindication*. This Letter charg'd you with no *Crime*, entred into no Controversy with you, but rather *compromised*Matters, and represented that there was no Contradiction between us so *great*, as to be worthy of any publick Controversy, Clamour, or Dispute.

This *pacific* Representation has *exasperated* you so much the more; and has occasioned you to write in a *bitter Manner*, declaring, that there was a *great Contradiction*between us, and that it was your*indispensible Duty publickly to contradict me.*

The State of the Case is thus: I suppose Mr. W- had a Scheme or Design to turn out the generality of Ministers in the Country, by perswading People to discard or separate from them as being unconverted, and to get a Supply of converted ones, many of which were to be Foreigners.

After discoursing upon this with you, I reported, that you said these [^307-note1] Words, "Mr. *Whitefield*told me, that he designed to turn the generality of Ministers in the Country out of their Places, and bring over Ministers from *England*, *Scotland*, and *Ireland*, and place them in their Room."

Upon which, you in your Letters to me say these Words.

"Tho' I remember no Conversation about Mr. *W*-- at that Time, "yet I have on some Occasions mentioned it as my Opinion, that Mr. *W*-- was formerly in the Opinion and Scheme of People's forsaking unconverted Ministers, which possibly you might hear of from others.-- I heard Mr. *W*-- say, that he had Thoughts of bringing over a Number of young Men from *England*, to be ordained by the *Tennant*'s. I have sometimes said to others, as I inform'd you in my late Letter to you, that I suppose that Mr. *W*-- was formerly of the Opinion, that unconverted Ministers ought not to continue in the Ministry; and I do suppose that he endeavoured to propagate this Opinion, and a Practice agreeable to it. It is true also, that I talked with Mr. *W*- about judging other Persons to be unconverted. Tho', as I said, I remember no Conversation about Mr. *W*-- at that Time; yet it is possible I might also say to you, that I believed Mr. *W*-- did aim at People's forsaking unconverted Ministers, and to endeavour that there should be a Supply of converted ones as far as in him lay; or something to that Purpose. In the same Discourse it is possible I might mention what Mr. *W*-- told me of his Design of bringing over some young Men from *England*, to be ordain'd by the *Tennant*'s in the *Jerseys.*"

These Words I quoted in my printed Letter, and said, *that tho' you had not used exactly the same Terms (in expressing*Mr. W--'s *Scheme) as I had done; yet you had used a variety of those which were equally full and strong. And if we still differ, it is only about some particular Terms,*and*inconsiderable Circumstantials*, *which are not worthy of any Controversy*or*Dispute*.---And I am of the same Mind still.

Now this *agreeing* Representation has very much *exasperated* you; and in your printed Letter you say, "that it appears you have owned no part of my Report, but most solemnly denied every Article of it." And proceed to make a most solemn Declaration or Oath in these Words, "I have no Remembrance that ever Mr. *W*-- said any Thing to me-- of any Design of his turning out any Ministers, or ever so much as hinted of any Thing of that Nature, or of his bringing over any Candidates from *Scotland*or *Ireland,*into any Part of *America*, or [^307-note2] from any other Country in *Europe*into *New-England*, or that ever I reported any such Thing to Mr. *Clap,* or any other Person, or that ever any thought of Mr. *W*-d's saying or hinting any Thing *like* either of these Things ever entred into my Heart, 'till I heard them as coming from Mr. *Clap*."-- ‘--There is a great Contradiction between us.’-- ‘--And it is my indispensable Duty publickly to contradict him.’

This is the State of the Case, and the principal Question upon it is, *Whether this* great Contradiction *lies most between*you *and*me, or *between* you *and* yourself.?

Now in order to determine this Question, I shall particularly go over my Words and yours, and compare them together.

I express'd Mr. *W*-*d*’s SCHEME in these Words, [*that he design'd to turn out the Ministers*,-- &c*.*] You express it in these Words ["Mr. *W*- *was in the Opinion and*SCHEME of People's *forsaking unconverted Ministers; that unconverted Ministers ought not to continue in the Ministry*;*that he endeavoured to propagate this Opinion and a Practice agreable to it*; *that he aimed at People's forsaking unconverted Ministers*,*and endeavour'd that there should be a Supply of converted ones as far as in him lay*."]--Here you have expressed Mr. *W*-*d*'s Scheme in much fuller and stronger Terms than I did, especially as to the Way and Method by which it was to be effected; and this is exactly agreable to what I and others always supposed, *viz*. that Mr. *W*- designed to *turn out*the Ministers in this Manner, by laying a SCHEME *that People should forsake them*, by advancing this Opinion, *that unconverted Men ought not to continue in the Ministry*; and *endeavouring to propogate this Opinion*among the People, *and the Practice agreable to it*, i. e. their forsaking them accordingly.

Now since you have here in such full and *strong Terms* expressed and declared Mr. *W*-*d*'s SCHEME, it seems very unaccountable to me, to see you so *flatly deny it,*and I think you must have in your own Mind some strange Quibble or Equivocation.

Perhaps you'l say, that Mr. *W*- did not design *to turn them out himself,* but laid a Scheme how *the People* should do it by forsaking of them. But is not this in effect, the *same Thing*?

Suppose General PEPPERIL should be taken and carried into *Ca-*[^307-note3] *nada*, and there examin'd about the present Designs against *Cape Breton*, and he should make a *solemn Declaration*or *Oath*, that he never heard the Governour of *Boston*say any Thing of any Design of his to *turn out* the Governour of *Cape Breton*, or to take the Place, or any one Man in it; and that no such Thought, or any Thing *like it* ever entred into his Heart, till he heard of it at *Canada*, and had this *Salvo* in his own Mind, that the Governour had no Thought of doing of it himself, but only laid a *Scheme* how it should be done by the *Soldiers*, and endeavoured to propagate this Opinion and Practice among them; would not the World think that he had been to School to the *Jesuites*?

Perhaps you'l say, that Mr. *W*--*d*'s Scheme was, that only *Part* of the People (perhaps the converted) should*forsake*their Ministers, and the rest adhere to him, and so he should not be *turn'd out*. But his is contrary to your own Account of Mr. W--*d*'s Scheme; for if unconverted Ministers ought *not to continue* in the Ministry, they ought not to continue to be Ministers to *Part*, any more than to the *Whole*. And Mr. *W*-- endeavoured to propogate this Opinion and Practice, that People ought to forsake unconverted Ministers among *all Men in general*, without any Restriction *to some.* Suppose the *Pretender* should make another Invasion into *England*, and should declare himself to be the right Heir to the Crown and that no other Person ought to *continue* in the Possession of it, and endeavour to *propagate this Opinion and Practice,* and thereupon a considerable Number should cast off their Allegiance to his Majesty King GEORGE, and own the *Pretender* for their King; but afterwards the *Pretender* being apprehended, should *solemnly declare,* that he had *no Design*to dethrone the King, or to dispossess him of his Crown; that *no Thought* of that Nature, or any Thing *like it*, ever entred into his Heart (any more than to dethrone the *Grand Turk*, as in your Comparison) and that he only intended to protect a few *Englishmen* who voluntarily and out of Conscience submitted to him, but *intended* to leave King *George* in the full Possession of the Throne and Crown notwithstanding. What Credit do you think the World would give to such a Declaration?--

But perhaps you'll say, "that if every Man forsook the Minister, yet if he was not by Force *turned out of the Meeting House*, but suffered to preach there (tho' to the bare Walls) you might very fairly and *solemnly* deny that he was to be*turned out.*" But, *dear sir*, it is amazing [^307-note4] to me to think that a Gentleman of your Sincerity and Integrity should use any such solemn Quibbles and Equivocations, to amuse and deceive the World. And yet I must say, that I cna imagine no other Way to reconcile your solemn Declaration with your Letters, or with the *least appearance of Truth*.

In P. 5th you say, "I have sometimes said to others, that I *supposed* Mr. *W*- was formerely of the Opinion that unconverted Ministers ought not to continue in the Ministry" And I do *suppose* he endeavour'd to propagate this Opinion, *&c*. But all that ever I said about it, has been only as expressing my *Opinion*, and not any *declared Design*of Mr. *Wh*-*d*." But what can you mean by this Distinction? Must we suppose that Mr. *W*-*d* laid this *Scheme*, and propagated this Opinion and Practice, and yet had no *Design* in it? or that this Design was *secret* and not open and *declared*? I never supposed that he made an open and *formal Declaration*of it; *calling God to Witness* to the Truth of it. But only that he expressed himself to you is such Terms as were *plainly* to be understood. Or do you mean that this was a meer *Opinion*or *Supposition*in you, founded upon no *sufficient Evidence*? Many others supposed there was sufficient Evidence of it from his *preaching*and *Journals,*and I presume, as I always understood you, that you had it from his *own Mouth.* And certainly I must presume that you had some *very good Reason and Evidence* for it, or else you would never have taken up such an Opinion of Mr. *W--d*, and publish'd it to *others*, as you own you did. And if you did *rashly* take up and *publish* such Opinion of him, meerly upon Report or evil Surmising, without any sufficient Foundation, you ought to make a publick *Recantation* and Acknowledgement for abusing Mr. *W-d*. I shall be ready to do it, when I am convinced that that Opinion is *groundless*: And since you insist upon a *publick Recantation*for the Vindication of Mr. *W-d*, I'll make you this offer, *that if you will make a*publick Recantation of *this Opinion*, and declare (without calling God to witness) that you now believe that Mr. *W-d* never was in this *Scheme of People's forsaking unconverted Ministers*, that he never did *endeavour to propagate this Opinion, that unconverted Ministers ought not to continue in the Ministry, nor any Practice agreable to it*, and that he never did *aim at People's forsaking unconverted Ministers*, nor *endeavour that there should be a Supply of converted ones, as far as in him lay,*and that you wrong'd Mr. *W*- in taking up such an Opinion, and *speaking of it to others;*then I also will make a publick *Recantation* for *reporting* such a Thing from a Gentleman [^307-note5] whose *Opinion*and Judgment in that Matter *could not be depended upon,* and desire the World to take no Notice of it as coming from *you*.

However, since you acknowledge, that this was *once*your declared *Opinion*, how then can this be true, "that *no Thought* of Mr. *W-d*'s "saying or *hinting*any Thing of any Design of his of turning out any "Ministers, or any Thing LIKE IT *ever entered into your Heart, till* "you heard of it as coming from Mr. *Clap*?" I must leave others to re concile it if they can. But to use your Words, it is*one of the most - amazing Things to me that ever I met with in my Life*.

Again you say, "Mr. *W*. was *formerly* in this Opinion and Scheme, *&c*." which implies that you suppose that he has *lately* laid it aside. I wish I knew what *Evidence* you have of that. 'Tis certain he has never made any publick *Recantation of that Scheme*; but those who have *practiced* upon it by *forsaking* their Ministers, still adhere to him, and he still *encourages*them by preaching at the *separate Meetings*, as the Prints inform us. If you could have produced any Evidence that Mr. *Whitefield* had *recanted this Scheme*, it would have been much more for his Honour, than to have pretended to *deny that he was ever in it*. And I can't see how you can, consistent with your self, countenance his preaching, until it appears, either that you were *mistaken* in your Opinion of his being *formerly* in this Scheme, or that he has *laterly*made a *Recantation*of it.

But to proceed, my Words are [*and bring over Ministers from England*,*Scotland and Ireland]*You say from *England* only, and have no Remembrance of *Scotland* or *Ireland*, Here is some *Difference* in our Memories, but this is an *immaterial Circumstance* in the Scheme, *and not worthy of any Dispute.*For if any Part of the present Ministry were to be *discarded*, and a Number of *Foreigners* brought over, it matters but little whether they were all to come from *England* or some from *Scotland*, *Ireland*or the *Orphan House*. Indeed in my former Letter, I mention sundry Reasons why I do *verily*believe, that you mentioned *Scotland*and *Ireland,* and that Mr. *W*- *did intend*to Bring some Candidates from thence, and could now mention more; but as this is an*immaterial Point,*I shall wave it. And indeed you mention it and pass it over as if you laid but little Weight upon it. P. 11.

My Words are [*and place them in their Room*] Your Words are [^307-note6]

["Mr. *W*--*d* did aim at People's *forsaking* unconverted Ministers, and endeavour that there should be a *Supply* of converted Ministers"] Now this new *Supply* must necessarily be in the *Room*or*Place* of such as were *forsaken*. 'Tis true you say in your Letter, "that Mr. W- *didn't say one Word of any Design of these Foreigners supplying the Pulpits of other Ministers, made vacant by their being turned out.*" But this in the Circumstance of Things is *necessarily implied*, whether he particularly *express'd*it or not. For when any People have *forsaken*and *discarded* their Minister, they must have *another* in his *Room,* or else they must live without; and many of these must *be Foreigners,*because our Colleges are in such a *dark State*, as he represented them, that but a *little Supply* could be expected from *them*. Perhaps you will say, "that these Foreigners were to settle only where *Ministers* *died*, or in *new Parishes*, or to *be confin'd*to the *Jerseys* and *Pensylvania,* and not come into *New-England*." But I would appeal to the Common Sense of Mankind, whether there be any rational Foundation for either of these Suppositions. And the constant Practice of the *Tennant*'s in sending their Missionaries to our Separations proves the contrary. And therefore you might have spared that Clause in your Letter and Declaration, wherein you say, that Mr. *W*- did not say that the Persons ordained by the *Tennant*'s were to come into*New England;*since I never said that you did say so, or that you mentioned *New England in particular*, but the Nature of the Scheme, and the Practice of the *Tennant*'s makes it evident that they were to come *here* as well as to other Places.

In the last Place, I observe, that you say, P. 3. that tho' "you have on some Occasions mentioned it as your Opinion that Mr. *W*- was in this Opinion and Scheme, which possibly you might hear from *others*, yet I have no Remembrance of my having any Conversation with *you* about Things of this Nature." Yet in P. 5. you say, "that might be, and I might forget it," and in P. 9. "tho' I Remember no Conversation about Mr. *W*-- at that Time, yet it is possible I might say to *you,* that Mr. *W*-- did aim at People's forsaking unconverted Ministers, and endeavour that there should be a Supply of converted ones, *&c*." Yet in P. 14th you seem to think, that 'tis not very *likely* that you should *reveal such*a SECRET *to Me*. I have before observed, that a principal Part of this Scheme that Mr. *W*-*endeavoured to propagate this Opinion and Practice of People's forsaking unconverted Ministers, and that he intended*some where or other*to get a Supply*[10] *ply of converted ones,*was no*Secret* to me; and this you own *you said to others;* but as to this Part or Circumstance, *viz. that Mr. W-- told you that he intended to bring over a Number of young Men from England to be ordain'd by the Tennant's*--*&*c: This was truly a *Secret to me* 'till I had it from *you,*and must have remain'd a *Secret* 'till the Great-Day, unless you or some other Person had *revealed it to me.*Now as you say in another Case, I challenge the whole World besides *you,* to declare, if ever they gave me this Information; and therefore I think it falls but little short of Demonstration, that *you*must be the very Person who *revealed this Secret to me,*unless I had it by *immediate Revelation*.

And thus I have considered your Words (by me quoted) in all the Constructions which they can possibly bear, as they are in themselves, and they stand related to any other words in your Letters, which can possibly explain or alter the Sense of them, and have considered all the Evasions which you have made, or might make, and after all am of the same Opinion I was at first, that your Words must and will speak the same Sense in Substance with mine, and can't be avoided without the plainest Quibbles and Equivocations: and I leave the World to judge, whether I deserve any ill Treatment from you for being of *that Mind*.

That the Reader may have a comprehensive View of the Whole, I shall set down my Words and yours in Contrast in three Columns.

_________________________________________________________

My Words.*Your Letters to me.*Your Declaration and Letter.

Now let every Reader compare the Words as they here stand (a little abridg'd for want of Room) and as they stand in your printed Letters, and see whether this great Contradiction lies between the *first Column*and the *second*, or between the *second*and the *third*.

And I leave the World to judge, whether you have not treated me in a very unhandsom and *unchristian* Manner, in making such a publick Noise and Clamour, and amusing the World about a *great Contradiction* between us, and casting such Reflections, and endeavouring to *begin* a publick and personal Controversy with me, altho' you could not do it without *contradicting yourself*. I could with the greatest Justice return back many of your unhandsom Reflection in your own Words, but the Scripture as well as my own Inclination forbid me to render *Evil for Evil, and Railing for Railing;*and I am so far from it, that I freely forgive you, tho' you never ask it, or see Need of it. I hope that the future your Time will be *better employ'd*.

I remain, *Rev. Sir, Your humble Servant*, Thomas Clap. New-Haven, April 1. 1745.

## B53. Letter from Jonathan Judd, September 2, 1745 B053.J.Judd-JE 9-2-45 edited

Jonathan JuddB053. Jonathan Judd to JE, 9/2/45. BRBL, Sermon on Ps. 37:3(c) (c. Sept. 1745), f. 139.

Revd. & Dear Sir

I have Just heard that you desire me to assist you at the fast that you have appointed. I should Gladly have done it but I have appointed a Jarney into Connecticut and purpose God willing to set out Wenesday next so that I can not Come nevertheless I hope not to be backward to assist on such occasions when God permits

I Remain your unworthy friend and Bror, Jonathan Judd

September 2 1745 Northhampton

P.S. I am unaquainted with executing of Chh Censors I do therefore desire you would Let me have a form of an admonition & excommunication & I write this now that I might have them when I return home either by sending or Coming --- Not that I know I shall stand in need of either ------ I don't desire you to send ym before you hear from me again but should be Glad they might be ready

## B57. Letter from Thomas Wait, March 9, 1746 B057.T.Wait-JE 3-9-46 edited

Thomas WaitB057. Thomas Wait to JE, 3/9/46. BRBL, Sermons on Matt. 12:41 (May 1747), f. 460, Titus 3:2 (May 1747), f. 811. Addressed on back, "Thomas Waits Objecti / ons Against Lt Millers / Complaint."

Revrd Sr. I Object against the complaint Exhibited me by Lt John Miller dated the 27th day of last Febry, that it is trifiling & ought not to be regarded.

There are two things charg’d against me in the sd Complaint. one is fornication, the Other is falshood. ---------

As to that of fornication, tis Said that Jemima Miller chargd it upon me in time of travail, & continues still so to do, & yt there are many circumstances, which Joined with the sd Charge make it Evident (as the complainant concieves) that I am Guilty.

& as to the falshood, tis Said, the complainant Supposes I have in Several Instances Spoken falsely, & knowingly Contradicted the truth, but has not Intimated what those circumstances are that being Joined with Jemima Millers Accusation, make it Evident [. . .][^319-note1] Spoken falsely & knowingly contradicted the truth, which Should have been done, Or how can You know Sr: Whether the Complainants Suppositions & Imaginations are So well grounded as to be worthy of Your notice or how Can it be known if the Complainant Should Object Against me in Matters of like nature here after whether I have not been twice Charg’d & obliged to Answer for the Same fault or how can I be Able to make any defence or how Can those things be preserved in Memory as they Ought to be

Thomas Wait

Northampton March ye 9th: 1746 To the Revrd. Mr. Edwds. Pastor of the first Church in Northampton

[^319-note1]: The portion in the Sermon on Tit. 3:2 begins here. Some text, probably a line or two, is missing in the middle.

## B58. Letter from Joseph Pynchon, April 1, 1746 B058.J.Pynchon-JE 4-1-46 edited

Joseph PynchonB058. Joseph Pynchon to JE, 4/1/46. BRBL, Sermon on I Cor. 6:11 (Mar. 1747), f. 723. Addressed on back: "Revd / Mr Jonathan Edwards / In Northampton."

Rev Sir ---

I have at length sent the things for your two Daughters, have not had a good Opportunity before; need not say anything directing Concerning about the things, (having given ye directions before) except as to the End. Veneris, which I advised to be taken abt. 6 or 8 grains I think at a time. I have mixed it with a Conserve, and would have the quantity of half an haezlenut taken at a time, first at night going to bed for 2 or 3 nights, then if no ruffle or disorder attends (which sometimes is ye Case) morning & night the same Quantity ------- Æthiops Mineral, have none yet, design very shortly to make some --- I am with due Regards to Yr Self, Madm & Family

Yr V Humbl Servt Joseph Pynchon Springfd, April 1. 1746 --- Rev Mr Jonathan Edwards ---
