## B62. Petition from Ephraim Marble to the Northampton Church, [After November 15, 1746] B062.E.Marble-JE after11-15-46 edited

Ephraim MarbleB062. Ephraim Marble to JE, n.d. [after 11/15/46]. BRBL, "Hebrew Idioms," f. 1211 (the cover of "Hebrew Idioms" is a copy of the *Boston Gazette* for Jan. 6, 1747). Addressed on back "For the Revd / Mr Edwards of / North Hampton." To the Curch and Conggregation in North Hampton Christian Frinds the petision of Ephm Marble of the North Parte of Sunder Land humbly sheweth that almighty god in his holy & wise Providence hath Layd his hand heavy uppon me not onely in multiplyd Deaths in my famely and Bodyly indispositions in my Self but also in outher Temmporall Losses Pertickerly in the Loss of my Dwell ing house a Considerable Part of the Furniture weavers shop Loom Tackling with my Store of Indin Corn Considerable outhr Grain with my outher Store for for the Suport of Life & I being a Stranger in these Parts my Native Place & Relations being at a great Distance and my Neighbours whear i now Live being new beginers and as yet but Low in Estate in generall and my Nesesetys great i am Contraned Ernestly to Beg your Charity that you would Contribute to my Nesesetys which great which if god shall Incline you to do I pray that he would grant me a thankfull heart boath to him self and you I would Earnestly Desire your Prayers for me that god would Sanctifie to me these Dispensations of his Providence. Sunderland Note the above mentioned Loss was by fire the Night fawling the 15 of this Instant Novembr I Subscribe your Humble Petisioner Ephraim Marble

## B63. Letter from Thomas Gillespie, November 24, 1746 B063.T.Gillespie-JE 11-24-46 edited

Thomas GillespieB063. Thomas Gillespie to JE, 11/24/46. ANTS f. 1744-46, #2. Probably a draft.

To Mr Edwards at Northampton N England Novemr 1746

R & D Sir

I have ever honoured you for your Works Sake, & what the great Shepherd made you the Instrument of from the Time you published the then very extraordinary Account of the Revival of Religion at Northampton I think in the Year 1735. The two performances you Publishd on the Subject of the late Glorious Work in New England well Adapted to that in Scotland gave me great Satisfaction especially the last of them for Peculiar Reasons this much I think myself bound to Say. I have Many a Time for some Years designed to Claim humbly the privilege of Correspondence with you. What has made me defer doing it so long When Some of my Brethren & Acquaintances have been Favourd with it for a Considerable While tis Needless now to Mention I Shal only Say I have blamed my self for Neglect in that Matter. I do now earnestly desire a Room in your Friendship & a Letter from you Sometimes when you have Occasion to Write to Scotland & I Shal Wish to be as Regular as I can in making a return I Propose to Trouble you Now & then with proposal of Doubts & Difficulties that I meet with & am exercisd with as for other Reasons so because some Solutions in the two Mentiond performances were peculiarly Agreeable to me & I find from these Discourses that Wherein I have differd in Some Things from Many others &c. My Sentiments harmonizd with Mr Edwards’s this especially was the Case in Some Things contained in [---] Thoughts concerning Revival of Religion in New England. All the Apology I make for using such Freedom tho Altogether Unacquainted is you Will find from my Short Attestation in Mr. Robe’s Narrative I am no Enemy to you or to the Work you have been engagd in & Which you have defended in a Way I Could not but much Approve. Also my Friend & Countryman the Rev Mr. Robert Abercrombie will inform you about me if you have Occasion to See him or hear from him.

I long’d Much to See Somwhat about Impressions respecting Facts & Future Events whether by Scripture Texts or otherwise made on the Minds of Good People & Suppos’d to be from the Lord for I have had too Good Occasion to know the hurtful yea Pernicious tendency of this Principle as commonly Mannagd &c. upon Many Persons & in [------] Instances & respects. it has indeed Surprized me Much that Wise holy & Learn’d Divines as well as others have Supposd this a Spiritual Experience An Answer of Prayers an Evidence of being highly Favourd by the Lord &c. & I Was exceeding glad, the Lord had directed you to give in so Seasonable a Caveat against What I’m Assurd you had the best Reason to Term "A Handle in the hand of the Devil &c." I was only Sorry your then Design had not permitted you to say more on that Point that Merits a Volume & the proper full Discussion of Which Would be one of the most Seasonable effectual Services done the Church of Christ & Interest of Vital Religion thro the World that I know of. I Rejoice to find there is a Good deal more on that Subject interspersed in your Treatise of Religious Affections which I have [-------] but could not as yet regularly Peruse. I humbly think the Lord Calls you D Sir to Consider every part of that Point in the most Critical Manner & to represent fully the Consequences resulting from the Several Principles in that Matter, good People as Well as others, have been so fond of if I don’t mistake Providence has already put that in your hand as a part of your Generation Work, & it will give me as Well as others vast Satisfaction to find more Said on the Subject by you if you don’t find What is in the Mentiond Treatise Sufficient as to Which I can form no Judgment because I have not as yet considered it. If any other Author has has Treated that Subject I don’t remember to have met with it & I Believe [2] Hell has been no less delighted than Surpriz’d a Regular Attack has not been made on that Side [--] Now [-] I doubt not they dread the Consequences of Such Assault with exquisite Horror the Neglect or Oversight Mistake of so Many Learned Authors who have Insisted on Doctrines that bear Similitude of Relation to this Matter while it was Pass’d over I humbly Think Should Teach us Humility & some other useful Lessons I Need not Name to Mr Edwards.

I hope D Sir it will not Offend you that I humbly offer Some Remarks upon What I have observed in looking into your Treatise on Religious Affections & upon farther perusal shal frankly represent what I may find difficulty about if any such passage shal cast up expecting you Will be so Good as to set me right if I have or Shal Mistake or Not perceive you Meaning. Pages 74 & 5. there are Several Passages I do not Well understand [-] [-----] Pag 74 Line 3 a fin You Say "That they Should Confidently Believe and Trust While [--] they yet remain without Spiritual Light or Sight is an Antiscriptural and Absurd Doctrine"[^325-note1] had you Said they could or would not Believe & Trust without Spiritual Light this [-------] but I humbly Apprehend the Position Will not hold as you have laid it Whether it is applied to a Sinner or a Saint as I Suppose you Understand it for tho the Sinner never will Believe on the Lord Jesus till he has received a Saving Manifestation of his Glory by the Work of Spirit yet every Sinner we know is Indispensably Bound by the Divine Authority to Believe instantly in the Lord Jesus. the Command of the Lord I Jo 3,23. [-] believe on the Name of his Son Jesus Christ &c. as to a Prescription of the Moral Law no less binds the Sinner to Immediate Performance than the Commandment not to kill to keep the Sabbath Day or any other Duty as to the present performance of Which in Way of Duty all Agree the Sinner is bound. I Suppose none of us think we are bound or will Adventure to Preach the Sinner should Delay to Attempt to Believe in the Saviour till he finds Light from Heaven Shining into his Mind or has got a Saving Discovery of the Lord Jesus. tho tis certain he cannot Believe nor Will do it effectually ‘till favourd with Such Light or Sight because we Should in that event put in Qualification where the Apostle Paul put none Such in their Exhortation to the Jaylor Acts 16,31. Also as it may be the last Call the Sinner is to receive in dispensation of the Word we are bound to require him instantly to Believe Whatever he does or does not feel in himself. If you did intend not the Sinner but the Saint in the [----] Positions as I am apt to think your Scope Plainly intimates Still Im Afraid there is Ambiguity at least in your Words for I humbly Apprehend the Christian is bound to trust the Divine Faithfulness plighted in the Promise for Needful Blessings be his Case with respect to Light or Darkness Sight &c. what it will & that No Situation the Saint can be in looes him from obligation to glorify the Lord at all Seasons by Trusting in him & expecting fulfillment of his Word Suiting his Case. Also I Would Imagine Is. 50, 10. [-----] the Saint to Believe in the Precise Circumstances mentiond in your Assertion above mentiond. Pardon my Freedom. You do Indeed Say it is truly the Duty of those Who are thus in darkness to come out of Darkness into Light & Believe" Pag 74 Lin 5 a fin fin but how to reconcile that with the Mentiond Assertion that immediately [3] follows I am indeed at a loss. Sometimes I think, it is not Believing the Promise or trusting the Lord & trusting in him you mean in the Positions I have cited but the belief of the Goodness of ones State that he is a Saint. if that was what you intended I heartily Wish you had Said so Much in the Book but as this is not ordinarily What is Meant by Believing in Scripture I Must Suppose it was not the Idea affixed to your Words. had you plainly Stated the Distinction twixt an Possibility ones Actually believing & its yet being his Duty to Believe in the Circumstances you Mentiond Danger of Mistake & a handle for Cavil [------------] had been Cut off. Pag 75 Lin 11 &c. You Say "to press and Urge them to Believe, without any Spiritual Light or Sight tends greatly to help forward the Delusions of the Prince of Darkness" had you Said to press them to believe the Lord was their God When going on in a Course of Sin or when Sinning presumptuously was of Such Tendency. Which Possibly was in Part what you design’d it would in my Humble Apprehension have been much more Safe for Reasons given. Also as ‘tis Ordinarily & Justly observd they who are most humbled think they are least so When under Saving Work of the Spirit perhaps in like Manner Spiritual Light & Sight may in Some instances be Mistaken or not duly Apprehended in Which Case the person upon your Suppositions, may be apt to give Way to Unbelief & Say if I am not to be Urg’d by the Lords Servants to Believe in my present Circumstances it Would Surely be presumption in me to entertain Thoughts of Attempting it. Or it may be he shal think he has not that Degree of Spiritual Light or Sight that is Absolutely Necessary in order to his Believing & thus the Evil Heart of Unbelief shal make him depart from the Living God & Neglect to Set too his Seal that he is true. if have deduced Consequences from your Words and Manner of Reasoning which you think they do not Justly bear I’ll be glade to be rectified by You D Sir, & Would be [---] Satisfied to know from you how the Mentiond [-------] tends to help forward the Delusions of Satan. I am apt to Believe the Grounds upon Which you proceeded in the Whole Paragraph I have Mentiond is you have with you Real Antinomians who Teach things About faith & Believing Subversive of New Obedience & Gospel Holiness & Inconsistent with the Scripture Doctrines Concerning them But as we have few if any Such at all (I Believe I might say more) who ever Vented Such Opinins in this Country & Numbers who Would have the most Accurate & Judicious [-] Evangelical Preachers to Insist a great deal more upon Doing & Less upon Believing for What Reasons you Well perceive I Am I expect a Mighty Clamour by the Seceders if the Book Shal fall into yr^hand. What is expressd by you Pag 75 Lin 22 &c. is I have frequently heard it Taught by them Accounted the most orthodox that the Believer was bound to Trust in the Lord in the very Worst Frame he could be in & that the Exercise of Faith was the Way to be Deliverd from Backsliding &c & tis Impossible one Should Err who follows the Course prescribed by the Lord in his Word. & I Suppose no Person is bound or Allowd to deferr Believing one Single Moment because he finds himself in a bad Situation, because the Spirit Breathes not on him or he finds not Actual influence rendring him capable of Believing or meet for it Communicated to him at that Season for this Reason that not our Ability or Fitness but the Lords Command is the Rule of Duty &c. on any Account.

Pag 275 You Cite as an Authority Mr Stoddard Affirming Lin 5 [--] "One Way of Sin is exception enough against Mens Salvation tho their Temptations be great" I well remember the singularly Judicious Dr Owen Somewhere Says that & to be affirmed [-] prevalence of a Particular Sin over a Person for a Considerable Time Shews him no Saint except when under the Power of a Strong Temptation [-] I Would Suppose Such Texts as Is 64:6 Ps 65,3. &c. Warranted the Doctor. to Assert as he did. tis no Small difficulty to Steer the middle Course twixt Affording Hypocrites ground Unwarrantably to Presume on the one Hand & Wounding the Lords dear Children on the other & All the litle knowledge of the Scriptures I Would hope the Lord has given me Satisfies me Mr Shepherd good & great Man as he he was verg’d not a litle to the last Extreme with whom If I mistake not Mr Stoddart has Symbolizes in the above Assertion for such is the drift & tendency of Mr Shepherds Principles. daily experience & Observation confirms me Still more we should be very Cautious & Modest when [-----] [------] Asserting on that Head & go no farther in the Matter than we have plain Scripture to bear us out. The Consideration that Indwelling Sin Sometimes gets such Ascendant that the New Creature is as fire buried under Ashes Undiscerned & Inactive lays Foundation for Saying Somwhat Stronger on that Point than I would Choose to Utter in Publick Teaching Pag 276. you Say "Nor can a true Saintose it belongs not to us precisely to Determine ever fall away so that it shal come to this that ordinarily there Shal be no remarkable difference in his Walk & behaviour Since his Conversion from What was before" I do not remember the Scripture any Where Mentions that David or Solomon were Sanctified from the Womb. & tis Evident for a Considerable Time Ordinarily & for a long Time in the Case of the latter there was a remarkable difference to the Worse on the Walk & behaviour of both of them when we are Sure they were Saints from what it had been in their Younger Years. besides let us Suppose a Person of a Good Natural Disposition bred up in Aversion to all Vicious Practices by a Religious Education & Example & Virtuous Inclinations thus Cultivated in him 2 Pet 2:20. Converted When come to Maturity & Afterward Corruption in him Meets with peculiar Temptations. I doubt much if there would be a remarkable difference twixt his Present Conversion & that in Irregeneracy the contrary I believe is found in experience & the Principles laid down leave Room to Suppose it.

I own in What I have above Said I have perhaps gone farther than became [---] [---] Man in Writing to One of Mr Edwards’s Reading & Experience & am heartily Sorry my first Letter to you in Providence is in Such a Strain & on Such a Subject but Love to you D Sir & Concern lest you should be thought to Patronize What I am sure you do not made me write with such Freedom & break over Restraints Modesty Decency &c. Should otherwise have laid me under that you Might have Opportunity to know in What Light these things I Mention to You cast up to some Who are your real Friends in this Countrey. A Valuable Minister on looking into what is Noticed in Pages 74 & 75 Said to me it would be right some Should Write you About it, & I take this first Opportunity that you may have Access to Judge of the Matter & what it may be proper for you to do or not to do in it

I Will expect an Answer with Convenience & hope you Will deal freely with me for I can Say I Would Sit down and learn at your feet Dr Sir Accounting my Self as a Child in Knowledge of the Scriptures When Compared with others I will not Name & the Longer I Live Value Still less [ ] knlwledge of other kinds. Conceal Nothing that you think will tend to put me right if you find my Views are not Just. I proposed at the beginning to trouble you with some Questions & Shal Mention one or two at present What should a Saint do who is Incessantly harassd by Satan can by no Means keep him out of his Mind has Usd all Means prescribd in Scripture Suggested by Divines known to him in vain it may be for a long Time has roard to Christ but he hears not Seems not to regard him all his efforts are Swallowd up in the Deluge of the Violence of the Foe do what he Will Seems to gain litle or no ground against the Powers of Darkness is apt to dread he shal Sink under the Load and never shal be deliverd in this World What Would you advise Such a Person to do What Construction think you he should put on the Sovereign Conduct & Dispensation of Heaven toward him I have Occasion to be Conversant about this Case practically Demonstrated of many Years Continuance & Will therfore be glade to have your Mind about it in a particular Manner & as much at large as you conveniently can. Rom 2:15. All Things Work for Good &c. As Degrees of Grace & Glory Will be in proportion to them of Grace how can it be Suppos’d & Made appear it is for ones Good what Somtimes happens to a Saint their being permitted to fall under Backslidings & Spiritual Decays & to Die in that State perhaps after continuing in it a Considerable While & When their Situation has been attended with the Melancholy Circumstances & Consequences that Somtimes have place in that State of Matters the Solution of this I Would gladly receive from you. Are the Works of great Mr Boston known in your Countrey Viz the Fourfold State of Man, View of the Covenant of Grace & a Discourse on Afflictions, & Church communion &c. if not inform me by your Letter. I have now need to own my Fault in troubling you with so long a Letter & so I Shal End &c.

[^325-note1]: Gillespie writes the insertion in the margin: "[illeg.] Say of ye Doctrine you are refuting ‘but this Doctrine as it is understood by Many is that Christians ought firmly to Believe&Trust in Christ [without / Light or Sight&tho they are in a dark dead frame&for the present having no spiritual experiences and discoveries].’" The conclusion, in brackets, is a conjectural reading supplied from the printed text where the edge of the MS ppage is rubbed away in the original.

## B70. Letter from William Russell, October 30, 1747 B070.W.Russell-JE 10-30-47 edited

William RussellB070. William Russell to JE, 10/30/47. BRBL, Sermon on Is. 47:3-4 (Sept. 1749), f. 306. Cut in two near left side, no address on back.

Revd: & Dear Sir

Mr Daviss of Long Island Latly came here and Sent to me to take care of a trunk wch. he had brought that belong’d to Cousin Sarah. wch. I did and it is now at my house. my family are thro Divine goodness in ordinary health. tho it hath been and is yet a sickly and dying time among us. I Conclude you have heard of Capt Phillips death wch. is a Publick Loss I thank you for the sermon you sent me and my Daughters send their Duty to their Aunt & Love to their Cousins thank her for their fans. I have nothing remarkable to Inform you of. please to Accept my Love and Service to yr Self and Sister. and give my Respects to Cousins. I desire a Continual Interest in yr prayers for me (& mine)

who Am Yr. Loving Brother W. Russel Midd: Octobr 30th. 1747

## B71. Letter from Samuel Hopkins of Springfield, May 18, 1748 B071.S.Hopkins-JE 5-18-48 edited

Samuel Hopkins of SpringfieldC071. Samuel Hopkins of Springfield to JE, 5/18/48. Incomplete at end. BRBL, f. 1187, sermon fragments.

Springfield May 18 1748

Revd Sir

I have been upon sister Backus's business &c. and find: That it is uncertain Whether those officers who are applying home will obtain King's pay; and if not there is no hope of a pension for any widow. Again it is uncertain (I can find no person yt can inform me) whether A Chaplin's widow, has right to a pension in any Case. Brother Backus's name is gone home to England in ye muster Roll and he is there represented as haveing died in ye service. Secratary Willys and others, therefore advised to let the matter rest till we Can know, whether those officers who are applying home do succeed. and till we Can find whether it ever has been usual yt A Chaplin's widow is ever Consider'd in such a case. I have taken Care that Agent Palmer should be Enquired of. And ye Secratary tells me: That if we hear from ye agent yt such are wont to have pensions. […] will be Easie and he will be ready to do what […]

## B72. Letter from Thomas Chapin (Copy), June 29, 1748 B072.T.Chapin-JE 6-29-48 edited

Thomas ChapinB072. Thomas Chapin to JE, 6/29/48. BRBL, f. 1536. Copy in unknown hand, possibly that of Sereno Dwight.

To the Rev: Mr Jona: Edwards, Northampton . June 29. 1748.

Sir. I have recd: your letter, & purpose shortly to give you an opportunity to discourse with me about your cows. In ye mean time, I design to have your cows, if we can agree upon reasonable terms. I desire & depend upon having your cows, when we can discourse about them.

from I am your servant, Thomas Chapin

## B73. Letter from Thomas Gillespie, September 19, 1748 B073.T.Gillespie-JE 9-19-48 edited

Thomas GillespieB073. Thomas Gillespie to JE, 9/19/48. ANTS, f. 1748, #1. Printed in *Edinburgh Quarterly Magazine* 1 (1798), with alterations.

Letter to Mr Edwards 19th Septemr 1748

R V D Sir

I had the Favour of yours in Spring last for Which I heartily Thank You. I did not Want Inclination to make you a return long Ago as I prize your Correspondence but Some Things concurr’d that effectually Prevented me And that has given me Concern.

It was Desire to be Inform’d & Inclination to make You Understood how Some Passages in your Book on Religious Affections did Appear to me & Some other Your Real Friends & Well Wishers in this Countrey that Determind me to Presume to Offer you Some Free Remarks on the Mentiond Passagges in my late Letter & desire of further Information engages me now with all respect to make Some Observations upon Some Things in your Letter & I hope you will Pardon my Freedom & bear with me in it & Set me right Wherin you may find me to Misapprehend your Meaning or to Mistake in Another Respect.

You say "there is a great deal of Difference between these two Things Viz its being a Mans Duty that is Without Spiritual Light or Sight [--] to Believe, & its being his Duty to Believe Without Spiritual Light or Sight" Now D Sir the Difference here I am not Able to Conceive for All are bound to Believe the Divine Testimony & Trust in Christ which you Acknowledge & the Want of Spiritual Light or Sight does not loose from the Obligation one is laid Under by the Divine Command to Believe Instantly and at all Seasons the Promise as his Circumstances require Nor does it Excuse him in any Degree for not Believing. I own a Person Who has No Spiritual Light or Sight cannot eventually if by Light or Sight is Meant the Influence & Grace of the Spirit by Which ones Mind is Irradiated to take up the Object & Grounds of Faith so as to be Made Act that Grace Yet Still even When One Wants this it is his Duty and he is bound to Believe for we know it is a Maxim Ability is not Rule of Duty I Also Acknowledge that no Person Who is & Always has been Without Spiritual Light or Sight is bound nor is it his Duty to Believe he has Actually Believed or to Conclude he is really a partaker of the faith of Gods Elect.[^335-note1] I have some Apprehension this is all you Meant by the Expressions I have Noticed & the Reasoning in Consequence of it or Certainly different Ideas are affix’d to Words With You & Among us.

There is indeed a great deal of Difference twixt its being ones Duty to Believe or to Act Faith & its being his Duty to Believe he has Believed or has Acted Divine Faith that is You Say You Apply Without Spiritual Light or Sight [--] to the Act of Believing by Which I Suppose you Intend none do really Believe Without Spiritual Light or Sight in Which I entirely Agree with You Tho the Word Duty is Ordinarily Supposd to Signify the Obligation the Person is under by the Divine Authority to Believe as Applied to the Matter of Faith And not [-] the Act of Faith put forth in Consequence of Such Obligation & had I not Suppos’d You plainly intended by the Expressions I Quoted from the Book the Duty or Obligation to Believe & Not An Act of Faith exerted I Should have made no Remark upon them. tis indeed Absurd for one to Conclude he has really Believd Without Spiritual Light or Sight or to Say One should Believe he has Believed eventually Without "these Things that Are Essentially Implied in Faith" but I must [---] ‘tis very proper to Say tis a Mans Duty to Believe Without Faith that is to put forth an Act of Faith on the Saviour however Void of Spiritual Light or Sight for if this was not the Truth the finally Impenitent Sinner could not be Condemnd for his Unbelief as the holy Ghost declares he Will be Jo 3,19. 8,24. & that Notwithstanding the Power of a Spirit of Faith must make him Believe.

You remark that I "Seem to Suppose that a Persons doubting of his own Good Estate is proper Opposite of Faith" & I own as it is a Believers Duty to expect Salvation through Christ Which in other Words is to Believe his Good Estate Acts 15,11. Gal 2,20. Eph 2,4 "doubting of it must be his Sin an Effect of Unbelief a Part of it & thus the proper Opposite of Faith Considerd in its full Compass & Latitude [-] doubting of [-] Good Estate by a True Believer & Unbelief in One Branch of it or one Part & Manner of its Acting are the Same Thing. [--] that Confident of ones Good Estate upon [--] Grounds & Faith & Conditions of it must be [---] Faith & Unbelief Are Opposed in Scripture [^335-note2] What is the Opposite of One Ingredient in Unbelief must be Faith in One Part of it one Thing that belongs to its Exercise A Persons Believing the Lord Will never leave nor forsake him Who is in a Gracious State Heb 13,5 is ownd to be his Indispensable Duty & this Comprehends or Supposes his being Confident of his Good Estate & is properly Divine Faith because it has the Divine Testimony now Cited on Which it Bottoms Jer 3,19. The Lord Says - thou Shalt Call me my Father & Shalt not turn away from me Which is evidently Faith Manifestly Belief of ones Good Estate or being Confident of it because the Expression must denote the Continued Exercise of Faith Crying Abba Father Ro 8,15. is Faith in the Lord as ones Father Which must have a being Confident of ones Good Estate Inseperable from it or rather Enwrapped in it [----] I Suppose What I have Mentiond is very Consistent with What you Say "That Faith & Persons Believing that they have Faith are Not the Same" for Ones Believing that he has Faith simply & by itself has for its Object the Mans inward Frame or the Actings & Exercises of his Spirit & Not a Divine Testimony but as I have laid the Matter A being Confident of ones Good Estate has for its Foundation the Word of God Heb 13,5 &c. Ultimately to be Sure, thus is One Way in Which Faith is Acted or One Thing in its Exercise.

I am far from Thinking [-] Unbelief or being Without Faith & doubting Whether they have Faith to be the Same Thing in an Unconverted Sinner Whom Your Words being Without Faith must Mean & therin we Entirely Agree. But I Must Think as the Believer his Doubting [--] he has Faith is Sinful because it is Belying the Holy Ghost denying his Work in him so [-] no Sin to Which that Doubting can so Properly be reducd As Unbelief. You know Dr Sir Doubting & Believing are Opposed in Scripture Mat 14,31. [-] 21,21. Mar 11,23. & I Cannot Exclude from the Idea of Doubting Questioning the Truth & Reality of a Work of Grace on Ones Soul for the Holy Ghost requires us to Believe the Reality of his Work in us in All its Parts Just as it is & Never Would Allow us, much less call us to Sin Believe a Falshood that one is Void of Grace When he has it that Good Might come of it the Person Might be Awaken’d from Security &c. I Jo 3,3. every Man that hath this Hope in him Purifieth himself as he is Pure Which I think Intimates in Proportion to One’s Hope [-] the Lord is his Father Will be his his Aim after Sanctification & his Attainment of it if so to Renounce[^335-note3] this Hope throw it up at any Season on any Account Must be Unlawful Whence I Infer for the Believer to Doubt of his Gracious State to Call it in Question on Any Account Whatever so as to Raze it it is Simply Sinful 1 Jo 2,12,15. [--] I Write Unto You little Children because your Sins are forgiven You V 15 Love Not the World -- here Forgiveness of Sin is Us’d as a Motive & Incitment not to Love the World & this Reasoning of the Apostle Would lose All its Force for so long Was it Incumbent on a Believer at Some Seasons to think he was not within the Bond of the New Covenant thus he is bound ever to hold that Conclusion fix’d The Exhortation not to Cast Away ones Confidence certainly Comprehends a Call to Persevere in Believing Interest in the Lord & to Practise it att all Seasons Heb 10,35. Jobs Friends endeavour’d to Make him Question that the Root of the Matter was in him & to Conclude that he was an Hypocrite He resolv’d tho’ the Lord should slay him he Would Trust in him Ch 13,15. be Confident of his own Good Estate & Ch 27 3,5 All the While my Breath is in me - & V 5 ‘till I Die I Will not Remove my Integrity from me & We See from the Whole Tenor of his Book What there he resolv’d he Actually did Practise Never entertaind the Thought of Supposing the Lord was not his God Notwithstanding the Grievous Eruptions of Corruption in him in Quarrelling Sovereignty &c And in the End the Lord Condemn’d his Friends for Speaking of him the Thing that was not right pronounc’d Job his Servant Who had Said of him the Thing that is Right from Which tis to be Presumd he Was Approv’d in Guarding against Razing his State 2 Cor 1,12 What the Apostle Terms there his Rejoicing Was What Supposd his being confident of his Good Estate that he was participant of a Principle of Grace Which Made him Capable of Acting as he did with Godly Sincerity All Which with other Considerations do Satisfy me that a Believer never should raze his State on Any Account Whatever & that as has been Mentiond doubting of his Gracious State is Sinful one way of Unbelief its Acting in him tho’ not the Direct & Immediate Opposite of that Acting of Faith by Which a Person renounces his own Righteousness & Closes with Christ yet the Opposite of the Posterior Exercise of Faith in him in Certain Respects. Your Book is now Lent & therefore I Cannot take Notice as you Wish & I incline of What you Say on this Head P 76, 77. More Particularly than I have done However I have I think touch’d the Precise Point in Difference twixt us

You Observe I Seem to Intimate "A Persons being Confident of his own Good Estate is the Way to be deliverd from Darkness Deadness Backsliding & Prevailing Iniquity" And You Add that " you think Whoever Supposes this to be Gods Method of delivering his Saints When Sunk into an Evil Careless, Carnall & Unchristian Frame first to Assure them of their Good Estate & his Favour -- And so to Make that the Means of their Deliverance does Surely Mistake Gods Method of dealing with such Persons" here I think You represent the Case Strong for the Words in my Letter to Which you referr were "I have heard it Taught that the Believer was bound to Trust in the Lord in the Very Worst Frame he could be in & that Exercise of Faith was the Way to be deliver’d from Darkness Deadness Backsliding &c." And Afterwards I Said When Questioning Whether the Believer should ever Doubt of his State on Any Account Whatever "I know the Opposite has been Prescribd when the Saint is Plungd in the Mire of Prevailing Iniquity" Now as a Believer may be thus Plung’d & Yet Sin at that Instant his Grief & Burden Ro 7,24. & he May have the Hope & Expectation of being Relieved from it even then Ps 65,3. I do Not think my Words conveigh the Idea you Affix to them Also you Will Observe I do not Say that a Persons being Confident of his own Good Estate is the Way to be Deliverd from &c." but that the Believer Was bound to Trust the Lord in the Worst Frame &c. this I Mention precisely to State my Words & they are I think Very Defensible for the Believer is Calld to Trust in the Lord forever Is 26,4. if so When in the Situation Mentiond the Woman with the Issue of Blood her Touching Christ the Success is I Suppose A Call & Encouragment to Touch him by Faith for having the Worst Soul Maladies Heald Mar 5,25. Trusting the Lord for Needful Blessings in the Situation Mentiond gives him the Glory of his Faithfulness & Engages him to Act in the Believers behalf thus to do it is both Duty & Interest Jonah in a Course of Grievous Rebellion & Awful Chastisment for it When perhaps he had Actually disclaimd Interest in the Lord or Was in Danger of it Said He Would look again toward [--] Holy Temple" Ch 2,4. & V 7 When my Soul fainted Within me I remembred the the Lord & my Prayer came in Unto Thee into Thine Holy Temple. Here is [^335-note4] My Assertion Exemplified in Practice by a Believer I may Venture to Say in an Evil Frame [--] tho a Prophet he deliberatly Disobeyd the express Instructions of his great Lord in a Careless Frame for he sleepd Securely in the Sides of the Ship While an Awful Storm Rag’d raisd for his Sake & the Heathen Mariners every one Calld upon his God Ch 1, 5,6. So far was from Dreading as he had Reason the Lord Would Plead a Controversy With him for the Part he Acted Dismal Security Awful Carelessness in a Carnal Frame for he Declar’d to the Lord he Said to him in his Countrey that he Would Repent of the Evil he had Said he Would do to the Ninevites if they Turnd from their Evil Way And Assignd that for the Reason Why he fled to Tarshish[^335-note5] & Displeasd him Exceedingly & he Was Very Angry that the Lord did not to to that People what he Threatend tho they turnd from Evil & upon this beggd the Lord Would take Away his Life & Said it was better for him to Die than to Live Ch 3,10. Ch 4 V 1-4. Horrid Carnality this for he car’d not What became of the Lords Honour if his Supposd One was Securd Was Sorry for the Success of his Mission Would rather have the Whole City Destroyd one of the most Populous the Sun Shone upon than he should Come under the Imputation of a False Prophet for Which there was yet no Foundation & as this was horrid Dreadful Selfishness may it in that View be termd Carnality Astonishing Pride thus Filthiness of the Spirit Worse than that of the Flesh in an Unchristian Frame for he sinn’d Presumptuously in the highest Degrees we may Suppose in Which ‘tis Possible for a true Believer so to Act & All Circumstances in his then Conduct evidence Such was his Frame Notwithstanding it Appears Under the Influence of the Spirit the Happy Turn began in him receiving Faith in the Lord as his God & being Confident of his Good Estate on Which he Prayed Was heard by his God V 7 & Deliverd out of his then Dismal and Dangerous Circumstances So that I have done more than I Was bound prov’d the Point not only in the Manner I Expressd it but in the Strong Light your Words a Comment on Mine had Set it for One Plain Scripture Instance Such as is that I have given is Sufficient to Prove Any Thing. And to All this it Cannot be excepted What I Mention was after Jonah had Acted as in Ch 2 V 4,7. for I might Detach What is Mentiond Ch 4, V 2, from the [^335-note6] Unchristian Also What we have Ch 2 V 4,7. Was his begun recovery What we have Ch 3 V 10 Ch 4, 1,3. a Relapse after Said recovery then in Consequence of Restoration to a better Temper he had received a New Prophetical Commission to go to Nineveh & Which he Executed & What was the Mean in Heavens Hand of his recovery in One Case must by Just Rules of Interpretation be Presumd to have been so in the other or to have been Suitable for that End & thus Usd by the Lord in his Sovereign Dispensation for that Purpose Which Comes to the Same. to Say that it is "the Lords method of Delivering his Saints When in a Backsliding Frame first to Assure them of their Good Estate & his Favour & so to Make that the Means of their Deliverance" is so far from being a Mistaking Gods Method as you Suggest that I give you the Words of the Holy Ghost as express & full for & as any Thing Possibly can by Jer 3, 12, 13 [-] 14. Turn O Backsliding Children Saith the Lord for I am Married unto You -- this Was to be Sure the Lords Intimating the Covenant Relation in Which he Stood to the Spiritual Israel Among them And V 22 of that Chapter the Lord Says return ye Backsliding Children & I Will heal your Backslidings & in the Close of the Verse we have the Lords thus Assuring them of their Good Estate & his Favour the effectual Mean of their Backsliding being heald -- behold we Come Unto thee for thou art the Lord our God. Hos 14,1. O Israel return unto the Lord thy God for thou hast fallen by Thine Iniquity here the first Words of the Lords Message to his Spiritual Israel are that the Lord was their God & the Expression fallen by Iniquity Conveighs a Very Strong Idea perhaps as Strong, as is Comprehended in your Words I think Were a Comment on Mine Evil &c Frame & I Must think this Verse is So Express’d to Work on Holy Ingenuity in them for its Revival When Under the Ashes of Corruption it Would perhaps be no Difficult Matter to Multiply Scripture Testimonies of such kind but these Adduced Are I think full Proof of the Point for Confirmation of Which they are brought tis like the Love of Christ Constrains the Believer to return from Folly as Well as to other Things in other Respects 2 Cor 5,14. I Might Argue here from the efficacy of the Love of God Apprehended the Genius of the New Creature & Nature in in Believers & a Variety of other Topicks but Choose Without [^335-note7] Expatiating to Confine my Self to Precise Scripture Testimonies. As to What you Say "that of All the Multitudes you have had Opportunity to Observe you Never knew one Dealt with in this Manner [-] but have known Many brought back from great Declensions that Appeared to be True Saints but it was in a very Diverse Way from this first - Conscience Awakned - they brought into great Fear of the Wrath of God - his Favour hid - they Subjects of a kind of New Work of Humiliation brought to great Sense of Deserving Gods Wrath - While they yet Feard it before God has deliverd from Apprehension of it & Comforted with a renewd Sense of his Favour" All I Observe upon this is the Way I have laid down Obviously is that the Lord declares in his Word he takes for bringing back his People from Declensions & thus in it that Mercy is to expected Persons dont perceive every Thing that Passes Within them far less are they capable to give a full distinct Account of every Thing of Such kind - Experiences of Christians are to be brought to the Touchstone of the Infallible Bar & to Stand or fall by it the Bible is not to be brought to their Test & Judgd of by them I own We May Mistake the Sense of Scripture but it is so Obvious in the Passages I have Just Quoted that I Cannot see how it can be Misapprehended.

I cannot say any Thing now About other Remarks I Made on your Book because I have it not to look into I Understand your Mind better by What you have Wrote & if Any Difficulty Shal remain after Comparing your Book & Letter I May come to Propose it to You afterwards

What You Wrote About the Case of Temptation was Very Agreable & I thank you for it. Shal Now State the Case more Plainly because I Want much your further Thoughts upon it ‘tis Precisely this A Person finds himself beset by Evil Angels What if I remember Right Voetius Terms Obsessio & One in that Situation Obsessus they Incessantly break into his Body & Mind Somtimes by Vain at other Seasons by Vile Thoughts Now by the Thoughts of a Business Neglected A Thing Seasonable to be done then by a Scripture Text or an Engaging Thought of Some Spiritual Truth When entrance is not to be had Another Way & by a Variety of other Methods. do All they can Perpetually to Letter[^335-note8] to Mr Edwards Pag 6 Line 13 Tarshish Ch 4,2. [^335-note9] Thus Would rather the Lord Should Want the Honour Would redound to his Name by the Repentance tho’ only outward of the Ninevites And the Whole City Should be Destroy’d one of the largest the Sun Shone upon & the most Populous himself shold lose the Honour & Comfort of being the Instrument of its Preservation than he Should fall under the Imputation of being a False Prophet for Which there Would yet have been no Foundation Horrid Carnality this for as it was Dreadful Selfishness it may in that View be termd Carnality Astonishing Pride thus Filthiness of the Spirit Worse than that of the Flesh And All Circumstances of his Conduct Considerd he was not only in an Unchristian Frame but an Inhuman One and he Sinnd Presumptuously in One of the highest Degrees we may Suppose in Which ‘tis Possible for a Believer so to Act

Pag 7 Lin 10 It is so far from being a Mistaking Gods Method of dealing with Such Persons as You Suggest (Pardon me D Sir) to Say that it is "The Lords Method of delivering his Saints When in a Backsliding &c Condition first to Assure them of their Good Estate And his Favour and so to make that the Means of their Deliverrance" that I give You the Words of the Holy Ghost for it as Express and full as Any Thing Possibly can be. Pag 8 Line 3 Lin to Teize defile & Discourage he is Conscious of the Whole Transaction & finds his Spirit broke by it &c. goes not About to Reason with Satan knows the Inexpediency of this Course is aware Satan wants no better than that he Pray Much & long Against his Temptations & so Won’t Pray himself out of Breath by his Instigation is Convinc’d the Remedy is to get them kept out of Body & Mind Trus[t] in Dependance on the Lord Use of Mechanical or Medical Moral Religious Means for that End because Experience Shews All of them are Expedient Advantageous in their Place but all is in vain no relief for him Relish of Divine Things Wore off the Mind No Comfort it renderd Callous by Cruel Constant Buffetings he Cries but the Lord hears not by What I Understand this is a Just Representation of the Case And Will lead You to the Knowledge of other Circumstances in in it What Would you Advise Such a Person to do how Shal he Recover a Savour of Spiritual Truths And Objects.

I Wonderd you Said Nothing in your Letter about What I Mentiond in Mine respecting Supposd Immediate Revelations of Facts & Future Events as Special Favours Conferrd on Some Special Favourites of Heaven. I give in to your Sentiments on that Nice Point expressd in the three Treatises you have publish’d And greatly like What Mr Brainerd said on this Subject as Mentiond I think by You in the Funeral Sermon on him Which I Perusd with a great deal of Pleasure And Shal Now Mention Some Things Said in Favour of that Principle of Which People are Very Tenacious. That I May have your Answers to them Which Will be a Singular Favour done me for Certain Reasons And Jo 16,13 is Affirmd to be an Express Promise of Such a Thing. tis Urg’d the Thing is Not Contrary to Scripture & therefore May be. tis Argued Jo 13,24--7 is an Example of it an Intimation what the Lord Will do in Such kind When it Pleaseth him till the End of Time. ‘tis Pretended and indeed this is the Strength of their Cause The Thing is a Simple Fact has Nothing to do With the Bible therfore Nothing About it is to be expected in Scripture & Simply to Deny it in All Cases is Daringly to Limit Sovereignty The Lord has Not Said he Will not Grant it and how dare Any Say it Cannot be tis Reasond there are Numbers of Well Attested Instances of the Thing in different Ages & Places Facts are Stubborn Things and to Deny them All is Shocking an Overturning All Moral Evidence. It is insisted on the Thing has been formerly tis Confessd and Why May it Not be Now. We are told a Considerable While before a Thing happend it has been Impressd on the Mind in All its Circumstances Which Exactly happend in every Point if When Askd What one can Say to this he Says perhaps it Was from Satan to this tis answerd does he know Future Contingent Events The Reply is at Hand tis not above him to Figure a Thing on the Fancy long before Which he is resolved by Some Means to bring About but to All this ‘tis Answerd by Advocates for Immediate Revelations Such Reasoning Tends to Sapp one of Main pillar of Evidence of Divinity of the Scriptures Prophecies I have by What I remember given you the Force of the Argument to Establish What What has had I too Well know very bad Effects as Commonly Mannagd in Britain as well as in New England a History of Instances of them Would not Want its Use & Materials for it are not Wanting I Will long Much to See What You Say in Way of Reply to All this. I am Sure you Can’t employ Time better than in framing it. I Should have Mentiond the Authorities of Eminent Divines are brought to bear on them Whose Stomachs Stand at Swallowing down Things like Additions to the Bible Fleming in the Fulfilling of the Scriptures Dr Goodwin &c.[^335-note10] but on this it has been Pleasantly Observd the Authority of the Worthies in the Eleventh of the Hebrews Would have done a Good deal better. I have Some Apprehension this is the Point the Truth in Which the Lord is to Clear up in this Age

I Read Your Humble Attempt &c with much Satisfaction Was Charmd with the Scriptures of the latter Day Glory Sett in one Point of Light Do think Humbly Your Observations on Lowman[^335-note11] have great Strength of Reason. The Killing of the Witnesses as Yet to Come has been to me a Grievous Temptation for Which Reason I perusd with Peculiar Pleasure What you Say on that Subject But if you Answer the Objection it Would Appear the Seventh Trumpet is to Sound soon after the Resurrection of the Witnesses & the Kingdoms of the World &c. but that has Not happened therfore the Witnesses are Not killd if this You Answer I have forgot I Should have Mentiond it Seems Evident the Doctrine of Immediate Revelations must be Simply Denied as Unscriptural & thus Allowd in No Case or must be Allowd in its full Compass and Latitude let the Consequences of it be What they Will for if the Thing is Allowd Possible Reasonings About its Effects Will Not Conclude nor Avail I can See No Mids twixt the two Things. That Principle taken for Granted by Almost All in All Time Past is as I Mentiond in my last Letter to me a Surprizing Thing.

Mr Whitefield Arrivd at Edinburgh Wednesday [--] last & Was to Preach on Thursday Evening but as I am 15 Miles from the City of Which 2 Miles Sea I have not yet heard of the Effects of his Preaching or the Number of the Audiences I Wish they May be as frequent as When he was Last here May Divine Power Specially Attend his Ministrations We Need it Much as we are indeed Generally fallen Under great Deadness I Believe he Will find Use for All his Prudence & Patience in dealing With us for Different Reasons With great Pleasure Friends to Vital Religion & to him Are informd he is to Make No Collections at this Time. I Was glad to hear you Write he Labourd with Success in [^335-note12] New England in rectifying Mistakes he had favourd About Intimations Made by the Lord to his People &c. & Heartily Wish he may be Directed to Apply an Antidote here Where it is Also Needed

I have tird You with a long Epistle & Shal therfore now break off What You Was Pleasd to FavoUr me With Upon the Difficulty Started from Ro 8,28. was very Acceptable & I thank You Much for it I Will expect a Letter from You first Opportunity after this Comes to Hand And in it All the News of New England Particularly Some Account of the State of Religion with You It gives me Pleasure to Think I may Write You my Sentiments on every Thing Without Reserve Please take the Trouble to Make my Affectionate Compliments to my Friend Mr Abercrombie[^335-note13] When You See him or Write to him & tell him I Remember I am in his Debt for a Letter I hope the Ship I am informed of for Carrying this is not saild & therfore twill not be so long in Coming to your Hand after being Writt as my last

Was I Am

## B75. Letter from John Willison, March 17, 1749 B075.J.Willison-JE 3-17-49 edited

John WillisonB075. John Willison to JE, 3/17/49. ANTS, f. 1749, #1.

Dundee March 17 1749

V. Revd & D Br

I thank you for yours of Octer last with your two Sermons wch[^337-note1] Mr McLaÛrin Sent me, wch two Sermons give me cause to Sing of mercy as well as of Judgment, that as one Shining & SÛccesful Youth is laid aside from Labouring in the Gospel, another is Sent forth to it;[^337-note2] Indeed worthy Mr Brainerd was, one among a thousand for carrying the Gospel among the heathen, as appears by the account you give of him in your Sermon, & by his Journals wch have been published here & prefaced by Dr Dodridge & Dedicated by him to the Society at Edr. We must be Silent Seeing he who hath removed him is holy just & wise. We must also lay our hands on our mouths with rpt to the Loss of our great & eminent Such as Dr Watts, Dr Colman, Mr Cowper & others. But O it is no loss to be absent from the body, to them who are present with the Lord. Great need have we to cry to the Lord of the vineyard to Send forth others in their room; It is easy for him to do it, from airths[^337-note3] & places we little expect. These are hopeful & promising accounts wch you have from your Correspondents in Scotland mention’d in your letter, May they all hold true, & be the forerunners of greater things, & the Dawnings of the Glory of the Latter days. I may add to them the Rising of a burning & Shining Light of a Church of England Minr in Dr Doddridge Neighbourhood for he dates his writings from West fflavel near Northampton; he hath lately publishd two vol. of Meditations on all kinds of Subjects,[^337-note4] in a most orthodox, Calvinist & Evangelical Strain, takes all occasions of exalting & Commending his Glorious Master Christ in a most Rhetorical way, & in a Stile I think inimitable, & in the most moving expressions, So that it is not easy to read him without tears, he freely taxes his Brethren of that Church for departing from the Doctrines of grace & of Justification by imputed Righteousness &c. wch were taught by the Reformers & their own Articles & homilies. And notwithstanding of this uncommon freedom he uses wt his Brn, great men &c. Never had any books [^337-note5] Such a Run in England as his, for in a year & an half's time there are five Editions of ym published at London, & Still ar greedily bought & read especially by persons of distinction; the stile being a little too high & poetical for the vulgar. His name is James Hervey A.B. Some Say he is of noble descent from the Earl of Bristol but I am not Sure of this. It is thought he is the man that Dr Doddridge points at in the Life of Coll Gardiner page 37. 38.[^337-note6] It looks well that So many in England Should become fond of Evangelical writings. –-- No doubt the books may be got to Boston by this time. Let us therefore Still wait & pray in hope. -- I should be glad to do any thing in my power for promoting the Concert for united prayer, And O that it were Spread both far & Near, it would be a token of a general Revival of Religion to be fast approaching. I know nothing that hath a greater tendency to promote the forsd happy Concert than the Book you lately published about it[^337-note7] (a copy whereof you Sent me for wch I humbly thank you) I wish it were universally Spread, for I both Love & admire the performance upon Subts So uncommon. -- I approve your Remarks on Mr Lowman.[^337-note8] His reason for beginning Antichrists reign So late as the year 756 is weak, viz. because then King Pepin invested the pope in his temporal dominion over that province in Italy called St peters patrimony -- when it is evident that the pope had usurped his tyrannical Dominion over Christs Church long before, wch is the main ground of his being called Antichrist; yea the popes usurped power was greater before K. pepins time than it is at this day, as for instance in pope Symmachus time anno 501. In pope Hormisda’s time anno 516 - In Pope Boniface 3d's time anno 606. In pope Constantines time anno 713. Yea Mr Lowman himself gives a dreadful instance of the [^337-note9] popes tyranny & usurpation both over the Church & the Emperor in page 97 of his book, wch happened anno 726 thirty years before he begins Antichrists reign, wn pope Gregory 2d Excommunicated the Emperor Leo for ordering Images to be removed out of the Churches, & forbad obedience or paying of taxes to him. Was not Antichrists Reign far advanced by that time? And we have Several Instances of the popes tyranny Similar to this recorded by Historians long before that Mr Lowman mentions, wch more directly denominat him Antichrist than his temporal doins[^337-note10] in Italy. We See how easy it is for the best of writers to Slip into mistakes & wrong Schemes. I agree wt you that Antichrists fall will be gradual in the way you explain it.

I am sorry to hear of Arminianism's growing in N. England. But I rejoice to hear of Gov. Belchers Zeal for Religion in New Jersey. May the Lord Spare him & bless him. As also I am glad to hear of the hopeful prospect of the Gospels getting ground among the Six Nations of Indians; & of Such a youth as Mr Spencer[^337-note11] being Sent among them; may the Lord prosper him as he did Mr Brainerd.

I Sympathize wt you under that affliction of your Daughters death but it's comfortable She was helped So to live And die, as to afford Such grounds of hope concerning her. And tho’ She was the fflower of your family, yet the Remembring of the Gracious hand that puled the fflower will engage your worthy Spouse & you to a becoming Silence, like Aaron. As he will do what he will, let us join & Say always, Let his will be done. - I would fain be at this in my own case, May the Lord help me to more Christian Submission & Resignation. I am now entered into the 69th year of my age & fallen under Severall[^337-note12] distresses whereby I have been Shaken over the grave these many months past & am laid aside from preaching. May the Lord assist me in my preparation for the dissolution of this tabernacle. I find it no easy matter to die & to die in faith & to die like Simeon with Jesus in my Arms. I very much need your prayers for me I am glad to hear D B that your parents are both alive, & that they hold the abilities of both body & mind So remarkably at So great an age, and partic. that your ffather at 79 years of Age performs the whole of his Ministerial work So constantly, without feeling it burdensom, & was able to travel 40 miles to See you; He is indeed a wonder of his Age, & would be reckoned So in this countrie where few Minrs come near to that Age & vigour. May the Lord Still Spare him with your Mother & make them Still flourishing in old Age, May they be blessed with much of Gods gracious presence; & with the Consolations & fruits of the Spirit in their aged & declining days. I Still kindly Remember your worthy Spouse & children remaining, & pray they may long be continued for Comforts to you, & you continued for a Blessing to them, to your flock & to many others as you already have been. I remain

R & D B Your most affect. B & Servt in Our Lord Jo Willison

P.S. The Revd Mr Whitefield came to Scotland in Septer last, & preached about 2 months in & about Edinburgh & Glasgow. But some Brethren who employed him, being challenged for it in Synods & presbyry, & debates arising thereupon, Mr Whitefield returned to London. To give a view of the Substance of these Debates, And what passed thereupon in the Synod of Glasgow, I have Sent you herewith a printed pamphlet containing the Same, with two othr books as a Small acknowledgement of your favours.

March. 17. 49[^337-note13] To the Revd Mr Edwards

[^337-note1]: Throughout the letter, Willison uses archaic ligatures for “wh” and “th.”

[^337-note2]: From Willison’s subsequent description, JE had sent his funeral sermon for Brainerd, *True Saints, When Absent from the Body, Are Present with the Lord* (1747), and an ordination sermon, possibly the one for Samuel Buel, *The Church’s Marriage to Her Sons* (1746).

[^337-note3]: I.e. a point from heaven or quarter of the compass; a direction.

[^337-note4]: James Hervey, *Meditations among the Tombs* (London 1746); Willison refers to the 2nd edition, *Meditations and Contemplations* (2 vols., London, 1748). JE notes in his “Catalogue” that Erskine had recommended this work in his letter of Feb. 14, 1749 (no longer extant).

[^337-note5]: **marginal.** [2]

[^337-note6]: Philip Doddridge, *Some Remarkable Passages In The Life Of Colonel James Gardiner Who Was Slain At The Battle Of Preston* (3rd ed., 1748).

[^337-note7]: I.e. *An Humble Attempt.*

[^337-note8]: I.e. Moses Lowman (1680-1752), whose *Paraphrase and Notes on the Revelation* (London, 1737) was used by JE extensively in the *Humble Attempt.*

[^337-note9]: **marginal.** [3]

[^337-note10]: I.e. dominions.

[^337-note11]: Elihu Spencer.

[^337-note12]: **marginal.** [4]

[^337-note13]: Dated by JE.
