## B78. Letter from Thomas Foxcroft, June 26, 1749 B078.TFoxcroft-JE 6-26-49 edited

Thomas FoxcroftB078. Thomas Foxcroft to JE, 6/26/49. Printed as separately paginated appendix to *Humble Inquiry* (Boston, 1749), pp. 1-16.

An APPENDIX BEING

A Letter to the *Author*, in Answer to his Request of Information concerning the Opinion of *Protestant* Divines and Churches in general, of the Presbyterians in *Scotland* and Dissenters in *England* in particular, respecting *five* QUESTIONS that relate to this Controversy.

*Rev. and dear* SIR, IF you look into Mr. Baxter's Controversial Writings against Mr. Blake, you will meet with such Accounts of Principles and Facts, as I think, may reasonably give an Inquirer much Satisfaction as to the common Judgment of Protestant Churches and Divines in the Points you mention. I particularly refer you to his *Five*Disputations*of Right to Sacraments, and the true Nature of visible Christianity*.[^340-note1] Where all or the most of your *Queries* are consider’d and answer’d, with a Multitude of *Testimonies* produced in favour of Sentiments contrary to those of your excellent Predecessor, the late Mr. Stoddard.- I have not said this from any Disposition to excuse my self from the Labour of making some further Inquiry, if it be thought needful. And as it may shew my Willingness to gratify your Desire, I will now say something on your *Questions* distinctly, but with as much Brevity as I can.

Quest. I. *What is the general Opinion respecting that* Self-Examination *requir’d in* I Cor. xi. 28. *Whether Communicants are not here* *directed to examine themselves concerning the* Truth of Grace, *or their real Godliness?*

Answ. This Construction of the Text, as far as I have had Opportunity to inquire, appears to me very generally receiv’d: if I may judge by what many celebrated *Expositors* have said, on the Place, and by what many famous Divines have written in Treatises of *Preparation* for the Lord's Supper, besides what is contain’d in public *Confessions, Catechisms*, *Directories*, &c. - I think, Dr. Reynolds, in his *Meditations on the Lord's Supper*,[^340-note2] has summarily express’d the common Judgment of *Calvinists* in these strong Lines of his. "The *Sacrament* is but a *Seal* of the *Covenant*; and the Covenant essentially includes *Conditions*; and the Condition on our Part is *Faith*. No Faith, no *Covenant*; no Covenant, no *Seal*; no Seal, no *Sacrament*.- The *Matter* then of this [^340-note3] *Trial* (says he) must be that *Vital Qualification*, which predisposeth a Man for receiving of these holy Mysteries; and that is *Faith*."

However, I may venture to be confident, that Mr. Stoddard's Gloss on the Text, who tells us in his controverted *Sermon*, "The Meaning is, that a Man must *come solemnly* to that Ordinance, *examining* *what* Need *he has of it*," is quite foreign from the current Sense of *Calvinist* Writers. And tho’ he makes a different Comment in his *Appeal to the Learned*, saying, "The *Examination* call’d for is, whether they *understood the Nature* of the Ordinance, that so they may *solemnly* *consider what they have to do* when they wait upon God in it,"[^340-note4] neither can I find any Appearance of a general Consent of the Learned and Orthodox to this *new Gloss*, at least as exhibiting the full Meaning of the Text. I might easily confront it with numerous Authorities. But the *Palatine* Catechism,[^340-note5] and that of the *Westminster-Assembly*, with the common Explanations & Catechizings upon them, may be appeal’d to as *Instar Omnium*. And I shall only add here, if it be allow’d a just Expectation that the *Candidate* for the Communion *examine himself* about the *same* Things at least as the *Pastor*, to whom he applies for Admission, ought to make the Subject of his Examination, then it's worth while to hear the Opinion of those un-named *Ministers* in New England (among whom the late Dr. Colman, I have Reason to think, was the principal Hand) that answer’d Dr. Mather's *Order of the Gospel* (Anno 1700) who in the *Postscript* to their Review thus express themselves: "*We highly* approve--that the Proponant for the Lord's Table be *examined* of his baptismal Vow; *his Sense* of spiritual Wants, Sinfulness and Wretchedness; *his Hope, Faith, Experiences*, Resolutions thro’ the Grace of God."[^340-note6] This, I think, is something beyond Mr. Stoddard.

Quest. II. *Whether it be the general Opinion of those aforesaid, that some who know themselves to be* unregenerate *and under the reigning Power of Sin*, ought *notwithstanding, in such a State, to come to the Lord's Table?*

ANSW. I am aware, Sir, tho’ you have seen fit to take no Notice of it to me, that Mr. Stoddard (in his *Doctrine of instituted Churches*) is peremptory in the *Affirmative:* but I have met with no Author among *Calvinists*, at home or abroad, consenting with him, unless it be Mr. *Blake*, and some that were for a promiscuous Admission, with little or no Limitation. If Divines in general, of the *Calvinist* Character, were for such a Latitude as Mr. *Stoddard's*, what can we suppose to be the Reason, that in treating on the *Lord's Supper* they so constantly consider it as one of the *Rights of the Church, belonging to the truly Faithful alone, exclusively of all others?* Why do we hear them declaring, *It is certain that the Right of external Fellowship resides in the Faithful only: and as to the rest, they are in that Communion only by Accident, and it's also only by Accident that they are suffered there*; *but being what they are, they have not any Part in the* [^340-note7] *Rights of that Society properly belonging to them?* If they tho’t the Sacrament instituted for *Conversion*, why do we never find them recommending it as a *converting* Ordinance, and urging Persons to come to it with that View, who *know* themselves to be in an *unconverted State?* If they tho’t that any such have a *Right before God*, and may come to it *with a good Conscience*, why do we find them so solemnly *warning* all that are truly *convinced* of their remaining yet in a *natural* State, to *refrain* coming to the Lord's Table in their Unbelief and Impenitence; as if they judg’d it a *sinful* and *dangerous* Thing for them to come under such Circumstances? I know, Mr. Stoddard in his *Appeal* disputes the *Fact:* but it has occurr’d to me in Abundance of instances, while reviewing my Authors on this Occasion.

Among the foreign Protestants, in *Germany, France*, &c. I shall name but two out of many Instances before me. The *Heidelbergh* or *Palatine* Catechism, which had the solemn Approbation of the Synod of *Dort*, and was especially praised by the Divines of *Great Britain*; which has been in a Manner universally receiv’d and taught, formerly in *Scotland* and still all over *Holland*, and by Reason of it’s Excellency has been translated into no less than *thirteen* several Languages; this is most express in claiming the *Lord's Supper* for a special Privilege of such as have *true Faith* & *Repentance*; and forbidding it to *Hypocrites*, as well as scandalous Persons, declaring that none such ought to come. See the *eighty first* and other Questions and Answers,[^340-note8] with Ursin's Latin *Explications* and De Witte's English *Catechizings* thereon.[^340-note9] Here, Sir, indeed you have the Judgment of a Multitude in One.- Another celebrated Book is Claude's *Historical Defence of the Reformation*;[^340-note10] in which I meet with repeated Declarations of the same Sentiments, perfectly on the *Negative* Side of the Question in Hand; but I think, too many and too long, to be here transcribed. The Language of some of 'em I have just now had Occasion to make use of.

As for the Church of Scotland, I find, they have adopted the *Westminster*-Confession, Catechisms and Directory, which debar all *ignorant* and *ungodly* Persons from the Lord's Table, and require every one to *examine* himself, not only as to his Knowledge, but also his *Faith, Repentance, Love, new Obedience*, &c.-- In their *Books of Discipline*, I observe sundry Passages that appropriate the Sacrament to the *truly Penitent and Faithful*, as the only proper Subjects. Their *National Covenant*, renew’d from Time to Time, has this Clause: To the which [true Reformed Kirk) we join our selves willingly, in Doctrine, Faith, Religion, Discipline, and Use of the holy Sacraments,*as lively Members* of the same*in Christ*our Head, &c.[^340-note11] And among the *Divines* of Scotland, I find many in their Sermons, Sacramental Speeches, and other Discourses, declaring themselves strongly on the *Negative* Part in the[^340-note12] Question before us, advising to Strictness in Admissions to the Lord's Supper, renouncing the Opinion of it’s being a *converting Ordinance*, inviting only the sincere Friends of Christ to it, and frequently *warning* Professors conscious of reigning Sin and Hypocrisy to forbear approaching the Lord's Table. I might bring much to this Purpose from Mr. Andrew Gray's Book of Sermons published *Anno* 1716. and his Sermons printed *Anno* 1746. with a Preface by Mr. Willison.[^340-note13] -So from Mr. Ebenezer Erskine's Synodical Sermon, *Anno* 1732.[^340-note14] --And from Mr. Ralph Erskine's Sermon on *Isai*. xlii. 6. and his Discourse at Fencing the Tables, annexed to his Sermon on *Joh*. xvi. 15.[^340-note15] -So from Mr. Willison's Synodical Sermon *Anno* 1733. where he sets down a Variety of searching Questions (no less than 27) which he advises to be put to Proponants, and their Answers to be waited for, before they are admitted.[^340-note16] - The anonymous Author of *a* *Defence of National Churches against the Independents* (who is reputed to be Mr. Willison) asserts it as a Presbyterian Principle, that none have *Right before God* to the compleat Communion of the Church, but such as have *Grace*; and that none are to be admitted but those who are *Saints*, at least in Profession; such as profess to accept of the Offers of Christ's Grace &c. and confess themselves to be *sincere*.[^340-note17] Mr. Aytone, in his *Review* against Mr. Glas, owns that the Lord's Supper is not a formal Mean of *Conversion*, but of further Growth & Nourishment to those *already* converted.[^340-note18] -In the same Strain is Mr. Naismith's *Treatise of the Entail of the Covenant*.[^340-note19] - And Mr. Warden's *Essay on Baptism*.[^340-note20] - In a Word, I find Mr. Currie (in his Synodical Sermon, *Anno* 1732.) testifying of the Ministers in *Scotland*, that they are *tender* (i.e. circumspect and cautious) *in admitting People to the holy Table of the Lord*; knowing, the *Design* of the Ordinance is *not Conversion*, but *Confirmation:* and he observes, that all who approve themselves to God here, will a thousand times rather chuse to have, was it but *one Table* or *half* a Table of honest Communicants, *true* *Believers* and *real Saints*, than have a *hundred* Tables, by admitting any that are *unworthy* (or *Christless* Souls, as he anon characterises them) of whom there are not moral Evidences of their *Fitness* for this holy Ordinance. And for the commendable Practice of the Church of *Scotland* in being *pointed* and *particular* in *debarring* the Unworthy from this Ordinance (says he) God forbid ever it turn into Desuetude.[^340-note21] - I think, I may here not unfitly subjoin those remarkable Passages in Mr. Anderson's excellent *Defence of the Presbyterians*, against Mr. *Rhind*: where he informs us, *They look upon this holy Ordinance as the common Privilege of the Faithful*; and therefore they usually fence the Lord's Table, in the Words of Scripture, I Cor. vi. 9. or some such like -To exclude the *Impenitent* from the *Privilege* of Gospel-Mysteries; to debar those from the *Lord's Table*, whom the Lord has, by the express Sentence [^340-note22] of his Word, debarred out of the *Kingdom of Heaven*, is what every one, who is not quite lost in Impiety, must own to be not only *lawful*, but a *Duty*.[^340-note23] - Upon which I beg Leave to observe, according to this Principle I do not see but that a Man who with apparent Signs of Credibility *confesses* himself habitually impenitent, ought to be debarred from the Lord's Table: And surely, by Parity of Reason, he that *knows* himself to be unregenerate, ought to *refrain* coming, since there can be no true Repentance without Regeneration. I think, we have no just Grounds to suppose, Mr. Stoddard's Principle in this Matter has hitherto any

general Prevalence in the Church of *Scotland*.

And now to pass over to *England*, neither do I find Reason to think the *Dissenters* there in general are for Mr. Stoddard's Latitude. The *Assembly of Divines* pronounce all the *Ungodly*, as well as Ignorant, *unworthy* of the Lord's Table; direct to *Preparation* for it, by examining our selves of our *being in Christ* &c. And tho’ they declare this Sacrament appointed for the Relief even of the *weak* and *doubting* Christian, who *unfeignedly* desires to be *found in Christ*; and having directed *such* a one to bewail his Unbelief and labour to have his Doubts resolved, they assert that *so doing* he may and ought to come to the Lord's Supper, to be *further* *strengthned*: yet I don't find any Appearance of a Hint, as if others who *know* themselves to be in a natural State, or are conscious of their being certainly graceless, may and ought to come to this Ordinance, that they may be *converted*. Nay, they expressly declare of ALL *ungodly* Persons, that while they remain such, they *cannot* without *great* Sin against Christ partake of those holy Mysteries.[^340-note24] - As to particular Divines, I find Multitudes of 'em among the Dissenters, in later as well as former Times, expressing the same Sentiments: distinguishing between natural and instituted Duties, between initial and confirming Means, between special Ordinances and common: and declaring the Lord's Supper a *Disciple-Privilege*, peculiar to such as have *Disciple-Properties*, and admonishing as well the *close Hypocrite*, as the more gross, of the *Sin and Danger* of coming to it in his unregenerate State, impenitent and unbelieving. Thus, Mr. Bolton, in his Discourse on *the Wedding-Supper* *and the Wedding-Garment*, warns the *graceless* not to come to the Lord's Supper; affirming, that an *unsanctify’d Presence* will be found as bad as a *profane Absence*. - Mr. Baxter, in his *five Disputations*, has much that runs in the same Strain; so in his *Reformed Liturgy*, and in his *Christian Concord*, where we have his Brethren joining their Testimony with his. - Likewise Mr. Charnock, in his Discourse of*the Subjects of the Lord's Supper*. - Mr. Palmer, in his *Scripture-Rail to the Lord's Table*. - Mr. Saunders in his *Anti-Diatribe. -*Mr. Langley, in his *Suspension Review’d*. - Mr. Doolittle, Mr. Henry, Dr. Earle, & others, in their Books on the Lord's Supper.- Mr. Shower, in his *Sacramental*[^340-note25] *Discourses*.- Mr. Flavel, in his Sermon on *Gospel-Unity*, and other Pieces.- Mr. Philip Henry, and Mr. Trosse, in the Accounts of their *Lives*.- Dr. Calamy in his Discourse on *Vows*, and his *Defence of Nonconformity*.- Mr. Simon Browne, in the Continuation of *Henry's* Expos. on I Cor. xi. 28.-Dr. Harris, in his Discourse on *Self-Examination.-*Dr. Jennings, in his Sermons to*young People*.[^340-note26] --I could, from all these Authors, cite Passages much to the Purpose: But it wou’d be too tedious. Yet I will give you a few Hints from some others-Dr. Williams, in his *Gospel-Truth stated*, says, Tho’ a Man had it reveal’d to him that he is one of the *Elect*, yet so long as he remains *unregenerate*, he has no Right to partake of the Lord's Supper.[^340-note27] - Dr. Guyse, in his late Sermon at Mr. *Gibbon*'s Ordination observes, that Men's being *Church-Members* supposes them *already* to have a *good Work begun* in them, and to be Partakers of Christian *Love*, even such as proceeds from *Faith*, in a prevailing Degree; and Persons (says he) that have nothing of this, *ought not* to be Church-Members.- Mr. Hall, in his *Exhortation* on the same Occasion, remarks, that the Seals of the Covenant are to be used as *discriminating* Signs of the real Separation of true Believers from the World; and urges to have the Fence kept up, which Christ has set about his Church, that it may appear to be a Body wholly *distinct* from the World: God's House being erected for the Entertainment, not of *Hypocrites* and dead Sinners, but of the Living in *Jerusalem*.[^340-note28] - But, says Dr. Watts, in his *Humble Attempt*, ‘tis true, this can't be practised universally and perfectly here on Earth, so as to prevent some *secret* Sinners making their Way into our separate Congregations, and joining with us in the most solemn Ordinances; yet he declares such *not really worthy* of any Room or Place in the House of God.- And in his *Holiness of Times, Places, & People*, the Dr. observes, The *visible* Christian Church is founded on a *Supposition*, that the Members of it are, or should appear to be, Members of the *invisible*: And *none* (says he) are to be admitted into this *visible* Church or esteem’d compleat Members of it, but those who make such a Declaration and Profession of their Faith in Christ and their avow’d Subjection to him, as may be suppos’d in a Judgment of Charity to manifest them to be real Believers, true Subjects of his spiritual Kingdom, and Members of the *invisible* Church.[^340-note29] - I find Dr. Doddridge in the same Sentiments, by what he says in his *Family-Expositor*. Thus, on the Case of *Ananias* & *Sapphira*, he has this Note, The *Church* is never *happier*, than when the *Sons of Falshood* are *deterred* from intruding into it: If it’s *Members* are *less numerous*, 'tis a sufficient Balance, that it is *more pure*. And on *Simon's* Case, he pronounces it to be *in vain* for Men to *profess* themselves *Christians*, in vain to submit to *Baptism*, &c. if their *Heart* be not *right with God*. And *such Persons* being admitted to *distinguishing* Ordinances, he calls an Evil, in the present State of [^340-note30] Things unavoidable: wishing for the *happy Medium*, between *prostituting divine Ordinances* by a foolish Credulity, and *defrauding* *the Children of the Houshold of their Bread*, by a rigorous Severity and mistaken Caution. He every where represents the Lord's Supper as the Sacrament of *Nutrition*, a reviving and nourishing Ordinance; but never that I can find, as a *regenerating* or *converting* one. Upon the Case of *Judas*, the Dr. observes, that if he had truly stated the Order of the Story, then *Judas* certainly *went out* before the *Eucharist* was instituted: And indeed one cannot reasonably suppose, Christ would have commanded him to *drink of this Cup* as the *Blood shed for* him *for the Remission of Sins*, when he had just before been declaring, in Effect, that *his* Sins should *never* be forgiven.- By which Observation, I think, Dr. Doddridge has quite demolish’d one of the most plausible Pleas in Favour of the secret and conscious Hypocrite's Claim to the Lord's Supper.[^340-note31]

In fine, even those who appear Advocates for a Latitude in Admissions to the Communion, I observe, generally in the Course of the Argument offer such *Distinctions* or make such *Concessions*, as seem by fair Consequence a giving up the Point, at least as stated in the present Question. For they usually distinguish between a Right *in foro Dei* and *in foro Ecclesiæ*; accordingly treat these as two different Questions, *Who ought to come?* and, *Who ought to be admitted?* considering the latter as an *Ecclesiastical*Case, and here they assert a *Latitude*; but the former, as a Case of *Conscience*, of private Reference only, and here they grant a *Limitation*. How large soever their Principles, while taking the Case in it’s *Ecclesiastical* View, yet I have met with very few Divines, that taking it as a *private Case of Conscience*, have gone Mr. Stoddard's Length, in asserting, that *some unsanctified Men have Right before God to the Lord's Supper*, and *may come with a good Conscience*, yea, *ought to come*, notwithstanding they *know* themselves at the same Time to be in a *natural* Condition. This he declares in his *Doctrine of instituted Churches*, and confirms in his *Sermon* & *Appeal*. But then he has made some *Concessions*, which seem to be subversive of his Opinion. For he expressly allows, that the *Sacrament* by Institution supposes Communicants to be *visible Saints*; and this Title of *visible Saints* he assigns to "such as have a visible Union to Christ, "such as are in the Judgment of rational Charity Believers, "such as carry themselves so that there is Reason to look upon them to be Saints."[^340-note32] Now, taking the Case as a *private Case of Conscience* (in which Light only Mr. Stoddard professes to have design’d to consider it in his Sermon, and not at all as an *Ecclesiastical* Case) I think, this *Visibility* *of Saintship* immediately respects the *Proponant* for the Lord's Table, & must be refer’d to his own *private Judgment* of himself. But then, how can there be a *Visibility of Saintship* in the Eye of the Man's own conscience, when at the

same Time he *knows* himself to be in a *natural* Condition! Or how can [^340-note33] a Man come to the Lord's Table with a *good Conscience*, as having *Right before God*, while he cannot form so much as a Judgment of *rational Charity* for himself; seeing he carry’s so, in the View of his own *Conscience*, that he has no *Reason* to look on himself to be a *Saint*, nay, even *knows* he is still in a natural State, and therefore in the Eye of his own impartial Judgment is not such a one as the *Sacrament* by Institution *supposes* the Communicant to be! -- Moreover, Mr. Stoddard in describing visible Saints, inserts into their Character *a serious Profession of the true Religion*, which he sometimes calls *a Profession of Faith and Repentance, morally sincere*:[^340-note34] and in his *Doctrine of instituted Churches* (pag. 19) he lays down

a remarkable *Position*, in these Words, SUCH A PROFESSION AS BEING SINCERE MAKES A MAN A REAL SAINT, BEING MORALLY SINCERE MAKES A MAN A VISIBLE SAINT.

Now according to this, it seems to me, the *Profession* it self, whether evangelically or morally sincere, is always of a *uniform Tenor*; having one and the same Thing for the *Matter* of it; and not respecting, in the different Cases, a Religion *specifically* different, or a Faith and Repentance of a higher & a lower *Kind*. -- But then it's quite beyond me to comprehend, how a Man who *knows* himself to be in a *natural* Condition, can be so much as *morally* sincere in his *Profession*, while it is in it’s Matter and Tenor *such a Profession as being* (evangelically) *sincere makes a Man a Real Saint*. For if he *knows* himself to be in a *natural* Condition, he then as certainly *knows* he hath not (in the Principle or Exercise) that *Faith and Repentance*, which is the just Matter of *such a Profession*: And how therefore can he be reasonably supposed, with any Degree of *moral Sincerity* to make *such a Profession*, when for the Matter of it 'tis the very *same* Profession he would make, if he *knew* himself to be a *real Saint!* Can a Person in any sound Gospel-Sense profess himself a *Saint* or *believing Penitent*, and herein *speak the Truth* with a common *moral Honesty*, while yet he *knows* himself to be destitute of all such *Characters* in the Sight of God and Conscience, being still in a *natural* Condition and under the Dominion of *Unbelief* and *Impenitence!* For my own Part, I must confess this a Difficulty in Mr. Stoddard's Scheme, that I am not capable of solving. His Favourite-Hypothesis, I think, must fall, if his *Position* stands, and his *Concessions* be abode by; which serve clearly to determine the present *Question* in the *Negative*, agreable to the general Sense of Protestant Churches and Divines.

Quest. III. *Whether it not be the general Opinion, that Persons admitted to* *the Lord's Table ought to* profess saving Faith and Repentance; *meaning that Faith and Repentance, which are the Terms of the* Covenant of Grace!

Answ. I believe, after what has been already offer’d, we need be at [^340-note35] no Loss to know the Mind of the Generality respecting the Subject of this Inquiry. Were there Occasion for it, I could easily produce a *Cloud of Witnesses*, to evidence that the general Opinion is on the *Affirmative* Side, in this Question. Repeated Searches have been made by diligent and impartial Inquirers, who tho’ of varying Judgment and Practice in Church-Discipline, yet agree in their Reports: And from them I will give you the following Attestations.

Mr. Lob (in his *True Dissenter*) tells us, It is the Judgment of all the *Nonconformists*, that nothing less than the *Profession* of *saving Faith* credibly significant of the Thing professed, gives Right to Church-Communion. And this he declares to be the Rule of *all Protestants* in general. He brings even Mr. Humphrey (tho’ opposite in Judgment) for his Voucher: Who acknowledges, That the *visible Church* is defined by a *Profession* of true regenerate Faith, and of no less than that, according to the most *general* Opinion of *Protestant Divines*. He speaks of it as the *common Opinion*, that a Profession of no less than true Grace or justifying Faith is the *Rule of Admission* to the Church-Sacraments. And tho’ Mr. *Humphrey* went off from the received Opinion, yet could he not come into Mr. *Blake*'s Notions in this Matter, who also had gone off from it, nor hope for their Vindication: Hence he makes that Challenge, *What Man is there,* *that dares revive Mr.* Blake's *Cause, and defend it against Mr.* Baxter's Right *to Sacraments!*[^340-note36]

Mr. Baxter in this his Book very copiously argues for a *Profession* of *saving Faith*, as the Rule of Admission to Sacraments, and much insists on it’s being so by the unanimous Consent of judicious Divines. He tells us, Mr. Gataker in his Books has largely prov’d this by a Multitude of Quotations from Protestant Writers. And he adds his own Testimony, repeatedly saying, It is indeed their *most common* Doctrine- It is the *common Protestant* Doctrine-And again, Certain I am, this is the *common* Doctrine of Reformed Divines-He subjoins, I must profess, that I don't know of *any one Protestant* Divine, reputed Orthodox, of the contrary Judgment, before Dr. *Ward* and Mr. *Blake*, tho’ some Papists and Arminians I knew of that Mind.- And again (beside Sir *Henry Vane*) he says, *All* that I know of, since Dr. *Ward*, is Mr. *Blake*, Mr. *Humphrey*, and one *John Timson*; and *John Timson*, Mr. *Humphrey*, and Mr. *Blake*.- He alledges Mr. Vines, as thus Witnessing in the Case on his Side.[^340-note37] To this Purpose *all our learned Divines* have given their Suffrage: I need not number Authors or Churches. It is so plain a Case, that I wonder, those (of the contrary Opinion) have not taken Notice of it, *there is an Army to a Man against them*.

Mr. Langley, in his *Suspension review’d*, observes; The *concurrent Judgment* of Divines, English and Foreign, Episcopal and Presbyterian, that Man of vast and digested Reading, the Learned Mr. Baxter hath demonstrated at large in Sixty *Testimonies*; sundry of which have *many* [^340-note38] in them, being the Judgment of many *Churches* and many *learned* Men therein; & more might easily be bro’t.-In short, He calls it the *old Protestant* Doctrine asserted against the *Papists*; & wonders at the Confidence of the Men, who tell us, against our own Eyes, that it is a *Novelism*.[^340-note39]

To these Attestations I subjoin that of our Mr. Mitchel (in his Introduction before the *Defence of the Synod*, 1662) who while asserting a different Latitude of the two Sacraments, yet pleads for Strictness in Admissions to the Lord's Table; and testify’s, It is most evident, that *godly reforming Divines* have in their Doctrine *unanimously* taught, and in their Practice (many of them) endeavour’d, a *strict Selection* of those who should be admitted to the *Lord's Supper*.[^340-note40] - I think, it may be not improperly observ’d here, that in a Manuscript, drawn up by this eminent Person for his own Satisfaction, and inserted in the Account of his Life, he has left his solemn Testimony against a lax *Mode of Profession* (exclusive of all Examinations and Confessions, of a practical and experimental Nature) as having been found by plentiful Experience a *Nurse* of *Formality* and *Irreligion*. At the same Time declaring his Judgment, with a particular Eye to the Churches of *New England*, That the *Power of Godliness* will be *lost*, if only *doctrinal*Knowledge & *outward* Behaviour come to be accounted sufficient for a Title to all Church-Privileges; and the use of *practical Confessions* and *Examinations* of Men's *spiritual* Estate be laid aside. For (says he) that which People see to be publicly required and held in Reputation, *That* will they look after, and usually *no more*.[^340-note41] - In another Place he observes, This will not only lose the Power of Godliness, but in a little Time bring in *Profaneness*, and *ruin* *the Churches*, these two Ways. (1) *Election of Ministers* will soon be carry’d by a formal looser Sort. (2) The Exercise of *Discipline* will, by this Means, be impossible. And Discipline falling, Profaneness riseth like a Flood.[^340-note42] - Agreably he says elsewhere; Certain it is, that we stand for the *Purity* of the Churches, when we stand for *such Qualifications* as we do, in those whom we would admit to *full Communion*; and do withstand those Notions and Reasonings that would infer a *Laxness* therein, which hath apparent *Peril* in it.--In Sum (says he) we make Account, that we shall be near about the *Middle-Way* of Church-Reformation, if we keep *Baptism* within the Compass of the *Non-excommunicable*, and the *Lord's Supper* within the Compass of those that have (unto Charity) somewhat of the *Power* of Godliness, or Grace in *Exercise*.[^340-note43] -- For, Mr. Mitchel as he thought *Faith in the special and lively* Exercise *thereof*necessary to a safe and comfortable Participation of the *Lord's Supper*, so he judged an *Appearance* of this unto rational Charity, judging by *positive sensible* Signs and Evidences, justly requir’d in order to Admission into *full Communion*. Whereas, he thought *Baptism* annexed to *initial* Faith, or Faith in the *Being* of it; the charitable Judgment whereof (says he) runs upon a great *Latitude*; and he conceiv’d the same *Strictness*, as to outward [^340-note44] Signs, not necessary unto a charitable probable Judgment or Hope of the *Being* of Faith, which entitles to Baptism, as of that *Growth* & *special Exercise* of Faith, which is requisite to the Lord's Supper.[^340-note45] These are the main *Distinctions*, on which he grounded his Opinion of a *different* Latitude of the two Sacraments.--For, I must observe, as strenuously as he pleads for a various Extent, as to the Subjects of them, he never supposes any Adult regularly admittable to either Sacrament, but such as in Ecclesiastical Reputation sustain the Character of *Believers*; such as in the Account of a rational Charity (judging by probable Signs) have the Being of *Regeneration*; or as he variously expresses it, have *true Faith*, in the Judgment of Charity; and do in *some Measure* perform the Duties of Faith and Obedience, as to *Church-Visibility* and *charitable Hope*; and therefore are such as the Church ought to receive and hold as *Heirs of the Grace of Life*, according to the Rules of Christian Charity.- Tho’ it seems, as Mr. Shepard before him speaks of his *Church Charity* and *Experimental Charity*; so Mr. Mitchel had his *Positive* Charity and his *Negative*, and conducted his Judgment & Administrations accordingly, in admitting Persons to the one Sacrament or the other.-I should not have been so prolix and particular here, but that I tho’t it might serve to prepare the Way for a more easy, short, and intelligible Answer to your remaining Queries.

Quest. IV. *Whether it be the general Opinion of Protestant Churches and Divines, in the Case of* adult *Persons, that the* Terms *of Admission to* both *Sacraments are the* same?

Answ. I presume, Sir, the Question do’s not respect a Sameness in the *Degree* of Qualifications, Experiences, and Evidences; but only a Sameness in *Kind*, or for the Substance and general Nature of Things. I suppose, you had no View here to any such critical *Distinction* as that beforementioned, between an *initial* Faith and a *grown* Faith; or between the simple *Being* of Faith, which intitleth to Baptism, and the *special Exercise* of Faith, which fits for the Lord's Supper; nor aim at a nice Adjustment of the several *Characters of Visibility*, or *Motives of Credibility*, in the one Case and the other: but only intend in general to inquire, whether Persons admittable to one or other Sacrament, ought to profess *true justifying Faith*, and not be admitted on the Profession of any Faith of a Kind *inferior* and *specifically* different. Now, taking this to be the Scope of your Question, I have good Reason to apprehend, that the *Generality* of Protestant Churches and Divines, of the *Calvinistic* Persuasion especially, have declared themselves for the *Affirmative*.

I think, all that hold, the *visible* Christian Church ought to consist of such as make a *visible and credible Profession of Faith and Holiness*, and *appear to rational Charity real Members of the Church invisible* (which is the common Language of Protestants) are to be understood as in Principle exploding the Conceit of a conscious Unbeliever's Right before God to special Church-Ordinances, and as denying the apparent Unbeliever's [^340-note46] Right before the Church to Admission, whether to one Sacrament or the other. I observe, *Eadem est Ratio utriusque Sacramenti*,[^340-note47] is a Maxim (in it’s general Notion) espoused by the several contending Parties in this Controversy about a Right to Sacraments.

That a credible Profession of saving Faith and Repentance is necessary to *Baptism*, in the Case of the Adult, I can shew, by the Authority of Claude's approv’d *Defence of the Reformation*, to be the general Opinion of *French* Protestants; and by the Palatine Catechism, by the Leyden Professors *Synopsis*,[^340-note48] &c. to be the prevailing Judgment of the Reformed in *Germany, Holland*, and foreign Parts.

And for the *Dissenters* in *England*, that they are in general of the same Judgment, I might prove from the *Assembly of Divines* Confession, Catechisms, and Directory; and from the Heads of Agreement Assented to by the*United Ministers,*Formerly distinguish’d by the names of*Presbyterian* and *Congregational*;[^340-note49] as also by a large Induction of particular Instances among Divines of every Denomination, wou’d it not carry me to too great a Length. I find Mr. Lob (in his *True Dissenter*) assuring us in general, "It is held by the Dissenters, that nothing less than the *Profession of a saving Faith* gives a Right to *Baptism*."[^340-note50] Nor do I see, by their Writings of a later Date and most in Vogue, any just Grounds to suppose a general Change of Sentiments among them. I will mention two or three Moderns of distinguish’d Name. Dr. Harris (in his *Self-Dedication*) tells us, The Nature of the Lord's Supper plainly supposes *Faith*; and that none but *real* Christians have Right in the Sight of God; tho’ a credible *Profession* Intitles to it in the Sight of the Church, who can't know the Heart. And he declares it the *same Faith*, which qualifies the Adult, both for *Baptism* and for the *Lord's Supper*; there being the same common Nature to both Sacraments, and the latter only a *recognizing* the former.[^340-note51] -- The late Dr. Watts (in his *Holiness of Times, Places, and People*) says, The Christian Church receives none but upon Profession of *true* Faith in Christ, and *sincere* Repentance; none but those who profess to be Members of the *invisible* Church, and in a Judgment of Charity are to be so esteemed. Our *Entrance* into it is appointed to be by a visible *Profession* of our being *born of God*, of real Faith in Christ, of true Repentance, and inward Holiness.[^340-note52] -In fine, to name no more, Dr. Doddridge (in his *Family-Expositor*, on *Act*. VIII. 37.) supposes a credible *Profession* of their *Faith in Christ* required of the Adult in Apostolic Times, in Order to their being admitted to *Baptism*; even such (says he) as imply’d their cordially subjecting their Souls to the Gospel, and their being come to a Point, so as to give up themselves to Christ *with all their Heart*.[^340-note53]

And for the Church of *Scotland*, Mr. Anderson, who well understood their Principles and Practice, assures us (in his *Defence* of them) that *Presbyterians* will not baptise without a previous Profession or Sponsion. To the Adult (says he) it is not only necessary (as it is also in Infants) that they be *internally sanctified*, but also that they make an *outward Profession* of which Baptism is the Badge and Token. To justify this, he observes concerning the *Catechumens* in primitive Times, that during all that State they were Probationers, not only as to their Knowledge, but Piety; and were oblig’d, before they could be admitted to *Baptism*, to give moral Evidences of the *Grace of God in their Hearts*. And he advances it as a *Presbyterian* Principle, that *Faith* and *Repentanc*e are *prerequir’d* to Baptism, in adult Persons at least. By this he points out the true *Matter* of baptismal Profession: And then in Opposition to such as pretend Baptism to be a *converting* Ordinance, he observes, If they can have *Faith* and *Repentance* without the *Spirit* and spiritual *Regeneration*, which they say is not obtained but *in* and *by* *Baptism*, I don't see why they mayn't go to *Heaven* without the Spirit and spiritual Regeneration: For I am sure, *Repentance* toward God and *Faith* toward our Lord Jesus Christ, is the Sum of the Gospel.[^340-note54] -Mr. Warden, another of their noted Writers (in his *Essay on Baptism*) says in the Name of *Presbyterians*, We think that Baptism *supposeth* Men *Christians*; else they have *no Right* to Baptism, the Seal of Christianity; all Seals, in their Nature, supposing the *Thing* that is sealed. He that is of Adult Age, is to *profess* his *Faith* in Christ and his *Compliance* with the whole Device of Salvation, *before* he can have the Seal of the Covenant administred to him.[^340-note55] - The Author of the *Defence of National Churches* (tho’t to be Mr. Willison) says, I know nothing more, requisite to Admission to the Lord's Supper, *in foro Ecclesiastico*, than unto Baptism in an adult Person; they being both Seals of the same Covenant. And he thinks the Objects of Church-Fellowship are "all who profess to accept the Offers of Christ's Grace, with Subjection to his Ordinances, and a suitable Walk, and who confess themselves sincere.[^340-note56]

I have reserved Mr. Baxter for my last Witness, because his Attestation is comprehensive and of a general Aspect. In his *Disputations of Right to Sacraments*, and other his Writings, he repeatedly declares, "It hath been the constant Principle and Practice of the *universal* Church of Christ, to require a *Profession* of saving *Faith* and *Repentance*, as necessary before they would *baptise*; and not to baptise any upon the Profession of any *lower* Kind of Faith. He must shut his Eyes against the fullest Evidence of History and Church-Practice, who will deny this. I desire those otherwise-minded to help me to an Instance of any *one* approv’d Baptism, since Christ's Time or his Apostles, upon the Account of a *Faith* that was *short* of *justifying*, and not upon the Profession of a justifying Faith. Hitherto this is not done by them: but the contrary is fully done by others, and yet they confidently except against my Opinion as a *Novelty*. Mr. Gataker's Books have Multitudes of Sentences recited out of our *Protestant* Divines, that affirm this which they call *new*. It is indeed the common *Protestant* Doctrine, [^340-note57] that the Sacraments do *presuppose* Remission of Sins, and our Faith; that they are instituted to signify these *as in Being*; and do solemnise and publickly own and confirm the mutual Covenant *already* enter’d in Heart. The *Jesuits* themselves do witness this to be the ordinary *Protestant* Doctrine.--It seems not necessary to mention the Judgment of our reformed Divines, as express’d in any of their particular Sayings, when their publick Confessions and Practices are so satisfactory herein."--Mr. *Baxter*, however, recites a Multitude of their Testimonies; producing the Judgment of *Luther, Calvin, Beza, Peter Martyr, Piscator, Melanchton, Altingius, Junius, Polonus, Zanchius, Ursinus, Paræus, Bucanus, Musculus*, Professores *Leyd.* & *Salm. Wollebius, Vossius, Wendeline, Keckerman, Bullinger, Alsted, Deodate*, Dr. *Ames*, Dr. *Moulin*, the Catechism of the Church of *England*, and English Divines, Bp *Usher*, Dr. *Willet*, Dr. *Fulk*, Dr. *Prideaux*, Dr. *Whitaker*, Mr. *Yates, Perkins, Cartwright* &c. the *Scottish* Church in their Heads of Church Policy, and Divines of *Scotland*, Mr. *Gillespy*, Mr. *Rutherford*, and Mr. *Wood*; the *Westminster-Assembly* of Divines, their Confession, Catechisms, and Directory, the Annot. of some of those Divines &c. "And for the *Reformed* Churches in general (Mr. *Baxter* observes) it is past all Question, by their constant *Practice*, that they require the Profession of a *saving* Christian Faith, and take not up with any *lower*.-- And respecting the then-practice in *England*, he says, This is manifest by our daily Administration of Baptism. I never heard (says he) any Man baptise an Infant but upon the Parent's or Susceptor's or Offerer's *Profession* of a *justifying Faith*.[^340-note58]

This leads to your last Inquiry.

Quest. V. *Whether it be the general Opinion, that the* same Qualifications *are required in a* Parent *bringing his Child to Baptism, as in an* adult *Person for his own Admission to this Ordinance?*

Answ. Here, Sir, I suppose you intend only the same Qualifications in *Kind:* or a Profession and Visibility, in some Degree, of the *same sort* of Faith and Repentance; meaning that which is truly evangelical and saving. And understanding you in this Sense, I'm persuaded, by all I can observe, that the Generality of Protestants are in the *Affirmative*; not assenting to a specifick and essential Difference, whatever circumstantial and gradual Disparity they may allow, between the two Cases you mention.

Mr. Baxter speaking of the Judgment and Practice of the Christian *Fathers*, tells us, that Faith (justifying Faith, and not another Kind of Faith) was supposed to be in the Parent, for himself and his Seed: because the Condition or Qualification of the Infant is but this, that he be the *Seed* of a Believer.- And he thinks the Generality of the *Reformed* are in these Sentiments. He declares his own Judgment in full Concurrence herewith, and backs the same with a Variety of Arguments, in his *Five Disputations* and other Writings. He observes, it seems strange to him [^340-note59] that any should imagine, a *lower* Belief in the Parent will help his *Child* to a Title to Baptism, than that which is necessary to *his own*, if he were unbaptised; because mutual Consent is necessary to mutual Covenant, and the Covenant *must* be mutual: No Man hath Right to God's Part, that refuseth his own: They that have no Right to Remission of Sins, have no Right given them by God to Baptism.-- If God be not at all actually obliged in Covenant to any *ungodly* Man, then he is not obliged to give him Baptism: but God is not obliged so to him. *Most of our Divines* make the contrary Doctrine *Pelagianism*, that God should be obliged to Man in a State of Nature in such a Covenant.-- If the Parent's Title be questionable (says he) the Infant's is so too; because the Ground is the same: and it is from the Parent, that the Child must derive it; nor can any Man give that which he hath not.-- We ought not (says he) to baptise those Persons, or their Children, as theirs, who are visible Members of the Kingdom of the *Devil*, or that do not so much as profess their forsaking the Devil's Kingdom: But such are all that profess not a saving Faith. If such are not visibly *in* the Kingdom of the Devil, at least they are not visibly *out* of it.-- All that are duly baptised, are baptised *into* Christ; therefore they are supposed to possess that *Faith*, by which Men are united or ingraffed into Christ: But that is only justifying Faith. Tell me (says he) where any Man was ever said in Scripture to be united to Christ, without saving Faith or Profession of it.- In a Word, Mr. *Baxter* takes Occasion to declare himself in this Manner. ""If Mr. Blake exacts not a Profession of *saving* Faith and Repentance, I say he makes *foul Work* in the Church. And when such *foul Work* shall be voluntarily *maintained*, and the Word of God abused for the *Defilement* of the Church & Ordinances of God, it is a greater Scandal to the *Weak*, & to the *Schismaticks*, and a greater Reproach to the Church, and a sadder Case to considerate Men, than the too common Pollutions of others, which are meerly thro’ *Negligence*, but not justify’d & defended.[^340-note60]

We are told by other impartial Inquirers, that *all the Reformed* do in their Directories and Practices require *Professions*, as well as Promises, of *Parents* bringing their Children to Baptism; even Professions of present Faith and Repentance, as well as Promises of future Obedience; and these not meerly of the Moral, but the Evangelical Kind.--The Judgment of the Church of *Scotland* may be known by their adopting the Confession, Catechisms, and Directory of the *Assembly of Divines:* who, when they require a *parental Profession*, (as in their *Catechisms* &c.) intend it not of any *lower* Kind, than a true Gospel-Faith and Obedience.-- The Mind of the *Dissenters* may be very much judg’d of by the *Reformed Liturgy*, presented in their Name upon King *Charles*'s Restoration; where Parents *credible Profession* of their Faith, Repentance & Obedience is required in order to the Baptism of their Children.[^340-note61] -- I might bring further Evidence from the Writings of particular Divines among them, ancient [^340-note62] and modern: But I must for Brevity omit this. Only I will give you a Specimen in two or three Hints. Mr. Charnock, that great Divine, observes, "Baptism *supposes* Faith in the Adult, & the Profession of Faith in the Parent for his Child."[^340-note63] -- The late eminent Dr. Watts, in his *Holiness of Times, Places & People*, thus declares himself, with respect to the *Infants of true Believers:* "In my Opinion, so far as they are any Way Members of the *visible* Christian Church, it is upon *Supposition* of their being (with their *Parents*) Members of the *invisible* Church of God."[^340-note64]

On the whole, as to our Fathers here in *New-England*, 'tis true, they asserted a *Baptism-Right* in Parents for themselves & Children, whom yet they excluded from full Communion; the Ground of which Difference was hinted before: and they deny’d a *Parity of Reason* between the *two Cases* now in View, on some Accounts. Their chief Ground was, that *Adult-Baptism* requires a Measure of visible *moral Fitness* or inherent Holiness in the Recipient: whereas, *Infant Baptism* requires nothing visible in it’s Subject, but a *relative Fitness* or federal Holiness, the *formalis Ratio* of Infant-Membership, accruing from God's Charter of Grace to his Church, taking in the Infant-Seed with the believing Parent. Baptism they supposed to run parallel with regular Membership; and the Child of such a Parent intitled to this Covenant-Seal in it’s own Right, on the Foot of a distinct personal Membership, derivative in Point of *Being*, but independent for it’s *Duration*, and for the *Privileges* annexed to it by divine Institution.--However, they certainly own’d *Parental Profession*, as belonging to the due Order & just Manner of Administration, both *meet & needful*.-Accordingly they provided, that *Parents* claiming Covenant-Privileges for their Children, should own their Covenant-State, have a Measure of Covenant-Qualifications, and do Covenant-Duties, in some Degree, to the Satisfaction of a rational Charity.--And it ought to be remember’d, they have left it as their solemn Judgment, that even taking *Baptism-Right* for a Right of Fitness *in Foro Ecclesiastico*, still the Parents whose Children they claimed *Baptism* for, were such as must be allowed to have a Title to it for *themselves*, in Case they had remain’d unbaptised: looking upon them, altho’ not duly fitted for the Sacrament of Communion & Confirmation, yet sufficiently so for the Sacrament of Union and Initiation; Professors in their Infancy *Parentally*, and now *Personally* in an initial Way; appearing *Abraham*'s Children, in some Measure of *Truth*, to a judicious Charity; justly therefore baptisable, in their Persons and Offspring, by all the Rules of the Gospel.[^340-note65] -- I am not here to argue upon the Justness of this Scheme of Thought on the Case; but only to represent the Fact in a genuine Light.

I have no Room (Sir) for any further Remarks. But must conclude, with Christian Salutes, and the Tender of every brotherly Office, from

*Your very affectionate Friend and humble Servant,* THOMAS FOXCROFT. Boston, June 26. 1749.

## B79. Letter from John Searle[?], [c. July 1749] B079.J.Searle-JE c edited

John Searle[?]B079. [John Searle] to JE, n.d. [c. 7/49]. BRBL, Sermon frags., f. 1160. Shorn at bottom.

Revd Sir,

These Wait upon you to inform you that we have made Choice of you to preach the Sermon wh will be expected on the Day of My Ordination, and humbly to desire you to gratify us in this thing - the People are unanimous in desiring it. and it Seems properly to fall upon you Revd Sir, Seeing you have had the Greatest Acquaintance with me of any of the Ministers that will be present.

The Journey it is likely will not be tedious for the Road is usually better at that Time of the year, than any other, it may be comfortably rid in 2. Days Glascow is about half way from Northampton here, and there is Comfortable entertainment, for man and horse.

I hope Sir, you wil not fail of coming, & preaching the Sermon, but if by any Consideration you are determined not to do it, be pleased to Signify it by the Bearer. I beg an Interest in your prayers to God for me that I Might be prepar'd for for the great work of the Gospel Ministry, & to come to this People in the fullness of the Blessing of the Gospel of Christ.

These, with my Duty to yourself & Madam and Love to your Children, are humbly offer'd by […]

## B83. Letter from David Parsons, Jr., February 21, 1750 B083.D.Parsons-JE 2-21-50 edited

David Parsons, Jr.B083. David Parsons to JE, 2/21/50. BRBL, f. 1331.

Hadly Febry 21: 1749/50

Revd & Hond Sr

Md Edwards has proposed to me a Question which for some Reasons I am unwilling to Resolve to any Person but your self; & to you sr: only for your private improvement which Please sir to take in this transcript of a letter to me

Revd sr Northampton People are desirious of having Some minister preach on the Opposite side of the Controversy to Mr Edwards, they have brôt an Application to this Association for advice & Lodgd with them a protest[^343-note1] & at their desire with the Advice of some of our Brethren in the ministry I have wrote to the ministers to desire them to Meet at -- on thursday Early in the morning I hope you will Come, for you Cant Easily think what Posture things are in, & unless we do Concert Some measures we Are in Danger of being overrun, & Northampton will proceed to Extreeme Measures (being Conducted by some Gent: not over tender of ministers or Chhs) which may prove of Pernicious Consesequence to us & all our Chhs.

I have the Promise of some Gent: of some hope you will not fail from yr Brother &c.

Feb: 20th: 1749/50

___________________

That you may have much of Divine Support & Direction under your unhappy Destressing Troubles is the Wish & Prayer of sr your oblidged friend & very humble Servt David Parsons

[^343-note1]: Conjectural reading; alternate: "Mr [--]."

## B84. Letter from Stephen Williams, April 5, 1750 B084.S.Williams-JE 4-5-50 edited

Stephen WilliamsC084. Stephen Williams to JE, 4/5/50. BRBL, f. 1335.

Springfield Apr 5th 1750

Rev. & Dear Sir,

We have received a letter from a Committee chosen at Northampton on the 2d Instant, desiring our advice whether the Church there should agree with your self, in your desire or resolution to go out of the County for two or three Churches or Ministers of a Councill to decide your labouring affairs we have return'd them an Answer, a Copy of which we Enclose to you, as of this also to them.

We are heartily concern'd at the unhappy situation of your affairs, and should gladly contribute to your help, we looked upon our selves in duty bound to answer their Letter, and you there see our sentiments as we have offered them to your people. We would also propose to your self, That you will use Condescendency and Christian methods, That the Question in debate, may be resolv'd; that thereby the way may be open'd to a decisive Councill, as soon as may be, which we understand you your self & the people are very desirous of.

The Revd Mr Hopkins has communicated to us, the Letter you wrote to him of the 2d Instant, and we are fully of the mind, that you ought to have opportunity to give your Reasons, why you should go out of the County, to those, who have the Consideration of the Case. And we hope, Sir, that you with the Church, will, in a friendly manner, agree upon some [2] Method for the resolution of that labouring Question.

And we need not say to you that the more of a Christian condescention is us'd on both sides, the nearer, you will come to the Obligations you ly under as Christians, and the more likely to obtain a happy Issue. Wishing the Divine Direction & Blessing to you & your People.

we are your Brethren & fellow Servts Stephn Williams, Moderator in the name & by order of the Association. To the Revd Mr Jona Edwards at Northampton.

## B85. Letter from Jonathan Judd, [c. April] 1750 B085.J.Judd-JE c edited

Jonathan JuddB085. Jonathan Judd to JE, [c. Apr.?] 1750. BRBL, "History of Redemption," Notebook 1, p. 87, f. 1212.

Revd and dear Sir

I desire (if your buiseness will permit) that you would take the trouble to solve a difficulty which at present I cant get over - I find mr Baxter insists upon [-] a professing of Saving faith in order to to members of the visable chh and in this faith he includes not only ye assent of Judgment but also the Consent of the will - (which no dout is included in Saving faith) but yet he allows not a necessaty of assurance of a saving faith - I will transcribe his words that you may fully understand what I aim at -- pag 43 by a profesion I mean in ye proper sence that which hath Somthing present for its object or Subject professed. its its a present assent assent and Consent that is to be professed &c- thus its evident according to him, that a person must profess that he believes with a Saving faith or he now with his whole heart beleives in Christ yet in the next pag he hath thes words. Note. Also that it is not a Profession of this faith of mine is Saving indeed saving Sincere Justifying or Saving faith, that I Speak of &c thes words either directly or indrectly show that he did not insist upon assurance - and the difficulty with me is this (viz) how a person Can Consistent with truth make Such a profession and not have assurence as I before observed, his words necessarily include, as much as to say I beleive with all my heart or further as much as that I have with my whole heart chosen Christ as my Savior and esteem him above all other enjoyments and I want to know how this can be complyed with Consistent with truth and yet the person is not assured - - - - In removing this dout or difficulty you will much oblige me yr und unworthy Son in the Gospel -- -- Jonathan Judd NH 1750

P.S. I meet with the Same difficulty in wt you have published (viz) in yr treatise upon the Aeffe Affection pag 298 and in your enquiry into the qualifications of the members pg 14 compared with page 110 -- --

## B86. Letter from Peter Clark, May 21, 1750 B086.P.Clark-JE 5-21-50 edited

Peter ClarkB086. Peter Clark to JE, 521/50. BRBL, f. 1327.

Salem Village May 21. 1750

Revd & Dear Sir.

Yesterday being ye Lords day, as I was Going down to Salem I receiv'd your Letter on ye 7th instant, & was desired by the bearer to return an Answer, & Leave it in Salem this day; & being oblig'd besides ye two Stated Exercises in public, to preach on occasion Extraordinary in ye Evening, it was Late before I return'd home at night. So that ye shortness of ye time to which I was limited, will allow me to write but a few lines, which I can Scarce call an Answer to your Letter. I find Sir, by your Letter, it is expected, that I would write to your people my tho't, of your Late Book, after I had read it; Indeed I had propos'd such a thing, but I think, I made no absolute promise of it, but only Said I might do it, if I tho't it proper, & adviseable &c. But since I have perused your Book, Especially Since you have explain'd yourself more fully on Some particular points in your Letter, I am more undetermined, whether it be proper; because I am more at a Loss to apprehend, wherein ye main ground of ye Controversy, between you, & your people lies; or where matters Stick, that shou'd hinder an accommodation between you & them.

For after you have Conceeded, that a person making a profession of the Essentials of Godliness, or ye Acts implyed in an hearty compliance with ye Covenant, made understandingly, if there were an external conversation agreable thereto, had a right to be receiv'd, as ye object of a publick Charity even tho' he himself might scruple his own Conversion yet that ye minister or Church, had no right Debar Such a professour, tho' he sho'd say, he did not think himself Converted; as you write in your Letter, I can't easily conceive, what can reasonably be objected, even by those that are in ye Sentiments of ye Late Revd Mr Stoddard, unless they will Say that ye Church must admit its members without any personal profession at all, or upon a profession of anything beside, or short of ye Christian Covenant, or unless they make ye obligation of ye Covenant ye Sole matter of such profession, yt is to Say, a profession, or acknowledgemt of their obligations to ye duties of ye Covt tho' conscious in ye meantime, of a reigning aversion in themselves to ye principal Dutys & privileges of it. The two former Suppositions, I believe, will not be asserted, or maintain'd. And as to ye Last, I am firmly of ye perswasion, that a present consent to both parts of ye Covt that is, a present Choice of God for our God in Christ, & an actual Compliance with ye Conditions of ye Covt imparting faith & Repentance (and not a promise De futuro) as well as a Consent to ye Obligations of ye Covt ought to be made ye matter of Such a Christian profession as gives a right of Admission into ye visible Church. for, as there is no other Door (if I understand ye Gospel) of admission to Spiritual Communion with Christ in ye invisible church, but a true faith, repentance, Selfdenial &c. So a visible profession of those Graces, & dutys is ye only Door of Admission to ye Communion of ye visible Church. That which you complain of in ye Establish'd method of ye Churches proceedings, as ye Ground of your Scruple, you Say is their publickly assenting to ye form of Words rehears'd on occasion of Admission to Communion, without pretending thereby to mean any Such thing as an hearty Consent to the terms of ye Gospel Covt - but to something Else -- Something Consistent with their knowing that they don't chuse God as their Chief Good, but Love ye world more than him &c. If this be a true account of ye proceedings of any Church, there Seems to be matter of Blame somewhere, either in ye form of words, or in ye assent to it; for either ye form of words, assented to, is ye Form of Sound words, or ye Baptismal Covt importing ye personal Dedication of him that assents to it, to God ye Father, Son, & Holy Ghost, or it is not; If it be not ye Christian covt Sealed in Baptism which is assented to, in order to admission to Communion, there is certainly a defect in ye Form, but if it be the Christian Covenant, (as I presume it is) then ye Defect must be in ye assent, and I confess, I see not how a solemn publick Consent to this covt with such a Construction put upon it, as you have represented, can be vindicated from blame. for I must insist upon it, as my principle, (as I declared in my Letter to Majr Pomroy) & I think it one of ye foundation principles of the oracles of God, that it is Credible profession of Repentance towards God, & faith towards our Lord Jesus Christ, which is Requisite, & sufficient to Give a right to Church Communion in Sacred ordinances. I hold it to be necessary, & you, Sir, if I may gather your sense from your Book, or from your Letter, agree with me in granting it Sufficient. And therefore according to ye principles Laid down in my Letter, I don't apprehend myself concern'd to contradict, or oppose anything material in the main Design of your Book. Some things, I tho't, needed to be explain'd (as we are apt to think, in reading any thing with a Critical attention) & for want of a fuller explanation did not know how far they might be carryed. But ye Chief of these you have explain'd to Good Satisfaction in your Letter. And if ye Good people of your Parish, think (from what I have written) that I stand on their side, I would hope ye Difference between you & them is not so Great, but that it may, by prudent & proper method, be amicably Composed. Dear Sir, I am not Conscious to myself of having had my mind prepossess'd with prejudice, from ye Reports & informations I have had from one side, or other in ye Controversy. - I shou'd be heartily Sorry, if any thing I have Said, or written shou'd be improv'd to your disadvantage, or if it were capable of being So improv'd, And particularly, that there shou'd be any mistake about what I said of ye Absurdity, of (what I was inform'd was) your opinion. I never Said, Sir, that your opinion, or ye opinion you maintain'd in fact was absurd, or easily Reduc'd to an Absurdity, but th I said it of ye opinion itself, by mistake reported to have been yours, this I did indeed, & do still tax with absurdity, as you also do, with arrogance, & presumption. And I had never said it to your people, but to account, as well as I could, for ye misinformation they had Receiv'd of my being engaged in Answering your Book. Yet have been Careful at ye Same time to intimate my Disbelief of it; And in my Letter to Maj. Pumroy, plainly signifyed, yt I wou'd not give in to ye belief, that you espous'd the principle referr'd to, for this very Reason, even because of ye absurdity of it. And if it has been improv'd by any to your prejudice, it was far beyond my intention, & (I think) the reason of ye thing. But tho' I believed you to be wrong'd in ye Report, yet I imagin'd you had given Greater Occasion for it than I find you have done, & was ready to think it more likely, (as I was inform'd by others) that tho' you disclaim'd a discriminating Judgment of ye Spiritual State of others, yet that you insisted upon persons having certain experience, & Evidence of a Work of Conversion in themselves, even to their own assurance, who offer'd themselves to your Communion, in order to their Admission, (which, I tho't, needed a little Correction) but even this, so far as appears, is Groundless; Whatever passages in your Book Seem to have an Aspect that way, ye t you have Given me abundant Satisfaction, in your Letter, that you are rather in ye Contrary sentimt in declaring it to be your Judgment, that a professour ought not to be debarr'd from ye Lords table, tho' he had scruples about his own Conversion, having ye Gospel requisites of a visible profession, to intitle him to the publick Charity. - I had thoughts of writing to you, Sir, when I was under a sort of Necessity of writing to your people. But you have happily prevented me, for ye Concessions in your Letter before mention'd, are ye fullest that I would have advis'd to, in order to ye Composition of ye Difference between you & your Brethren; And if ye Same be propos'd to them, I can't but be perswaded of introducing an harmony between you & your people. Which I sincerely Wish & pray & [^346-note1] hope that it may please God by his overruling providence & grace to bring to Effect. But I must Confess, as I intimated in my Letter at first, Since my Reading your Book & Letter, I Seem to be more in ye dark, about ye main point on which ye present controversy turns, than before, and So may not be in so fit a Capacity to Give advice.

Yet this I would Say, rather than there shou'd be a breach between you & your people, pray, Sir, condescend to ye utmost you can, with a Safe Conscience, & Consider how far it may be Expedient to yield to a prevailing Custom consistently with your faithfulness to your charge for preserving ye unity of ye Spirit in ye bond of peace. I am very Sensible your trials are Great, under which you will have need of much wisdom, & meekness, & occasion for ye use of those eminent ministerial Gifts & graces with which God has furnish'd you; -- I heartily Sympathize with you, in your Difficulties & troubles, being not wholly a stranger to ye heart of a minister under trials of a like nature -- I would add much more on ye Subject of your Book & Letter, but must crave your excuse of my abruptness, by reason of ye difficulty, of writing, & want of time. Whether it may serve any Good End, for me to write any tho'ts further upon it to you, or them, as I proposed, I am still in doubt. I wish all peace & happiness to you, & your family & the Good Brethren of your Flock whom I respect & honour, And Earnestly intreat ye God of all Grace to grant you Guidance & assistance in your Difficult affairs, & conduct them to a peace full & happy Issue, And with desires of your prayers also for me I rest Dear Sir, your Affectionate Friend & brother in ye Gospel Peter Clark

To ye Revd Mr Jona Edwards.

[^346-note1]: **marginal.** [3]

## B87. Letter from John Owen, June 2, 1750 B087.J.Owen-JE 6-2-50 edited

John OwenB087. John Owen to JE, 6/2/50. BRBL, f. 1330.

Revd: and much Honoured, Sir.

Altho' I stand in a Low and vastly unequal station to you, to whome I'm going to write yet I trust you'l pardon my Boldness herein, Since you are a professed Deciple of the Lord Jesus Christ, and an Instructor of the Ignorant; who are So in matters of Religeon and Such a one I must profess myself to be in a great measure in Spiritual and Divine things. I have but Little time I can Spare from the Business of my Occupation, yet I have Spent Some of my Spare Howers in Reading your tract, Concerning the Qualification of members to full Communion; & I must Say (without flattery) the Arguments are fully Satisfying to me, and do appear abundantly Clear: your Book has also been a means of Convinceing Some persons, of Religion good understanding to be of the Same mind; but[^347-note1] others are So prejudiced against the Doctrine you have there maintained, that will not read the Book; but Condemn it before they See it; I think I am thankfull that providence has Seen it to bring you on yt Side of the Quest: and hope in time true Christians will all Embrace that Doc: but at ye Same time we have reason to be Sorry & Concerned for the unhappy Difference among Professors on account thereof, and Especially among the People of N: Hampton; Now is the time ye Great Enemy of mankind will improve to ye uttermost, to Divide Christians among themselves; Now Satan will use his utmost Skill to Cause all Revealled Religeon to be Derided and Scoffed at; now will Deists, & Athiests Rejoice in Heart; and hope for more & more Confusion among Professors, Oh! how will they mock, how will they Vaunt themselves over Gods Heritage and Say So is it come to pass as we Imagined & Sayed it would.

But I need not add here you (Revd: Sir) are not Ignorant of Satans Devices; but while in the Body have not ye best Christians need to watch & pray least they enter into temptation. - - Your People have their Spirits Raised, (as I perceive by talking with Some of them) and Should they not be treated with a Spirit of meekness, Love & tenderness? Should they not be Intreated perswaded, and invited, in these things? are they not in this Regard (tho' old Xns) Babes in this Doctrine of X you've maintained? they have been perhaps from their Childhood trained up in the contrary Scheme, they have received ye opposite Doctrine, almost Universaly from One of the most Eminent Divines in N: England, I mean your Venerable Predicessor; they have many if not the most of them taken it upon trust (as most people do all their principals in Religeon) without any Examination; & they are hardly beaten from it; they are hardly perswaded to enter into any Examination about it: (as I have found by talking with Some of them) they think it almost Sufficient to Say Mr: Stoddard[^347-note2] Sayed So, & So; they take him for a Text, and never Examine into ye Holy Scripture to Se whether the things he Speak in this Regard, were So, or not; From hence Revd: Sir, does it not appear that must have all patience used with them? let them have time; let their Spirits Cool, perswade them both publickly & privately. and it is to be hoped they will in time, Come to See the Truth of the Doc: You hold to.

But after all Should they Continue to Reject the Same, & refuse to Examine anything about it & to Cast you out from among them; yet Dubtless you will have the Testimony of a Good Conscience, which will yield more true peace & Comfort, than any Earthly Enjoyment whatsoever: And tho Some Great Divine Should appear on ye other Side of the Question; you will not be Surprized; knowing the Doc: you've Espoused is the Doctrine of the N Testim-[^347-note3] [-] ent, & will finally be owned by the Great Lord of Chh Jesus Christ, Since none but true Christians will be accepted with him at Last: But fearing I have transgressed by writing too much, I conclude only would Say, That altho I am fully Satisfied with the truth of your Scheme yet Some Scruples have a Risen in my mind (and Some have been objected to me) which I should be glad to have more fully Cleared, and if ever you Should apear in Print again on this Subject, If you (Revd: Sir) think them worth your Notice, you will be pleased to take Some Notice of ye Folloing things: vizt: 1. What Shall one do; being Convinced of the truth of yt: Doc: yt: none have right to ye Sacrament of the Lords Supper unless they can truely make a profession of Godliness, and yet was formerly admitted on the Contrary principal?[^347-note4] Shall Such a one not thinking himself Converted; Continue Comeing to ye Sacrament, or Shall he forbare? 2: Shall an unregenerate man that has owned the Covenant (as 'tis Called) bring his Children to Baptism, or Shall he forbare? 3. Whether it be the Duty of a person that is a member of a Chh to Join in the Sacrament with a Chruch that admits members with a profession of Godliness?

There is another objection made to me by a Revd: minister; And tho' I think it not to ye Case, yet because it Came from a minister will mention it - - 4.: whether a member of a Chh So often as he is in Doubt about his Real Change Stay away from ye Sacrament of ye Lords Supper, or Shall he Come? 5 It has also been brought to me as an Argument against the truth of[^347-note5] your Doctrine by a person of Religeon: viz: That none that come to ye Lords Supr: while unconverted, & afterwards have been hopefully Converted do repent their Joining with the Chh: whilst unregenerate, they think their coming to yt Sacrament was a means of their Convertion, and therefore Judge it a Duty to Come to ye Lords Supper while unconverted - - - - - - - - -

These have Lain on ye minds of Some as objections to ye truth of yt: Doc: yt: maintains yt: churches Should admit none as members in full Communion with them but Such as make a profession of Godliness: and tho' I don't them Sufficient on any Account to overthro' yt: Doc: yet (for ought I know) it might be best these & any other Scrules people have on their minds may be answered Thus Revd: Sir; Hopeing the doctrine you've maintained will in a Short time Spread it Self among all Christians, and the present Difficalties at N: Hampton terminate for Gods Glory and ye Good of Souls; & your & Family's welfare: I conclude by Beging your prayers for me & mine, that God would give us Renewing pardoning & Sanctifying Grace & use [-] me & mine as instruements of his Glory in the world through Jesus Christ

Amen

From your Sincere tho' unworthy Friend & Humble Servt: John Owen Simsbury 1st Society June 2nd: A:D: 1750:

P.S: If you would print again on the Subject aforementioned I wd endeavour to promote ye Same
