## B88. Letter from John Searle, June 4, 1750 B088.J.Searl-JE 6-4-50 edited

John SearleB088. John Searl to JE, 6/4/50. Hartford Seminary, Edwards Papers.

[Revd, and Hond Sir,

Sixteen Days after the Date of your Letter I receiv'd it, where in I am desir'd to give in a Particular Testimony that your Opinion respecting the Lord's Supper, which] has Occasion'd such Tumults at Northampton of late, was not kept a Secret 'till after Col. Stoddard's Death. If the Letter had come speedily to my Hand, I suppose before this Time you might have receiv'd a Reply; which might have better Answer'd the End you had chiefly in View- however, I will endeavour (too late I fear) to give some Account of the Things propos'd.

When I winter'd at Northampton at Deacon Pomroy's, which was in part of years 1746, & 47, you deliver'd, & and at Sundry times discours'd upon your Opinion, That a Profession of true Godliness was a Qualification requisite to full Communion in the Visible Church of Christ - Once in particular, you plainly manifested your Mind in Discourse with three of your Neighbours, which were as I remember, Capt. Sheldon, Lieut N. Phelps, & Noah Parsons. - Besides, at another time, which I Shall not, probably, soon forget, as I was in your Study, you Mind appear'd considerably exercis'd and in a Moving Manner, said, "It Seems I am born to be a Man of Strife"! Then after mentioning two or three Tryals then past, you proceeded, Sir, to name One with which you was then exercis'd, viz. The Prospect of many Difficulties in ye Way of a certain Duty, which was a forsaking the Plan which Members had been Admitted into ye Christian Church: "I have for a long Time, you said, been reasoning [upon this Matter, and am come to a Satisfying Conclusion of the Truth, [^348-note1] or Mind of Christ in ye Affair; Nor can I in Conscience, proceed for the future as I have done hereto fore"-or in Words to ye same Purpose.- Then, Sir, you gave it as your Opinion yt Col. Stoddard would Strenuously Maintain the Other Side of the Question, as well as far ye greater part of the Question, as well as far ye greater part of the Town. Then Straits and Difficulties, which might exercise your Family, upon your future Proceedings, Arose to your View.-Your leaving that smooth Path so long occupied] & smooth'd by Mr Stoddard, for a Straiter, perplex'd with Bryars & Thorns, seemed then much to try, not to Weaken your resolution. - One of the Wisest Means of Accomplishing your Purpose, you supposd might be Writing upon the Subject;- which I then Suppos'd you would soon engage in. And what seems Worthy of Notice, is, that you never enjoyn'd Secrecy upon me or Any other according to ye best of my Remembrance. - At Deac. Pomroy's I discoursed with him often upon this Affair, or I am strangely Mistaken; and read to him some Passages out of your Book of Religious Affections (p. 298-300) where I told him yt your Opinion with Regard to Xian Communion, was, if not expressly, at least implicitly laid down, & might be fairly & safely concluded, which I think he Allow'd.

Eleazar King & Eleazar Burt, both very Sociable Men, to my Knowledge heard of this Opinion; & which I believe they will Allow; And is it not very probable that their NeÎbours would had some free Intimation?- The Pretence of Some Persons, in Northampton that sd Opinion was kept entirely a Secret till after Col. Stodard's Death, has appeared Strange to Me. Whether their late Exercises of Mind have eras'd some Things from their Memory, or whether their forgetfulness is Owing to some other particular Cause, 'tis not for me to determine. - The Spring after my Wintering at Deacon Pomroys, which was before Col. Stoddard's Death, I travel'd to Lebanon [^348-note2] where Rumours of your Opinion had Spread, concerning which, some People in the Crank enquir'd of me; and upon enquiring of Mr. Wheelock, the Opinion had been known there, Months before. If the present Opportunity would Allow, & if Need requir'd, I might have been more particular as to some Circumstances. -

Tender & Humble regards to your Family, from Revd. Sir, your unworthy Son and Humble Servt. John Searl

GuilfordJune 4th. 1750.

I remain still in a low State of Health, while my mind is exercis'd with Several Tryals; I therefore Need an Interest in your Prayers. J. S.

[^348-note1]: **marginal.** [2]

[^348-note2]: **marginal.** [3]

## B89. Letter from Edward Billing, June 11, 1750 B089.E.Billing-JE 6-11-50 edited

Edward BillingB089. Edward Billing to JE, 6/11/50. Cold Spring, Mass. BRBL, f. 1326.

Revd & Dear Sir.

I have communicated ye Letter Missive from yr Chh to ye Chh of Cold spring, and proposed to their Chh. to Send a Delegate: But could obtain no vote: What ye reasons were I cant tell. But I was informed last week. that ye Chh would not let me go to Counsel: because my principles and Circumstances were such. as must render me an unfit Member of that Counsel: which suggestion (without doubt) was put into ye Noddles of some weak people. by some of your Chh renowned for Superiour wisdom. Another who came from N Hampton said yt He refused to vote. because many people at N H told Him they did not desire ye Counsel should sit upon ye affair. for they should not look upon themselves oblieged to follow ye advice of ye Counsel. And that If the Counsel should advise Mr Edwards to tarry longer, they would not regard it etc.

This is ye sum of what I can say upon ye Matter: So that you see Revd Sir I am excused from ye buisnes which you desired me to perform. I hope you dont stand in need of my advice. But If I might advise you. it should be to this purpose: not to be run down by Northampton at last. But to propose to ye Chh yet to send to some other Chh to supply ye place of this Chh.or else to chose a or If not to desire your Chh to send a Letter to Me and to Some particular person of this Chh or some Neighbouring Chh. desiring us to come Join ye Counsel. for doubtless your Chh has a power to chose some member of this Chh or some other whethe and whoever is Chosen may go whether ye Chh wh He belongs to will send Him or not.

If you think what I propose is reasonable then propose to yr Chh to send their request in a Letter sealed, to Ensign Dwight, or Jonathan Graves, or Joseph Bridgman. But I rather chose they would send to Col Dwight or Doc Pincheon. To come in ye room of a Delegate from this Chh. this is but a new scheam a[n]d possibbely you and I shall think it will not do when we haved viewed throughly.

I have no more to add but my desire and prayer that God would be with you and carry you thro' and support you under all yr troubles.

From yr real Friend & Brother Ed Billing

June 11. 1750.

PS. I might have said further. some that belonged to this Chh Have said that mr Foxcrofts Chh refused to send a delegate with Him after He had read ye Letter wh you Sent Him to ye Chh. which misinformation I suppose they h some of your people gave with a view to hinder this Chh from sending a Delegate. so that doubtless ye hand of Joab was in this & therefore If I was in your case I would insist upon having some Chh that Yr Chh should send to some other Chh to supply ye room of this. and let it be Mr Eatons Chh. and If they will not do it I would not submit ye matter to ye Counsel when it comes upon ye spot.

## B91. Letter from Solomon Williams, August 20, 1750 B091.S.Williams-JE 8-20-50 edited

Solomon WilliamsB091. Solomon Williams to JE, 8/20/50. BRBL, f. 1334.

Lebanon Aug: 20 1750

Revd. & dear Sir

I received yours by Mr Fowler of ye 21 of last Month & should have Returnd Answer by Mr Lyman who was here soon After but he was in hast & I could not have time to write. As to the Answer to your Book Abt wch you Speak & desire to see, You have been Misinform'd. I did the beginning of ye Last winter Set My Self to Examine the Controversy you have Written upon with such helps as I had or could Readily get with a design to Gain Conviction if you was on the Right side or to answer it if it appeared to Me you was wrong, & Upon such Examination as I was Able to Make I could not but Judge you was on the Wrong Side of the Question & began to draw up An Answer; but it Pleased God to visit the Place, & My own Family with the distressing disease the throat distemper by which he Called one of My sons out of ye world & held two of them for along while as it were over the Grave calling Me to Other work than controversy, I thru by that subject & did Nothing More Abt it till the week before I Recd your Letter. I have been Often Askd About it & have been moved to prepare An Answer for the press & believe I have sd that I had An Aversion to Controversy, as I thought you was so fixd in your Sentiments I had No Expectation that I should be Able to Convince you & it wd probably be an Endless Controversy & not Choosing to Spend My Life in that way, I had little Inclination to print Upon it. I am now as I have leisure, going thro the Consn of your Arguments which if I shall be Enabled to finish I shall Submit to the Judgment of Others whether to Allow to be printed or Not. I am heartily Sorry that there Could be no best Accommodn & forbearance between you & your people & that things Are bro't to such A Pass as to put An End to your Ministry there. With due Respects I Am

Sr Your Affectionate Kinsman & hume Servt Soln Williams

## B92. Letter from Samuel Davies, August 26, 1750 B092.S.Davies-JE 8-26-50 edited

Samuel DaviesB092. Samuel Davies to JE, 8/26/50. BRBL, f. 1328.

Revd. & very Dear Sir,

The Continuance of the Correspondence your friendly Condescension begun will always be very agreeable to me: tho' ye Prospects of so many Interruptions as our Distance & other other Circumstances, will unavoidably occasion, is afflictive. This (sir) is like to be the only Method of Conversation we shall be blest with, till we come to our Father's House above, where everlasting Intimacy subsists between all His numerous Children, & where they are more fit for mutual Acquaintance & Society, than in this Stage of Imperfection. Thither, I hope, I am aspiring, tho' faintly: & I request the Help of your Prayers to accelerate my Motion.

Blessed be God, I am free from the burdensome Necessity of an idle Life. So large & rude a Quarter of the Lord's Vineyard is committed to my Care, that I can hardly behold it, without being animated to Industry, or (which is frequently my Case) sunk in Discouragement at the Disproportion of my Strength to my Work. O! that I mayn't have more Reason to cry out at last than Grotius had, "Proh! Titam perdidi Operosî Nihil Agendo" - I hope my poor Ministrations are not wholly in vain; tho' my Success is not, I think, equal to what the Circumstances of these Parts wou'd seem to promise, according to common Observation. Nothing seems wanting, but larger Effusions of the Divine Spirit from on high, & better Accomplishments in the solitary, sleepy Watchman. Thousands are eager to hear, from a Principle of Curiosity, or a better: sundry are proselyted; & a few, I hope, are in the place of ye breaking forth of Children. There seems to be of late a greater Solemnity among the People, especially at the Meeting-house where the greatest Assemblies are won't to attend, than I have observ'd for some Time. - The labours of that pious Enoch (for so I may denominate him from his intimate Walk with God) Mr. Davenport, who has been here about 2 Months, have been generally acceptable, & I hope serviceable to sundry. By observing his Conversation, & reading Mr. Brainerd's Life, I have had Clearer Discoveries of my prodigious Defects, than ever I had before - O! my Brother, What a Misery, what a Hell is it, to be unlike to God! 'Tis our criminal Inadvertency that makes us so tho'tless about it; & our unaccountable Stupidity that renders us so insensible of it - Forgive me, My Dr Br. that I make these Complaints in your Name as well as my own; for I cannot once think that you or any of the Heirs of Heaven, have so much Reason for them, as I have - I have often, with an aching Heart, read that surprising Delineation (or rather hypotyposis) of a Xn's Life, which the Mercy of God has given us in Rom. 14. 7, 8. May I never rest 'till I find myself the glorious Transcript of it!

I hope, Sir, your Endeavours have not been wanting, to provide some Supplies for the numerous Vacancies in this Colony; & your Prudence will direct you to send none but such as you judge qualified for a Place attended with so many peculiar Difficulties. Please to inform such as intend to come to Hanover, that it will be necessary for them to come about the 10th of April or October, that they may be qualified by the President & Council, who then sit 24 Days, for they have taken away the Power of qualifying Ministers from County Courts, & appropriated it to themselves. As for the new Settlements, where there 9 or 10 Vacancies, their Distance secures them from the Inspection of the Council; & therefore Ministers may officiate there without Molestation at any time.

I had some tho'ts of preparing for the Press the substance of 4 Sermons I deliver'd lately on 2 Cor. 4. 3. & Acts 8. 22. On the first Text I proposed I. To shew who those are to whom ye Gospel is hid. II. In what great Danger they are in of perishing; Or, That it is dreadfully uncertain whether ever they will be bro't out of their present Condition. III. To vindicate the Justice of God in suffering such to continue ignorant of the Gospel, & perish. On the 2nd I propos'd, as far as I now remember (for I have not my Notes about me) I. To shew that it is awfully uncertain whether ever those who are now impenitent, will ever be bro't to Repentance, & so obtain forgiveness. Yet II. That it is possible. III. That a meer Possibility is sufficient to excite the Impenitent to use all Means for obtaining Repentance, &c. It pleased the Lord to make these Discourses solemnizing to sundry; & I have found since they were peculiarly fit for the Awakening of the Secure here. This, together with an Apprehension yt they might be suitable to the Cases of Secure Sinners, has inclin'd me to publish them. If you think any of them will be needed in your Parts, please to inform me, & I shall endeavour to send them to such Places, as you shall nominate.

Pray sir, write to me as often as you can; & when you cannot find a readier Method of Conveyance, direct yours to the Care of the Revd. Mr. Burr at Newark - I shall be glad to know of the Affairs of the Church with you - And now, committing you to that God, whose you are, and whom you serve, I must break off Conversation with you, & only assure you that I am,

Revd. sir, Yr affectionate Br & Fellow=Labourer in the Lord's Vineyard, Saml. Davies

Hanover Augt 26 - 50

P.S. When I review my Letter, I cannot but secretly blush to see what Freedom I have used wth an entire stranger: But while I was writing, I found my Affections to you so warm, & the Pleasure of free Conversation so great, that I cou'd not easily restrain myself; & therefore, I hope, Dr Sr, you'll take it in good Part.

Westfield March 22 175[0/1]

Revd Sir Having now an opportunity and Mr Ballentine Informing me that He Disyn to Send to you If he had opportunity to accquaint you with the mind & Desire of People in our Town: That whereas The Comtee of North Hampton Have Sent to Mr Ballentine to Preach the Next Sabbath at North Hampton and Mr Ballentine Inform'd me he Determined to go to which our People gave Consent Provided Mr Edwards wold Come and Supply his Place for a valuable Consideration of money and given Me order's to Pay 5ll or 6ll or wt you Demand as we Can't Expect you Should Come without Satissfaction from us

And Now Sr If you Can any way Condescend to Come and Preach with us Next Sabbath (otherwise we Shall be Destitute) you would greatly oblige our People Mr Ballentine & your Humble Servant -

Israel Ashley

Northampton July 10th: 1751

Rev [Sir]

[T]hrô divine mercy I ariv’d Safe home the next morn after I left Stockbridge about Ten o clock. came this Instant from Yor house & Your family are under Comfortable circumstances. ## B98. Letter from Josiah Willard, October 19, 1751 B098.J.Willard-JE 10-19-51 edited

Josiah WillardB098. Josiah Willard to JE, 10/19/51. MA Archives, 13:262.

Boston Octobr. 19. 1751.

Sir

I have herewith inclosed a Lettr written by Order of the General Court to the Inhabitants of Stockbridge which is (in Part) an Answer to your Petition. I have covered it to Coll: Ephraim Williams as the principal Gentleman in the your Town: Which When you have read it please to seal & deliver it with the inclosed Note if you think it necessary.

I must beg you’d excuse me that this matter has been delayed so long: I never knew a single Sillable of it till several days after the Rising of the Court when I came to engage[?] the Minutes of Assembly, It having been transacted in my Absence. I heartily pray the Divine Blessing on yr

important Mission; & remain with great Respect

Sir Your very humble Servt

P.S. Please to give mine & my Wifes kind Respects to Mrs Edwards

Revd. Mr. Jona. Edwards

## B100. Letter from Samuel Hopkins, March 11, 1752 B100.S.Hopkins-JE 3-11-52 edited

Sheffield March 11. 1752.

Rev. Sir,

I have lately received the enclosed Line from the rev. mr. Bellamy; which I send to you, because the thing propos’d must be decided by you. It is a Matter of Indifference with me, whether the Time be postponed or not: but I conclude it is not so with you, for, if I remember right you chose the first of May. when the Matter was concluded upon at Stockbridge; and rather chose the Meeting Should be Sooner, were it not for the Difficulties of Riding & Horse=Keeping. I shall be oblig’d to Mr Edwards if he will inform me, by the first Opportunity, whether he complies with this Proposal of Mr Bellamy’s or not. for I expect an Opportunity to Send to him in a short Time. I am

your humble Servant, Samll Hopkins Rev. Mr Edwards.

## B104. Letter from Aaron Burr (Draft), July 13, 1752 B104.A.Burr-JE 7-13-52 edited

Aaron BurrB104. Aaron Burr to JE, n.d. [7/13/52]. ANTS, Aaron Burr Letterbook, ND1, #2.

Revd evr hd & dr Sr Fathr

We at la now must part wt or worthy & dear Mother whose Coma[^363-note1] has been both pleasant & profitable to us.

We should insist much on her tarrying longer did we know how much she is desrd & wanted at Home. - May she have a prosperous Journey to you by ye Will [of God][^363-note2] And be long preserved a Comfort to you & Blessing to us & ye World.

I could not let ye Opportunity pass without a Line as a token of Respect tho whatevr I have to communicate you will hear in a more agreable manr -

I cease not daily to bless God for the desirable Prospect there is yt my Relation to yr Daughter will make my Life more Comfortable & usefull and twill be my Study & endeavour yt it shall [be][^363-note3] hers also. - I am Abundantly confirm’d in the Opn[^363-note4] I form’d of her yt she is eminently qua:ified to be an extensive Blessg in the Statn God has now placed her in - And tis I am persuaded tis her earnest Prayr & const[^363-note5] Desire yt she may be so - Not only a Sense of Duty, but the Sincerest Affectn will dispose me always to treat her with all the Respect, Fondss & Kindss wc lies in my Power. - And I am satisfd I shall meet wt all the good Treatment from her as I could wish - We depend on seeing you here sometime in Augst -

I have sent the Review &c And shall [^363-note6] be glad from Time to Time to communicate any Thing new. -

We greatly need yr Prayer - That God would keep us hul[^363-note7] & thankfll in Prosty[^363-note8] - give hearts prepared for Trials & give secure us agst Temps[^363-note9] - and Make us Blessings in ye World.

[^363-note2]: Burr’s omission.

[^363-note3]: Burr’s omission.

## B105. Letter from Elisha Williams, August 19, 1752 B105.E.Williams-JE 8-19-52 edited

Elisha WilliamsB105. Elisha Williams to JE, 8/19/52. RIHS, Ms. v. VI, p. 1. Copy in hand in Ephraim Williams.

Stockbridge Augt: 19th 1752

Reverend Sir

I have yrs of yesterday; and Sorry for the Accident you speak of as to the mannar of My Letters Coming to you which was Accidentally dropped by ye Servant who was orderd to carry it to you which and after searching for it was told an Indian had Taken it Up and Carried to you - and proved too Ignorant of the Duty of going and Acquainting you with it - of which Accident as Soon as it Came to my Knowledge I sent a Kindsman to you to Inform you of it - Which was done before yr Letter Came from you - But I did Not Imagine the Genuine and Natural meaning of my Letter would have been so Inverted as appears to me is done in yrs - you are pleased to say I took the Matter very wrong in Speaking of an Interview, with Colo Dwight my Uncle & Capt Kellogg - and say you did Not Single out those Names adding - which Wou'd have been to Exclude others Concerned. - You your Self Sr Spoke of Misunderstanding s between yr Self my friends here and Capt Kellogg by Name and by Expressions you Used in speaking of it - I did suppose Colo Dwight also was one between whom & yr Self their was Some Misunderstanding between all whom I Earnestly wished a good Understanding might Take Place. - and did suppose yr Self also desir'd it, and Mentiond Such an Interview - with view to such an End. - when I spake therfore of an Interview in the beginning of my Letter with those Persons by Name I had No thought of any Interview but with all Parties Concerned. If you Knew of Any others concerned, it was with you to Mention or have yr presence. - It Never Enter'd into my Head to prescribe to you, or to desire ye Exclusion of any Such. It was an Entire and thorough reconciliation which was in my desire by an Interview of Contending Parties - who if they Shou'd Come together with Candid Dispositions (as I hoped they wou'd ) by free and open Conversation did think they might find out a way to have their Misunderstandings removed and a Happy Harmony Effected. - and why you Shou'd speak of such an Interview before Me as a Judge or Mediatour as you do again & again - and fetch your reasons from that Consideration against that Interview it self, when I had from the Beginning disclaimed such a thought - Expressly told you I did Not desire Even to be Present at Such an Interview - Unless desir'd by yr Self as well as them, is to me Very strange - Contentions I Hate and am grieved yt Any Such thing Shou'd Take Place between my Friends here & their Minister by which his Usefulness to them Might be prevented &c. and it has been only with a Friendly design that I have moved any thing Shou'd be done to procure (as I hoped) Peace & Love - If all is Misconstrued I Cant help it. - you are Really Mistaken Sr when you say I desir'd an accot of you of the Misunderstandings that had here subsisted. - it was you sp0ke of them - after I Asked you If you had any weighty reasons against Mrs Dwights having the Charge of ye female Indian School to which she had been Appointed: and had no further thought then of a free Converse on that Subject which you declin’d, and spoke of the Interview above referred to - & which also by yr former Letter I percieved you declined - I therefore resumed that particular Point Since you had Said in that Letter you was full in it - that for Mrs Dwight to Undertake the Care of a Female Boarding School wou'd in no wise answer ye design or Expectation of the Society London with regard to Such a School: - and since they had appointed Her to be the mistress of yt School - my Self also to be one of their Commissrs & had desired me to Come to this place and Acquaint My Self as fully as Might be with regard to ye Indian Affairs & I promised them so to do. - I supposed it my Duty to Inquire of you after ye reasons of [^364-note1] such a Judgment of yours. - For though She was Appointed by them - It was with her to Accept or refuse it. - and if Cou'd Know of any Good Reason against it her Taking that Charge I had Good reason to believe I Cou'd prevent it, as I think My self in such Case my duty to Endevour it. - I therefore did & yet do suppose I have a right to know the reasons of that Jud[g]ment of yours, as I Said in my former Letter - as I stand in such a relation to yt affair which I mentioned as the Ground of it, I have a right to be informed - And for you to turn aside from the plain & Obvious Meaning of the Word - and Tell me you did Not know I was vested with such an high Authority &c is So Trifling & such Treatment as did it determinate on your Self, I imagine you woud think Injurious - Indeed I think that She as a Christian standing in the relation she does to you has right to know those reasons. - You Cant suppose I had reference to such reasons as you intimate Might possably be in your Mind which ought to be their Concealed - Nor is it to be suppos'd your reasons in this Case are of such an Nature since you speak afterward of your rediness to give them to the Commissioners if Called to it - and let me add I think it is Acting the part of ye man & ye Christian to let her know the reasons or my self - that I may have an oppertunity to prevent her Entring on yt Charge if it ought to be done & So prevent a Publick Declaration of them to ye Commissioners which if of any weight to set her aside from that Employ Must at least tend to her disrepute - of whose reputation you have professed to have so tender regard & when you Intimate yt I thought well of your giving those reasons before such as might be present at such an Interview. I had been desireous of. - You are Mistaken theirin - I thought of No such thing, Nor Cou'd I Conceive any Occation for it; the only thing I Said with regard to that was of your letting me Know them - who you Suppos'd had such a respect for her that I was not likely to Injure her - as to What you are plesed to say Concerning my Conversation with Mrs Ed-ds tho the Charge runs prety high & Augmented by several Agravated circumstances yet meerly as a personal thing I had over Lookt it. - but for a pravailing hope that as it is Easy to make appear Apparent your Constructions & resentments Concerning it were entirely Groundless - your Mind may be dispos'd to apprehend the Same more than possable Concerning many things handed to you relateing to or Coming from others - & who in Consequence of such Constructions & resentments you Account & Treat Inimical Unto you. - I hope, Sir it will not furnish out fresh Accusation against me if I Say I Cannot but in Justice to you suppose yt Accot you had of ye Conversation was an Imperfect one - and yt had you been Acquainted with what gave rise to those words you Mentioned as So Obnoxious & Injurious & What Imediately followed after with which I thought yt Little affair hand[^364-note2] Ended, Not only would you Not have Treasur'd up & thus discover'd resentment, against Me on Accot of them, but had Never felt such resentments at all - the fact stands Sr Just thus Mrs Ed-ds had taken Occasion to introduce into Conversation NHampton affairs & perticularly the Controversy Concerning the admission of members into Chh fellowship - in which she asserted to be one part of Mr Stoddards Principles to admit all sorts of Persons and that it was the Duty of all (Enumerating at the Same time Many black Carracters) to Come to the Lords Table [upon][^364-note3][^364-note4] which I indeed did replie Madm You Must Know better. Mr St-d has plainly declared in his book on that Subject his Sentiments were yt none but Visable Saints ought to be Admitted - Upon which Mrs Edwards Said She did Not Know For for she had never read the Book - where Upon I immediately replied - then Madm I Ask beg your Pardon I took it for granted you had read it when I Used those words - and Mrs Ed-ds going on to Express some resentment another Person added it was Natural to suppose you had read Mr Stoddards Book as the Controversy was on [-] foot in that Place - this Sr is the faithfull and Naked Account & of which if Needfull there are Several vouchers & among them (one at least if I may Judge by a passage in your first Letter) your Self wou’d not be disposed to [refuse.][^364-note5]

I Am Sir your best well Wisher & Humble Servt Elisha WilliamsCoppy Copy To the Reverend Mr Edwards

[^364-note1]: **marginal.** [2]

[^364-note2]: MS sic; “had.”

[^364-note3]: Conjecture where MS is damaged.

[^364-note4]: **marginal.** [3]

[^364-note5]: Conjecture where MS is damaged.

## B106. Letter from Jasper Mauduit, April 19, 1753 B106.J.Mauduit-JE 4-19-53 edited

Jasper MauduitB106. Jasper Mauduit to JE, 4/19/53. Univ. of Virginia, Alderman Library, New England Company Letterbook, 1688-1761, p. 274.

April 19th: 1753

Mr Jonathn Edwards Sr

Your Lre of Mar. 10th I duely recd, but had not an opportunity to lay it before the Compy till last general Court, wn it was read, & the Compy think themselves oblidg'd to you for the prticular accot. you have given them of our Indian affairs at Stockbridge. I have given Mr Oliver & the Commissrs, ye Compys thots upon ye whole affair, to whose directions you will of course attend, in ye mean time as blankets were desired at Stockbridge for the Mohawks & wth a View to promote the female School, a bundle of blankets is ordd to our Commissr. Elisha Williams Esqr, I am, heartily wishing you wisdom for a right behavr in ye difficult station providence has placed you in. your humbl servt

Jaspr Mauduit

## B107. Letter from Ephraim Williams, May 2, 1753 B107.E.Williams-JE 5-2-53 edited

Ephraim WilliamsB107. Ephraim Williams to JE, 5/2/53. RIHS, v. VI, p. 2. Copy by Ephraim Williams. Addressed on verso: "A Coppy of letter to Mr / Edwards May 2: 1752 No 2."

Sr,

I receiv'd a line from you of this days date wherein wherein you say "A Complaint has lately Enterd Against me to the Church for Several Things: Then you add These words "Being willing to proceed in the Most Ammicable Manner I desire you wou'd give me with the Two Deacons Woodbridge & Brown Oppertunity for some private Conversation with you About this affair.

Now whither I am to Understand these words "Being willing &c: To refer To refer to the Disposition of the Chh or your Self I am at a Loss; - But being it the disposition of the Chh I thank Them, or if you intend It as yours I Also Return my thanks, - But I hope It is Not inconsistent with that Amicable Manner of procedure you propose, to Inform me of the Several Things Complained of Against me, and who the Informer, Some little Time at least before you Desire my Answer - Either in private Either in private Conversation with your Self & Deacons or otherwise - you Say they are lately Enterd against me by this Expression I am led to Suppose that they are Articles which I never heard of and so are Not Contain'd Among those for which I have been Debarred of your & the Chhs  for Several Months past - I hope therefore I Shall not be Blamed If I decline as I do any procedure in this affair on my part Either by way of private Conversation with your Self & Deacons or Otherwise under present Circumstances - but I Shall be Glad to be properly Informed of the Just Grounds Upon which the Chh have Debarred me of their Communion or and the New Articles of Complaint against me If such their are and as Soon as I am So Informed - I hope I shall be readily Disposed wherein I have given Just Cause of Offence to make all Christian Sattisfaction

I am with all due respect- Reverd Sr your Most obet: Humbl Servt Eph Williams

The Revr'd Mr Jonathan Edwards

## B108. Letter from Joseph Dwight (Fragment), July 3, 1753 B108.J.Dwight-JE 7-3-53 edited

Joseph DwightB108. Joseph Dwight to JE, 7/3/53. RIHS, Ms. #1146. Fragment (bottom of pp. 1 and 2).

[ …] have to Query - Is It consistent with Christianity In Stockbridge Chh publickly & by Their Vote to withdraw their Charity so far, as to put such a Suspension upon Me, without acquainting me That any Matters of Complaint were laid in with Them against Me, or That They were in the least uneasy at any part of my Conduct? -

Query was not this Act of theirs a publick Censure of Me, & in measure an Excommunication, or of the Nature of it? -

Query was It not more inconsistent with Christianity for you & the Chh to do this, when I was present with

[ …] Mr Edwards without alledging one single Word of what Was said or done d in this State of the Case who can tell Whither to speak something said to be spoken or do something said to be done be a moral Good or moral Evill for my own part I am inconscious of any Such Evill said or done by me against Mr Eds & If you Sr & yor Chh who censure me will not inform how shall I ever know? or how are you acting the part of Christianity, wch obliges to proper Endeavours to work Repentance & Reformation in an offending Brother? - will a Rod reform

A

## B109. Letter from Aaron Burr (Draft), [c. Early Fall 1753] B109.A.Burr-JE c edited

Aaron BurrB109. Aaron Burr to JE, n.d. draft [c. fall 1753?]. ANTS, Burr Letterbook.

Revd Hond & dr Sr

The Affr of Mrs Sergts Letter has perplexed Me beyong[^368-note1] all ye Bounds of Reason. I do not know yt so trifling affrs ever gave Me So much Concern - Not yt they I have ye least Difficulty abt Clearing Mothr & my Wife, for for yy are Clear. & I can wt grt Freedm own my Self ye Author of yt Report - But tis not so easy to clear my Self from Blame. The impartial World wn they Compare ye Report with ye Letter, will condemn me and my own Cons. condemn me of acting contrary to ye golden Rule - I have done as I would other Should be done by - - And I am persuaded if Should try to Justify my Self, I Should give ym a Handle agst me & expose my Char - But what grieves me most is 1. That I did not take a Cop of yt Lettr; being in a Hurry & imagining there was no Need. - But She will expose her Self if She refuses to Shew it to you or any Body yt desires it - I well remember ye only Sentence in it wc related to yt Affr, I think, ye very Words. It was in Answer to my having Congratulated her on y her designed Marriage Thus. viz. "As to what you Say concerning a Certain Gentm if there Should be Occasion Such a Thing Should be (wc wants Proff or considerable Proof.) I hope your Wishes will take Effect" - What made me think She would not Show it, was the Respect exprest in [^368-note2] it to me - But tis too mean for me to take Notice of yt - There is Nothing in ye Letter yt will Justify my Saying what I did And you know in ye Eyes of ye World it has a Mean Look to expose any thing from in a private Letter - Tully Says &c.

The mean & disingenuous Conduct to Madm & my Wife, don’t make at all ye more excu but Serves to convince Me what Sort of a Woman She is - And Makes me more Carefull to do Nothg for wc She can reproach me in ye Eyes of ye World. -

I thought my Duty as a Christian & a Regard to my Reputation, obliged me to Say as much as I have by Way of Reflection on my Conduct - Notwithstanding her fair Pretences as to me. I have no Depen but She will represent me in all the bad Colours She can - And if I Should try to Justify my Self it would give her a fair Handle - I don’t feel ye least Restraint abt injuring hurting her but what arise from ye Rules of the Gospel.

2. But what most concern me is a Fear, least what I have Said will not please you & Mothr I can only Say yt there is no Person in ye O I am so much concerned to approve my Self to (exct ye W. of my Boisom) And if I have not done it in this Affr tis not for Want of most eart Desire to do it.

I think I have fully cleard Mr & my Wife [^368-note3] from being ye Author of yt Rept. - And so far as it concerns me (tho I expect a good Deal of Reproach from yt Qur) I Shall be easy abt it, wn I know you are Satisfied - - I believe I have tired you with this Subject; I have my Self very thoroughly - It would have been easier for Me to have composed 4 Serms than have Mrs Sergts Lettr & this Part of yours. - No more write abt.

1. Mr Wife Health - 2 Mr Tennts Voyage - 3. writing to Society - 4. Abt Mr Gordn - 5. Abt his coming to Nk. -

[remainder of page blank]

P.S. [^368-note4] My Lettr not going as I expected I add this P: S: - The Affr of Mrs D is Still a Perplexity to Me - I plainly perceive you dislike my Conduct in yt Affair wc has given Me a great Deal of uneasiness - But as I am fully persuaded in My Cons: that I did wrong in reporting what I did. That there is no Sufft Foundn for it in yr Letter for it

I that Should expose my Self Chr & Friends by attempting to Justify what I Said . - I know not what to do. - If I Should Attempt to expose her by any Thing She Said or did here; - I think it would be Sinfull & returning evil for Evil. - I always canot but think, that Some like what I have wrote is most likely to vindicate my Friends & self from her unreasonable . - However tis the Way in wc I Shall feel the most Peace.

[^368-note1]: Ms sic; “beyond.”

## B110. Letter from Nathaniel Hazard, December 19, 1753 B110.N.Hazard-JE 12-19-53 edited

Nathaniel HazardB110. Nathaniel Hazard to JE, 12/19/53. MHS, Sedgwick, II, 7-5. One folio sheet. Countersigned by JE on bottom of verso, "Mr. Hazzard decem. 19. / 53."

New York, Decemr. 19th. 1753.

Revd. Sir

By the advice and direction of the Revd. Mr. John Smith of Rye, (who sends his kind respects to you and Mrs. Edwards) and from yor. known disposition & endeavours to promote the Interest of the Redeemer’s Kingdom in the Most extensive manner you can. I presume to request your Charitable aid and assistance in getting the Revd. Mr. Bellamy removed from Connecticut and settled among us in New York. I suppose you will have heard before this reaches you, that both our Ministers are dismissed at their own request, and that we had sent for Mr. Bellamy here, where he preached six extraordinary Sermons; since which Mr. Pemberton is removed to Boston, to the People that gave him a Call when there last fall or Summer, but before he Embarked, he hear’d all Mr. Bellamy’s Sermons, & got fully acquainted with him, as he Lodged him in his House. All our Ministers this way, as well as Mr. Pemberton, Mr. Cummings, Mr. Lawyer Smith & our Congregation in General, thin[k] Mr. Bellamy the only Man for New York. Mr. President Burr was with us chief part of last Week, and Encourages very much, says he will do his utmost for us, as well as all the Presbytry, and think we shall Succeed. There has been proper pains taken to know that this is fully the mind of the People and Mr. Bellamy himself cannot but be sensible of it, notwithstanding he greatly discourages us in using any Means to Seek after him, his Reasons for which I immagine are his great regard for his people, his respect to his adjacent Brethren in the Ministry, and his present state of Tranquility, &c. all which Reasons, and as many more, if of no greater weight, I humbly conceive you will deem insufficient when compared with the crying necessity and importance of his Labours in this City, as well as an undoub[t]ed prospect of his having an extensive influence all around us, in our Presbyteries, Synods and Colledges &c. I am not insensible it will require selfdenyal in Mr. Bellamy, as well as Zeal for Public Good. This Revd. si[r], when you duly consider our Case, I trust you will find freedom to excite him to, as well as Answer his Objections and press upon him a Sutable sense of Duty in the Case. Revd. sir, you Will excuse my freedom in the present affair: was I interceding with you for Riches or Honours, I might justly blush & esteem my self impertinent, but as I am for my self persuaded it is the Cause of the Redeemer, I have freedom to intreat your engaging in it for Christ’s Sake. And as the Chief or Main Difficulty is to prevail on Mr. Bellamy, his people, & his bretheren the Ministers of that Association to consent to his Removal to Us, so I doubt not from Your using Your intrest with him and Influence with them, we Shall soon feel the good Effects of your Pious & Charitable Labours for us, and [v.] you have the Satisfaction in Your own breast of having been greatly Instrumental of Serving the Common Cause of our Redeemer.

With best Respect, I am Revd. Sir Your most humble servt Nathl. Hazard

P.S. Mr. Smith Desir’d me to excuse his not writing to you for want of time, but says he will also Write to Mr. Bellamy and his Brethren, and is much engaged in our behalf.

## B111. Letter from Ephraim Williams and "Aggrieved Brethren of Stockbridge Church, April 6, 1754 B111.E.Williams-JE 4-6-54 edited

Ephraim Williams and "Aggrieved Brethren of Stockbridge (Mass.) ChurchB111. Ephraim Williams et al to JE and Stockbridge Church, 4/6/54. RIHS.

To The Revd Mr Jonathan Edwards Pastor of the Chh in Stockbridge to be Communicated to the Said Chh -

Revd Sr It was with Some Surprise, we read your message of November 19th, your Severe Resentments at Some Expressions used by us in our remonstrance; and what (we must Confess) added to our Surprise, and in Some measure Interrupted our Serious Consideration; was our finding the Revd Pastor & Chh had fallen Into the Same Error (If it be an Error) they were Condemning in us (viz) Suggesting to us, that we have been guilty of Grossly abusing abus the Chh of Stockbridge; and that we are Chargable with the most Glaring absurdity; and that upon ye foundation of Such a Glaring absurdity, we go on to treat the Church In a reflecting & reproachfull manner; Stiling our reasoning Taunting Language; and again your Suggesting to us that we treat ye Church in an assuming manner; Interspersing here & there, in Invidious & Supercilious Language, Censorious Suggestions & insinuations. Might we not Justly think Sr that whilst your were reprimanding us, for Expressions which were harsh; that you would have been Cauteous of avoiding the unhappy mistake: for we Cant but think those Sacred texts; Rom 2:1 I:21: have Some relation to the Conduct of ministers & Chhs, as well as others - but least you think we would Excuse our selves upon this foot; we frankly own, it is no Excuse for us, If we have been Criminal, that you have been so too; tho’ we do not at present Determin, that Either of us have been so - we therefore now proceed to offer a few a few things, in Vindication of our selves, in using the Expressions you Except against; and with respect to them we Say; we don’t Charge them upon the Pastor, and Chh, any further then the principle they Seemed to us, by their votes to Set up oblidged us to - we had Signified our Dissatisfaction with The Pastor and Chh; and had desired that our Grievances, might be heard and and Decided by an Ecclesiastical Council; the Chh refused to gratifie us, and by their votes as appeared to us, Claimed a Prerogative, of Determining the Cause Themselves. It its true true they offered us, to Refer the Consideration of our Grievance, to the Honble Commissioners but at the Same time, Signified to us, that they had a right to Judge the Matter themselves.

And at least Intimated to us, that they would, unless we Complied with [^370-note1] Their proposal of referring to the Commiss Commissioners; This Was Excepted against to us matter of offence; we Except therefore against both the priniciple and proposal, & Supposed we had a right to do So. But Especially against the Chh’s right, to Set as Judges, it being their own Case; we argued upon this point only, to Shew & Expose the Nakedness & absurdity of pretending to Such a Right. We Humbly Repesented what face the Setting up Such a principle Reflected up upon our minds; and Could not but think, others would view it in ye Same light with us - but now Sr If we are mistaken and the Chh By their votes do not Claim Such authority; as you Seem to Intimate in your written message that the [ ]: our Controversy is so far at an End with them, for our observations and arguings were all founded (as is manifest) upon the Supposition, that the Chh had by their latter of their votes Claimed Such power which[?] you Say Sr to Shew, that the Chh did not Claim Such a power, Shall be perticularly Examined by & by.

At present we would only observe, that upon the Supposition the votes of the Chh do give us ground to Conclude, they Claimed Such a right, as we have Supposed they did; our observations, and reasonings which you Except against must we think, in the very letter of them, be vindicated, by the Common Sense of mankind - the principles we Supposed the Chh had by their votes Set up, appeard to us Ridiculous (If you will pardon the Expression) we attempted to Expose the nakedness, and absurdity of them. And tho’t our Selves Justifiable in doing So; & Should have Suspected you Sr, the least of any man, as finding faulty with us for it; after reading your declared opinion upon this point, in your Book Entitled misrepresentations Corrected &c for in the first page of your Preface you Say - I Desire that it may be Justly Considered by the reader, what is, and what is not Injurious and unhandsome treatment of an author, in a Controversy: And here I woud Crave leave to Say, that I Humbly concieve, a Distinction ought to be made, between opposing & Exposing a Cause, Or the arguments used to Defend it, and reproaching persons. he is a Weak writer, Indeed (you Say) who undertakes to Confute an opinion, but Dares not to Expose the nakedness & absurdity of it; nor the weakness And Inconsistence of the Methods taken and arguments used by any To maintain it, for fear he Should be guilty of Speaking Evil of those Things, and be Charged with reproaching them. If an antagonist is angry [^370-note2] At this, he thereby gives his readers too much occasion of Suspicion towards himself, as Chargable with weakness or bitterness now Sr have we done any thing more then to Expose the nakedness and absurdity of the principles, Set up by your votes, and to Shew, the weakness & Inconsistence of the methods taken, and arguments used, to maintain them and does this deserve the names of Taunting, Invidious Supercilious Language, you your Self being Judge. & for you Sr to be angry at Us for doing this (and we Cant th but think you was in Some little Degree of temper, when you wrote your message to us; If we adopt, And your own Sentiments and Expressions affords us to much occasion Of Suspicion towards you as Chargable with weakness or bitterness.

Nay Sr had we gone further then we have done, & taken full liberty in this respect, and represented this matter, So as that it might be vewed Justly in all its nakedness; yea Should we now Shew further, how the badness of [-] your Cause, as we apprehend; oblidges you to be Inconsistent, with your Self, Inconsistent with your own professed principles, and with things Conceded, and asserted, in the book above referred to; we Should be apt to think our selves Excusable, before you; Since, you have taught us to think, that this would be So far from Injurious treatment that Should we be afraid to do it, and to do it as thoroly as we Could . we must look upon our Selves to be foolish.

But we proceed now as we proposed, to Consider what you offer, to Convince us that the votes of the Chh, gave us no ground, to Conclude, that they Claimed a power to Determin, and Isue the matter of our Complaint themselves - you are pleased to Say, noting Can be more manifest, then that the Chh, in thus Expressing themselves Conditionally, avoid Saying or giving the the least Intimation, whether they think these things Should be finally Issued by themselves, or no - Answer. we never Disputed whether the Ch might not aim to wave any Positive Determination of that matter; for the time (viz) whether our Complaint Should be finally Issued by them, or no) and Indeed they Could Scarce do other wise, after they had voted to give us a hearing, before the Commissioners &c: but that they did avoid giving us the least Intimation, that we must abide their own Decision, If we rejected their proposal of referring to the Commissioners; we think far from being manifest at all; and this is all we Ever Suggested.

Here Sr let us Examine, whether the votes of the Chh do not manifestly [^370-note3] give us Such Intimations as these. we often find the Chh in these votes, Speaking of themselves as JUDGES of these things, and JUDGES to give JUDGMENT upon these things, and Speak of it as Dubious, whether the JUDGMENT of these things would be referred, to any OTHER JUDGES besides THEMSELVES. when we ought to lay our reasons, and produce our Evidences, to Support our Charge. that they are Such Judges, as have an undoubted right to Insist on this, and AUTHORITY to require it; and that whether it be Supposed to be proper that the Chh Should act as DECISIVE JUDGES in the affair or no: and this method of Stile Sr, you Seem to be fond of, for we find you Continuing it, in your late message; where you Say, as to our joining with you in referring the matter of your Complaints to other Judges besides the Chh . and tell us, that we must appear be[fore] the Chh, & Exhibit our Evidences and give the Chh opportunity to Interrogate &c before any Such Step Can be taken, as you propose: (that is) refering the matters of our grevance, to a Council (If it Ever be taken) Intim Intimating, that it was matter of great Doubt, and uncertainty, wh whether the Church would ever, give us that liberty; but it Seems that it is most manifest, that all this, Carries in it, not the least Intimation, that the Chh Claims a power to Determin and Issue the matter of our Complaints themselves. Suppose one Neighbour, or Brother, objects a Scandal, against another, and Desires of him Satisfaction, or Desires him to refer it &c: Should we hear hear upon it the person accused, upon it, thus Expressing himself: If the Judgment of these things be referred to any other Judges, besides my Self: and whether I yield that your objections, Should be Carried to the Chh, or a Council, or ANY OTHER JUDGES beside MYSELF or no . and that Such & Such things he has authority to require: whether it be Supposed, to be proper that he Should act as a Decisive Judge, in the affair or not. would it be most manifest, in Such a Case, that the accused avoided giving the least Intmations, of his Setting up his rights of Judging, and deciding the matter of the accusation? on the other hand, does not the Language Convey, Such Intimations in a very Strong manner, and give Just ground to Infer Such a Conclusion; and tho’ the thing thus Conditionally Expressed might Shew him at present undetermined Whether it were a point of prudence, or the most fit and proper[^370-note4] method of Issuing the matters of grievance, acting by HIMSELF acting as a DECISIVE JUDGE in the affair; yet would not his words manifestly Imply, that he has that Authority and may Improve that right If he pleases? and that it may be Expected he will do it, unless Some other measures be Come Into, to him more agreeable, and Should this unaccountable oddity be represented to him, in all its nakedness yea tho, it were done as thoroly, as the Complainants Could do it for his Conviction; Could he with propriety or Justice Charge him hereupon with Taunting language &c? and would not his being angry at it, Give to much occasion of Suspicion towards himself, as Chargable with weakness or bitterness? or would it be any Sufficient vindication of himself, Should he Say, that his giving the least Intimation of Such a thing Implyed Implied the most Glaring absurdity, and that nothing Can be more manifest then that he in Expressing himself thus thus Conditionally, avoided Saying, or giving the least Intimation, whether he tho’t the matter of Charge Should be finally Issued by himself or no - Such a Conditional way of Expressing himself would Indeed Seem to Intimate he was at present Some what unresolved whether to act as a Decisive Judge in the affair himself or whether he Should refer it to Some other Decision

________________________________________________________________

* these are the words Interlined: Being represented as hinting, that he has a right, to Determin and Issue matters of Controversy himself -

________________________________________________________________

as to what you Say under your 9th perticular, which Comes next under our Consideration, in order, we observe, that tho’ you Seem to offer at Some thing to Convince us, that we ought to lay before Church the reasons and Evidences by which we Expected to Support our Complaints; because you had Cited ,those of us who had absented from the Sacrament, before we had offered the reasons of our absenting &c: you Seem to lay great wait upon this, and by the time you Spend upon it, and the manner of your writing, to Conclude, that If all the rest Should fail, this must Stand the most Impartial Examination, and Secure the whole, you have Insisted on: and Indeed Sr our Eye was fixed upon it with no Small attention, but upon Examination, we found it utterly Insufficient, to afford the least measure, or Degree of Conviction; for be the Case as you Suppose; that you had a right to know what we had to offer in vindication of our Conduct, in absenting &c: we would Humbly ask: That when the Chh of Stockbridge, with their Revd Pastor, Came[^370-note5] to be Informed, that the reason of our absenting, was matter of Scandalous offence; that lay with us against Pastor & Chh: that they had a right to Demand of us the reasons and Evidences, we had to Support the Charge Exhibited; unless they had a right to act as Judges: and the Case (notwithstanding, they were the party accused) properly lay before them, to Judge and act upon: and tho’ you pretend to Claim a right to judging; yet as you have never offered us the least Shew of reason to Support Such a right; as we are Humbly of the opinion, it is Impossible for you to do it, it being not only repugnant to reason, but Contrary to the universal Sentiment of mankind: we beg leave to Conclude, (that had we not Exhibited the reasons of our absenting &c; previous to your voting, and Sending unto us a Citation of appear before the Chh; to lay before them the reasons and Evidences of the Charge Exhibited &c:) we Can not be judged Criminal in refusing but we would further observe; the great mistake you have fallen into, in representing as putting in our Complaint, to Bar the Citation of the Church. when it is Evident, that our Complaint was laid before the Chh, previous to the Chhs voting, or Citing us to give the reasons of our withdrawing from the Sacraments, as will appear by Examining the Dates the respective papers bear; our Complaint bearing Date August 3d 1753; and your Citation So late as Septr 8th 1753.

2: the letter of your votes & message: which is as follows - This is to Inform you, that it was voted by the Chh at their meeting the last Tuesday that they Desire and Expect that you Should appear before the Chh the next Tuesday at my house &c: to lay before the Chh the reasons and Evidences by which you Justifie, the Charges you have lately publickly Exhibited, against the Chh and more Especially against the Pastor, and Some of the members; & also that the Chh then Expects, to hear, the reasons why you have lately absented &c. So that the very nature, and letter of your votes, & messages Shews, the falshood of the foundation of all your argument upon this head; we must therefore beg leave again to Conclude; that all the undoubted RIGHT the Chh had to Insist upon our laying, the reasons and Evidences of our Charge before them; and their authority to Demand it; built upon a false foundation, must with its Support, fall to the ground - as to what you Say under the 3d head we are not able to Comprehend the Inconsistency you Charge us with; for we Can’t See how we Contradict our Selves in asking, whether it was Honest to object the peculiar State of the Chh, as a reason you Could not join with us in Calling a Council, when it was Evident this was no objection to the Chhs acting in the other Case mentioned, we therefore Determined that we had reason to Conclude, that the objection against [^370-note6] Joining &c: founded on the peculiar State of the Chh was really no objection bec because the Chh paid no regard to it themselves; nor is our saying, we think it Evident, by the votes of the Chh that they Claim a power of Determining and Issuing the matters of Complaint themselves, at all Inconsistent with our asking, whether it be honest, to make Such an objection; for If this be the Case [-] the objection must We apprehend be y [-] and your Claiming this power, would be utterly Inconsistent with your making the objection, but as you are fond of fastening Contradictions upon us; you proceed to tell us under the 4th perticular that our Conduct, is not Consistent with our pretences - we have no Suspicions, that in our Conduct that we have Contradicted what we pretended; tho’ we are very Sensible, we have Contradicted what you have pretended, was our Duty (viz) to lay, the reasons and Evidences of our Complaints before the Chh, in which you Seem to Suppose the Inconsistence of our Conduct with our pretences lies; but we would Seriously ask? whether we Ever pretended, to lay our maters before you as an Ecclesiastical Judicature? whether we Ever pretended, to Submit them Even to the hearing of the Chh in that Shape? you Can’t but be Sensible, that we utterly Disclaimed this, and all ways Supposed the Church had no right, to act and Judge upon them in that Capacity . it is therefore Surprising to us, that you Should Suggest as you do under the 5th perticular; that our practice is Inconsistent, with our professed Desire to have the matters of offence removed: Can’t we heartily Desire thus? unless we Submit to lay the matters of Complaint before the Chh as Judges must we Concede that the Pastor and Chh are have a right to judge and determin in whether they are Innocent or guilty of the Charges we have Exhibited against them or fall unde the Imputation of Hypocrisy in professing a desire to have the matters of offence removed Can their be no other way of making our Desire manifest, but the method you Seemed to point the reasons and Evidences of our Charge before you, in the Shape you Contend for? must we concede? that the Pastor & Chh. have a right to require us as Judges (which is the Character you So Zealously Contend for) to have the Evidences Exhibited and give to Interrogate us upon them? or fall under the Imputation of Hypocrisy, in Professing a desire to have the matters of offence removed: we apprehend your reasoning under this perticular would humbly propose, whether your reasoning under this perticular, is not forreign to the points you have Set up (viz) your acting as Judges having power to Call us to an account, having a right to Demand of us, the reasons and Evidences of our Complaints; to Interrogate &c: & whether you were not Extreamly Streightned, for arguments & finally, whether you were not [^370-note7] Extreamly Confused - what you observe to us under your 7th perticular, we are Humbly of the opinion, Serves rather to fill up the Number of perticulars, then to add force to your reasons, against Complying with our Desire, of a Council &c. for is it not Evident the persons perticularly mentioned in the Complaint, are Included, in the Greater part of your Chh, we Say we have Special reason to be offended with, for making & publishing & afterwards Exhibiting, to the General Court a libellous Writing, Containing many, & various falshoods &c. why may we not then reasonably Expect, that ye their Case, So far as they have been Concerned in the affair of the libellous Writing, be Carried to a Council? what greater reason have to Excuse themselves, that the other members of the Chh, Can they do it? because we apprehend, they are more Especially Criminal in two things relating to that affair (viz) mentioned in they being as we apprehend d principle agents, in Contriving, promoting making & publishing Said libellous Writing.

2ly: that they, or Some by their procurement & privily, did forge & Counterfit the hand of Jona Devereux, by putting his name to the Said libellous writing with out his Consent or privily: ought they to be Excused, because they are Charged with more bad actions in the affair then Some of the other members? the reason Certainly Seems to be on other side or Can it be Supposed that the Chh have a right to judge and act upon those bad actions Certainly, If it be reasonable for us to Expect, that that Case, in which we apprehend the greater part of the Chh are Concerned, be Carried Immediately to a Council; it Cannot be unreasonable for us to Expect, that that those things mentioned, which, If true, rendered the Conduct of Some of the members much more Criminal, in that affair, be also laid before the Same Judges. and we would humbly offer, whether it is not reasonable to Expect, that Since you have Solemnly taken those brethren as you say under your Care, that in stead of doing anything to Screen them from a fair tryal, before proper Judges, that you Set before them, the reasonableness of Submitting the matter of our Complaints, in its Circumstances to a Council - And upon the whole Sr, as it manifestly appears to us, the Chh have no business, to set as Judges upon this our Complaint, we are under no obligation to appear before them, to lay you reasons &c by which we Expect to Support it, this Shall be done, in proper Season when the Case Comes to be laid before proper Judges - we are willing we We Trust, to do what is proper or becoming us to do, as Christians, wishing [^370-note8] the prosperity & peace of the Chh in Stockbridge. but as we have Exhibited our Complaint against the Pastor & Chh; we Esteem it their Duty, to Come to us, & Seek to give us Satisfaction, and not Cite and Require us authoritively, to Come and lay before them our reasons &c. and If upon their Coming they fail to give us Satisfaction, that they Consent and agree with us, to Refer the Consideration of our Greivance to an Ecclesiastical Council, mutually Chosen, who may hear and Decide the matter for us: which being agreed upon, we Stand ready to give them a Copy of all the charges particularly, we shall Exhibit against them, & Endeavour to Support before the Council. and thus we Shall be ready to do at any Seasonable time before their Session; that So Pastor & Chh may have opportunity, to Examine them and prepare to vindicate - we are we Say free to do this and as we Can’t but think this the most fit and proper method to be taken, so we Judge the most likely, to Settle the Difficulties Subsisting, and bring both you and us to a right understanding of things; but as to our appearing before the Chh, as a Judicature in this affair, we utterly Refuse it: nor will our meeting them as a body, Especially at first, Ever (as we think) be likely to Issue the affair; we shall be in Danger of provoking Each others tempers and advantage may be taken of words dropt in that Heat of Spirits; and So the breach widened rather then healed: as our writings are resented by you we have Some reason to fear that our words will be much more: words are liable to be missrepresented, and mistakes upon this head are too Common, as we have Experienced Since this Controversy began: but writings are not Exposed to this Hazzard, they will Speak for them selves the Same Language at all times - We pray you Sr to lay this our message before the Chh, that they may have opportunity, Either to Close with or Reject our proposal within mentioned & offered. & you will oblidge your Aggrieved Brethren & Friends - Stockbridge April 6:th 1754

## B112. Letter from Joseph Hawley, January 21, 1755 B112.J.Hawley-JE 1-21-55 edited

Joseph HawleyB112. Joseph Hawley to JE, 1/21/55. Draft. NYPL, Hawley Papers, no. 36.

Revd. Sr.

I recd. yours of Novr 18th for which I am much oblidged to you, and am So far from being disgusted at ye freedom and Openess with which you Sr. Treat the affair I wrote to you upon that I receive kindly and thankfully. And If I should not apprehend myself (on Solemn Examination) to be in all respects so guilty and Culpable as you do Sr yet I have thereby diverse particulars Suggested, some of which perhaps I should not so particularly put to my Conscience If they had not been mentioned - In the general I am Sensible that the Affair from the time you first Communicated your different Sentiments, so that it was generally known that you had altered your opinion, to the Time of your leaving the Town, There was a great deal of Censoriousness and uncharitable Conjecture and a great deal of unchristian heat, and many harsh and bitter Speeches both in private Conversation and in publick meetings appeared among the people a good much of which I was personally knowing to - and altho I have not at present a particular remembrance of all that passed within the Compass of my Observation yet upon Serious reflection I cannot be Conscious to myself that from the beginning to the Time of your ye [ ] what was called the definitive Council, I ever Encouraged or Countenanced any thin or promoted any thing of that Nature (but frequently spoke against and reprehended it) Excepting what you Sr. once mentioned to me viz at one of the first Conferences on ye affair When the Church was Stayed on ye Sabbath in ye meeting house after Exercise When I say said that I apprehended that it was high time ye matter was brought to an Issue; and that it was Necessary that there Should be a Speedy Conclusion of it - or Words to that Effect - Which by the Effect and influence it had on ye minds of many, appeared to be unhappily said, and for which I often have been and am Still Exceeding Sorry and, so far as I can remember was Spoke with an immodest immoderate and irreverend Air - As to what I said at Father Lyman’s before the previous Council- I have Never freely Confess Sr. and own that the Air and Mode of Speaking there was with which Considerable wh of what I said there was delivered was Irreverend immodest derisive and magisterial and Such as very ill became me when arguing with you, who was so much my Superiour in age Station and Accomplishments, and who deserved from me great respect and defference for which I humbly and sincerely ask your forgiveness, and am very Sorry, Not only for that it was far It was disrespectfull to you Sr. But also a very ill Example to others and had a tendency to abate the respect and reverence which the bystanders ought to have maintained in their minds towards and which it was my Duty to have by all means Endeavoured to have maintained and probably had an Influence upon the hearers towards prompting them to a disrespectful and Irreverend treatment of you afterwards But with regard to the Sentiments I then delivered, upon the most Impartial Consideration I have ever been Capable of I have not been able to discover sufficient reason to alter them - and apprehend that If I had declared them in a decent moderate humble manner I Should not have reason to reflect upon myself therefor - and I make no doubt Sr But that If I had opportunity for free and Calm Considerversation upon the matter I could Satisfie you that there was No Inconsistency in what I said before that Council with my wholly declining to Act as the Chhs agent in the matters that were laid before them But there is not room therefor in this letter without being tedious

How far it was my Duty to have Endeavoured to prevent any Steps being taken towards a Separation until the people were brought to a Calm Temper and a Cool Consideration of what you Sr. had to say on your side of the question I am not fully satisfied - I was sincerely desirous and truly endeavour that means might be used and such as Seemed to me most likely that If it were possible there might be an Accommodation & that you Sr. and the people might Continue together Each retaining their respective Sentiments (though I freely Confess I myself coud never see how it could be Accomplished) for that purpose I once Obtained a vote of the Church at a time when you Sr. was not present, for sending for some wise moderate men, who had not interested themselves in the Controversy, who should Concert and propose some method of Accommodation, so that you Sr. and ye people might remain together Consistent with good Conscience on both Sides, But afterwards the vote was reconsidered and reversed - And far It became me to C have Continued Neuter & declined acting as agent for the Chh before the Council which advised to a Separation I am not fully resolved - However I have never been able upon Close Examination to discover that I was Influenced by pride or vanity or any Ill will to you Sr. & yours Nor can I see reason to tax myself with any unfair mangemt. so far as I was Concerned before that Council, nor do I remember that in any thing I treated you Sr. with ye least disrespect and as I proposed the case in its true and Naked state so far as I knew it befor in order to the Council’s devising an Accommodation so I never was at all against it but Should so far as I can recollect always rejoiced at it in any manner Consistent with the sentiments of Each party - It’s true there was a Set of Arguments drawn up in Writing which were read by me and if I remember right Committed to the Council, which were Conceived in Terms which Never were agreable to me, and Some of which I very much disliked - But that was all done by another hand and I had nothing more to do with it than to Copy it and read it to ye Council which was insisted upon that it might not appear to be [ ] and I am Extreamly Sorry that I ever Consented that anything in a Draft so severe and bitter and disrespectfull should go to [^371-note1] the Council - Another thing I have been often since very sor Sorry for, was, that I opposed the adjournmt of the Matter for About two months (If I do not misremember ye time) which was proposed by the Council to ye Church, which I opposed Strenuously But I acted my Judgment in the affair then tho’ I have often since thought, that It might have been Attended with good very well and have been and am very Sorry that I ever opposed It Indeed Sr. the Temper that appeared in the people in one of the days of the Council’s Sitting, (which I cant remember, but I know it was When the Council sent a Comtee to see how many there was against an immediate Separation) was indeed Shocking to me and did then and has often since Excited a horror in me, and I never was till then in any degree Comparitively so Sensible of the undue Engagedness of the people - And instead of It’s [-] being in any degree agreable to me fill’d me with great Concern sorrow and melancholly - But I indeed thot apprehended that a Separation was Absolutely necessary which determined me to vote for it.

With regard Sr. to the remonstrance and the Conduct of the Church when the last Council was here I have but little to say to Excuse myself; Indeed I had no thought of cannot remember that I had any thought or disposition to insert any thing in it to the disadvantage of any particular persons character before Capt. Wright and I had Consulted with ye Gentleman who was assisting in Composing of It; all that I had apprehended was necessary or Expedient to remonstrate to the Council was that the Separation of those who were desirous of you being Settled here as minister to them was unnecessary unjustifiable and would probably be attended with very ill Consequences - and that I had no apprehension in the time of Composing it that contained anything but was true and Could be made evident. But I freely Confess that I was Consenting to ye model of It, was active in Co Collecting and putting together the materials and was also Active in the dra principally Active in the Draught of It and in leading the Chh into the vote respecting it, for all which I am heartily and I trust Sincerely Sorry and truly wish that there had been Nothing in it but a plain Calm and Moderate argument respecting the Expediency of your resettling in this place As minister to those who were then desirous of It - I have no disposition at all to go into the Consid Examination or Consideration of ye particulars mentioned to ye disadvantage of particular persons Nor how much of that nature which was said or implied was true or very probable - But Inasmuch as It was, as I now apprehend, unnecessary. It was uncharitable and unchristian to have mentioned any of It, Much More so to Do It in so harsh Strong and Satirical[^371-note2] Terms as many were which were therein used - I have been Since very Sorry and am still Sorry that I opposed that Council’s having a Conference with the Church which they repeatedly desired Earnestly - and I think It discovered a great deal of Self Confidence and think that it was presumtuous for us to refuse hearing What that council Could say or propose to us, among whom there were several Justly in great reputation for grace and Wisdom, and acknowledge that I was very Active in opposing such a Conference As to What was Sinfull and Injurious in the remonstrances I and a Certain Gentleman who assisted me about it (I apprehend) ought to take ye fault and blame of principally to ourselves, and to say (If It may be said without vanity) as David Did in a another Case, We have Sinned and Done wickedly. But these Sheep What have they done - for it is true I don’t doubt, that many who voted for it Acted very implicitly and perhaps were blameable only for rashness and too great precipitance as to what was Injurious to you Sr. and others therein, (and what that what you have Contradicted was so I am Satisfied for I can believe what you say respecting it,) I am heartily Sorry was ever inserted in it, and do humbly and Earnestly ask your forgiveness and prayer to God that he would forgive me, and Deal with me according to my deserts therefor; as I also do in like manner for all that I have here before in this letter Confessed myself faulty in - I also Sr. desire your prayers that my Sorrow and repentance for these things may be Sincere and genuine and Such as God for Christ’s sake will Accept and that A Sense of my faults and sin herein in those instances may make me more humble and Self-diffident for ye future and much more Cautious for the future and that If there are other things wherein in the Series of that malancholly affair I have Acted Sinfully and ought particularly to humble myself for that God would would reveal even them unto me that I may make proper reflections upon myself therefor The foregoing reflections I make freely and Cherfully and am free you should Communicate them to whom you See meet for I care not how publick they are made am Not unwilling it should be known that I have made them.

Sr I particularly thank you that you was pleased to give yourself the trouble to write so long a letter to me when you was so ill able to do It - and desire that assure you Sr that I received and read it without any the least resentment or uneasiness with you for ye plainess and freedom you have been pleased to use in it, and am truly glad that you have dealt So freely with me therein and also give you thanks for ye kind wishes you express therein express concerning me

I am Rd Sr. with humble and Sincere Salutations to you and Madm Edwards and family yr. most Obl Humble servt. J H N.H Janry. 21st. 1755 Mr. Edwards

P.S I freely confess Sr. that in ye whole progress of the affair from the beginning to the End I was not properly affected Nor my Spirit duly impressed with the vast Importance &[^371-note3]

[^371-note1]: **marginal.** [3]

[^371-note2]: **marginal.** [4]

[^371-note3]: The remainder of the postscript is written perpendicularly in the left margin.

## B113. Letter from Eleazar Wheelock, October 29, 1755 B113.E.Wheelock-JE 10-29-55 edited

Eleazar WheelockB113. Eleazar Wheelock to JE, 10/29/55. Darmouth College Lib., Ms. #755579. Addressed on verso: "To The Reverend / Mr Jonathan Edwards / At Stockbridge." JE’s notation follows: "Mr. Wheelock Oct. 29. 55."

New Haven, Octr 29. 1755.

Revd & Hond. Sir.

I recd. a Lettr from You (I believe) more than 12 months ago, desiring me two take Indian Boys &c. When I was in Expectation of two from Mr. Brainerd, concerning Whom I have long been, & was then held in suspense & therefore cd not answer You, after Sometime they came & are Still with me who are as many as I dare undertake to support by Charity but No Opportunity presenting I did not Write 'till it was So late that I concluded it wod probably be of No Service.

Since that we have been pursuing a Design of a Charity School in favour of the Native of any or all the Tribes in N. America. Mr. Joshua More of Mansfield has given a lott of Land in the Center of My Parish for that purpose The Rev. Messrs Moseley of Windham & Pomroy of Hebron[^372-note1] with myself (who are undertakers) in our last Discourse upon it, were inclined to think, tho' not fully determind, it wod be best to Set it up this fall, Notwithstanding Subscription for a Fund for the Masters Support is not yet completed, and hope that the hearts of Good People will be Sufficiently opend to Supply it ‘till it be. Which there is a prospect may Soon be, unless discourag’d by our publick Charges. I Suppose our Meeting on the Affair will be Soon after my Return when we purpose to determind the matter after which I purpose to take the first opportunity to give you a more full Accot. of the Whole Affair, and ask your assistance & the benefit of Your great Influence at home and abroad. &c.

But the Special Reason of my catching this minute, amidst a Crowd of Business, to Write You is, that Yesterday Mr. Prudden of Milford[^372-note2] told me that you had wrote to Mr. Bellamy to take Six Boys on the Societys pay, and that he cod not take them. If we Shall Set up the School this fall it will suit us well to take them, provided they are not Vicious &c one of the Boys with me is under convictions &c. We have Yet determind who to appoint for Master [^372-note3] we have discoursd of the Rev. Mr Barker lately dismisd from his people at Killingly, also of Mr. Sherwood, & Sr. Brooks,[^372-note4] but which of them or whether either I can't tell - we want advice. please to Accept most Ssincere Regards to your Self & Spouse. And let my Hurry Excuse the Many Imperfections In What I have written. & Remember in your Devoutest thoughts

Your Very Hearty, tho' Unworthy Brother Eleazar Wheelock

The Rev. Mr. Edwards -

[^372-note1]: Samuel Moseley (1708-1791), pastor of Second Church in Windham, Conn., 1734-91; Benjamin Pomeroy (1704-84), pastor of Hebron, Conn., 1735-84, and trustee of Dartmouth College.

[^372-note2]: Job Prudden (1715-1774), pastor of Second or Separatist Church in Milford, Conn., 1747-74.

[^372-note3]: **marginal.** [2]

[^372-note4]: As it turned out, none of these became the master. Nehemiah Barker (1720-1772), pastor of Third Church in Killingly, Conn., 1746-55, then of church in Southold, Long Island, 1756-72; Samuel Sherwood (1730-1783), pastor of Weston, Conn., 1757-83; Thomas Brooks (c. 1719-1799), pastor of Brookfield, Conn., 1757-96.

## B114. Letter from Ebenezer Grant, March 30, 1756 B114.E.Grant-JE 3-30-56 edited

Ebenezer GrantB114. Ebenezer Grant to JE[?], 3/30/56. BRBL, Sermon on Gen. 3:17-19, n.d. [after 3/56), f. 935. No address.

Windsor March 30th 1756 -

Revd Sr

your's of ye 6th Instant, have Recd - wherein you are desirous of my Engaging Elijah Lomis to Come up and live with a year - have been with him upon ye business, proposed your motion, & Indeed shew'd him your Letter, who (I take it) Accepts your offer, and Intends to be with [you][^373-note1] at ye time, thô it wo'd [have] been more Acceptable to him to have began his years Service Sooner, that he might be dismissed ye next Spring Sooner. as I recommended him to you, hope when he's in your business, his Service will be Acceptable - Am, Sr, with a great Deal Respect, Your humble servt

Ebenr Grant
