## C120. Aaron Burr to Jasper Mauduit (Draft), March 9, 1753 C120.ABurr-JMauduit 3-9-53

Aaron BurrC120. Aaron Burr to Jaspar Mauduit,3/9/53. ANTS, Burr Letterbook.

To Mr Jasper Mauduit in Lime street London

Sec try to h. S:

Sr

A Letter from one Whose Name Perhaps you have never heard, would doubtless be unexpected: but I hope ye Design of my writing will be thought a Sufficient Excuse for my giving you this trouble.

I have had undoubted Information That Coll n E: Williams (who was lately at London) with his Kindsman at Stockbridge, who were have a Design y t to make a Representation to ye hon ble Society in Lond n against the Mr Edwards and to attempt his Removal from his Mission there. And y t they have endeavoured to engage Some Gent n in Several Parts of ye Countrey to concur with y m on in the Design

My Relation to Mr Edwards having lately Married into his Family; gives me Some Reluctance to write on this Occasion - But as I have been for many Years a Correspond ts for to ye Society in Scotland for propagating Christian Knowledge, And have had Some Special Opportunity [^516-note1] of being well Acquainted with ye Affair at Stockbridge, I hope my writing will not be thought altogeth r improper . -

Mr Edwards’s being appointed to y t Mission, gave gr t Satisfaction to ye more Sane[?] & Judicious Part of ye Countrey, both Ministers & People. - And seem to put new Life into the Design of propagating ye Gospel among the indians —— His Ch t as for Piety, Learning & gr t Faithfull s in his Work, is so well hi established, y t those y t are most ag st to his continuance at Stockbridge, will not I am persuaded pretend to Say any thing ag st it - They will, I Suppose, pretend y t there are some things in him y t unqualify him for y t Work. - But Such as are the best Judges y t Case & well Acquainted w t him, think he has Some peculiar Q o for y t Business, w c are rarely found —— I have had Opport y by being acquainted in his Family to observe his uncom n Talent for Instruction in a familiar Way by Question & Answ r - All y t know the Temper of ye Indians; know how much value, Gravity, Integrity & steadiness in men. - [-] for w c he is well known to be em t

And the y Indians are very much pleased w t & remarkably attached to him, Notwith d Some Attempts to allienate y r Affect ns from him —— And so are all ye english at Stockb d excepting one Family —— And Should the hon ble Society from envy & partial Repr tations be induced to remove Mr Edwards, it would be a fatal Blow not only to ye aff r at Stockbridge, but to ye whole Design of pro= =pagating ye Gosp l among Ind ns in those Parts There is one young Gent m now at Stock g [^516-note2] learning ye Mohawk Langu. - and Another going this spring from ye Correspond ts to ye Society in S-ld. on ye Same Design with a view to go into y r Country. w n they are qualified - But Should not Mr Ed-ds be continued they would both drop it. And two so like y s men, y t would be willing to undertake it, I am persuaded, would not be found in America . ——

I feel the gr ter Freedom in writing in this Man r not only from a Conv n y t tis with a view to preve hind r aug prevent the ye Obstruc n of y t noble Design the Society have at Heart; but have a Perswasion y t it will be agreable to what you [-] will hear from ye worthy Comiss rs in Boston, who as thus Gent m of the best Char s in y t Part of ye Country & will I trust be esteemed best Judges in this Affair. ——

I use ye Freedom to enclose you Some of ye printed Acc ts of ye infant College of New-Jersey - which we are carrying on thro a good Many Dificulties as we have No Assistance from ye [^516-note3] Gov t - the Ruling Part of o r Ass bly being Q rs [^516-note4] who are no Friends to Learning —— Should it ly in y r Pow r to befriend So impor t & usefull a Design it will be an accep ble [ ] of [ ] to ye [...] - & add but hopes y t God would [ ] and [ ] to y t Design of y r h ble Soc ty for poor of Sending ye Gosp l to ye poor benighted Pagans in these Parts that there be an eff l Door open for it Spreading through t distant Tribes. and am

w t much Respect -

Mar h 9. 1753.

## C121. Aaron Burr ot Thomas Foxcroft (Draft), March 19, 1753 C121.ABurr-TFoxcroft 3-19-53

Aaron BurrC121. Aaron Burr to Thomas Foxcroft,3/19/53. ANTS, Burr Letterbook.

To Rev d Mr Foxcroft ——— M ch 19. 53

Rev d & d r Sr

Your Fav r of Dec r 5. 53. with the enclosed Pamphlet was very acc ble especialy on Acc t of y e agreeable News y t are like to be Suited again in a Companion for Life. - I have longed to hear Something more, who the Person is y t has the Happiness of Suiting your [——] critical & refined Tast. Methinks She must have Some very extraordinar virtues, My Opinion of her runs high. - Before this, I trust you are happy in Enj tof y e Person you Admire & Love.

My Wife has been confined by Illness almost y e whole Winter. but now begins to rid Abroad & is hopefully recovering. - This Notwithstanding. I can Speak freely in Favour of y e married State, I find much more Comf t & Satisfact n in it than I ever expected. I now See the Wisdom of y t Institution & y e Weakness it of my Reasons for not entering into y t State before. -

Mr Hawley has been I have lately had a large Paquet from Stockbridge - with a full & particular Acc t of Mr y r Atta Dificulties & y e Design ag st Mr Edw ds —— I am now fully Satisfied they intend to do y r utmost to remove Mr Ed s - Coll: Dwight is open in it Coll E. W. & his Lady will or Seem readily[?] certain[?] & tell y t they can engage . - I have by Adv. of Coll n Pyncbon wrote [^517-note1] to Sec ry of Society - w c I Send open for y r Perusal & entirely Submit to y r Judg t whether to Send or Suppress it. —— I enclose 2 of Mr Ed. Serm s- It Sems long Since I heard from you . - My last I hope came Safe ——— This comes by a Young Gent m graduated at o r College 1752 —— He is a good Man of Good Sense, a good Schoolar & hopefully pious . -

My Wife Joins in most most res tfull Salu ts
